The database provides a systematic reference for metallic coherent heterophase interfaces and demonstrates the importance of separating strain and chemical energy contributions when interpreting alloy behavior.

items.title: Ferroelectric control of the $K$--$\Gamma$ valley landscape in R-stacked bilayer WSe$_2$
authors: Katsunori Wakabayashi, Souren Adhikary, Tomoaki Kameda, Kazuhito Tsukagoshi
items.summary: In bilayer WSe2 the valence-band maxima at K and {\Gamma} lie within a few thermal energies of one another, and gating redistributes holes between a light and a heavy valley of different mobilities on a landscape that stays fixed. We show that rhombohedral (R) stacking moves the landscape itself. The three-fold symmetry of R stacking forbids interlayer tunneling at K but not at {\Gamma}. The K coupling is therefore exactly zero, not merely small. A fit that leaves the coupling free returns an upper bound of 0.017 meV, three orders of magnitude under k_BT at room temperature, while the {\Gamma} coupling is 361.8 meV. The polarization creates a potential step between the layers and splits the K doublet. Each K state stays on a single layer, so the K edge shifts by half of that splitting, 41.7 meV, which any tunneling would reduce. {\Gamma} barely responds. Two consequences follow from symmetry alone, whatever the size of that shift. The two registries, carrying opposite out-of-plane ferroelectric polarizations, are exact mirror images along the displacement-field axis, and reversing the polarization reverses the displacement of the landscape. Their differential-mode transconductances are equal and opposite at zero field, where the response vanishes for an ideal nonpolar reference. The stored polarization is read out as a reversal of sign and not as a difference of current. Sweeping the field is a second route to the same parity. In the ideal symmetric limit the transconductance passes through zero at the field that cancels the polarization, 1.07 V/nm, at a single temperature. Both routes are limited by the symmetry of the device more than by the band structure. Stacking also renormalizes the landscape, so the polar one is not a translated copy of the nonpolar reference. Absolute offsets follow the exchange-correlation functional. The symmetry relations do not.

items.title: High Characteristic Voltage YBCO Josephson Junctions Written With a Focused Helium Ion Beam
authors: Rochelle Y. Qu, Aravind R. Sreeja, Adhilsha Parachikunnumal, Alexander Brooks, Nicole Y. Chin, Jay C. LeFebvre, Roger K. Lake, Shane A. Cybart
items.summary: We report in-plane Josephson junctions written directly into YBa$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{7-\delta}$ (YBCO) thin films with a focused helium ion beam (He FIB). The characteristic voltage $I_{\mathrm{C}}R$ of these junctions, where $I_{\mathrm{C}}$ is the Josephson critical current and $R$ is the junction resistance, sets the operating frequency and the sensitivity of the circuits built from them. A single line irradiation with a dose of \SI{500}{ions/nm} across a \SI{4}{\micro\metre} wide electrode produced a junction with $I_{\mathrm{C}}R$ of 929 \si{\micro\volt} at \SI{1.6}{K}, which is `higher than the 200 to 400 \si{\micro\volt} typical of junctions fabricated previously in our laboratory. Temperature dependent resistance, current-voltage characteristics, magnetic field modulation of the critical current, and Shapiro steps under 20.5~GHz microwave irradiation show Josephson behavior with an excess current below 5 percent of the critical current. The critical current falls steeply with temperature near the junction transition and saturates at low temperature. We attribute this behavior to a barrier at the metal insulator transition, where hopping conduction through localized states is active at finite temperature and freezes out on cooling. We describe the changes in surface preparation, sample selection, beam focusing, and sample storage that accompanied the improvement, although the present data do not separate their individual contributions. Larger characteristic voltages at these dimensions are an encouraging result for rapid single flux quantum and adiabatic quantum flux parametron logic and for superconducting quantum interference devices operating at elevated temperature.

items.title: State Diagram of Dual-Free-Layer Perpendicular Magnetic Tunnel Junctions for Artificial Spiking Neurons
authors: Arthur Courberand, Ajay Jha, Ricardo C. Sousa, Stephane Auffret, Joo-Von Kim, Ursula Ebels, Liliana D. Buda-Prejbeanu
items.summary: The performance of perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) depends critically on interfacial properties and layer thicknesses, small variations of which can substantially modify their magnetic and transport characteristics. This work investigates, experimentally and numerically, a perpendicular MTJ with two free layers, a configuration that preserves the precessional dynamics of the device while simplifying its fabrication. Quasi-static state diagrams measured under magnetic fields and DC or pulsed bias reveal static parallel, antiparallel, and bistable regimes, as well as a dynamical windmill regime in which the reversal of one layer triggers that of the other, giving rise to spiking neuron-like signals. Macrospin simulations reproduce these diagrams, and a stability analysis of the Landau-Lifchitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation yields an analytical description of the critical lines, including the windmill threshold voltage. The comparison also reveals a quadratic term in the voltage dependence of the spin-transfer torque that Joule heating cannot explain. The analytical model shows that the threshold voltage can be lowered either by approaching the spin-reorientation transition, at the cost of thermal stability, or by enhancing the quadratic contribution to the spin-transfer torque. These results establish guidelines for optimizing multilayer MTJ stacks for artificial spiking neurons and a broader range of neuromorphic and spintronic applications.

items.title: Hidden Heat-Current Transport Channels Behind Observable Temperature Dynamics
items.summary: Diffusive decay and wave-like oscillations in temperature dynamics are commonly used to characterize heat conduction, yet these signatures do not uniquely identify the underlying heat-current transport mechanisms. Here we reveal a spectrum of constitutive heat-current channels whose microscopic organization can change without a corresponding qualitative change in observable temperature dynamics. We develop a two-level spectral theory that first resolves the finite-wave-vector constitutive response into relaxational and streaming channels characterized by their poles and heat-current residues, and then connects their combined response to equilibrium temperature fluctuations through energy conservation. First-principles calculations for NaF at 17~K reveal that the same streaming-induced mode coupling responsible for the perturbative nonlocal correction in the Guyer--Krumhansl (G--K) reduction drives a nonperturbative transformation of the isolated momentum-organized relaxational channel into a dominant complex-conjugate streaming pair. This transformation breaks down the single-relaxational-channel constitutive structure of G--K, while oscillatory temperature dynamics persist below the short-period boundary of its predicted oscillatory window. At shorter periods, heat-current weight redistributes among multiple collision-coupled streaming channels before approaching independently damped phonon streaming. Increasing temperature provides a distinct route beyond hydrodynamics by eliminating the isolated momentum-organized sector, even as oscillatory temperature dynamics persist. Thus, the breakdown of a hydrodynamic constitutive description can reflect a reorganization of heat-current transport rather than the disappearance of oscillatory temperature dynamics, and agreement with temperature measurements alone does not validate the constitutive structure of a reduced theory.

items.title: Charge-Transfer Energy Governed by $f$-$d$ Coulomb Interaction in Rare-Earth Systems
authors: Norimasa Sasabe, Shinji Watanabe, Akira Yasui, Naomi Kawamura, Kojiro Mimura, Takayuki Uozumi, Masaichiro Mizumaki, Hitoshi Sato
items.summary: The $f$-$d$ Coulomb interaction ($U_{\rm fd}$) plays a central role in low-energy theories describing valence fluctuations and quantum valence criticality in rare-earth systems. In contrast, core-level spectroscopies have conventionally been analyzed using the phenomenological charge-transfer energy ($\Delta$), and the relationship between these two descriptions has remained unclear. Here, we develop a spectroscopic framework demonstrating that the charge-transfer energy contains an $f$-$d$ Coulomb contribution $U_{\rm fd}n_d$ arising from the $d$-electron occupation ($n_d$), leading to the charge-transfer energy $\Delta'$. We apply this framework to the prototypical valence-transition compound YbInCu$_4$ and demonstrate, from combined analyses of core-level photoemission and $L$-edge x-ray absorption spectroscopy, that the observed spectroscopic evolution across the first-order valence transition is consistently interpreted in terms of the variation of $\Delta'$.

items.title: Compact Projected Pfaffian States for Rydberg-Blockaded Quantum Spin Systems
items.summary: We numerically demonstrate that a compact projected Pfaffian ansatz effectively describes the ground state of the nonintegrable PXP model. The variational wave function is obtained by applying separate Gutzwiller and Rydberg-blockade projectors to a general fermionic paired state, and each blockade-allowed configuration has an amplitude given by the Pfaffian of a configuration-selected pairing matrix. The exact blockade-projected product state of a known frustration-free deformation of the PXP model lies within the variational manifold and provides a physically motivated initial state for the variational Monte Carlo optimization toward the ground state of the pure PXP model. For a one-dimensional system of $N$ sites, optimizing all symmetry-allowed pairings in an $O(N)$-parameter wave function yields a near-exact ground state with a normalized energy variance (V-score) of order $10^{-9}$ despite the exponentially large blockade-constrained Hilbert space. On the square lattice, an $O(N)$-parameter wave function with the same amplitude structure yields relative energy errors below $0.2\%$ for clusters accessible to exact diagonalization and produces magnetizations consistent with available benchmarks. These results show that the same projected Pfaffian construction can be applied to blockade-constrained systems in both one and two dimensions.

items.title: IANN: A Unified Framework for Equivariant InterAtomic Neural Networks with User-Friendly Implementation
authors: Changzhi Ai, Xueping Qin, Dimosthenis Sokaras, Frank Abild-Pedersen, Johannes Voss
items.summary: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now approach density functional theory (DFT) accuracy at a fraction of its cost, but the practical benefit is limited by software fragmentation: each state-of-the-art architecture is released as a separate codebase, with its own data format, configuration system, training loop and molecular-dynamics interface. Comparing two architectures on the same dataset, or moving a trained model into a production simulation, therefore requires substantial re-engineering. We introduce IANN (InterAtomic Neural Network), an open-source PyTorch framework that reimplements equivariant graph neural networks - PaiNN, NequIP, MACE, Allegro, EquiformerV2, EquiformerV3 and UMA - behind a unified data object, a unified trainer and a single deployment route, so that the architecture is a one-word change in a configuration dictionary. Forces, stresses and virials are obtained for every architecture from one analytic differentiation of the energy with respect to the edge vectors of the atomic graph, exact under periodic boundary conditions. Distributed training is configured automatically from the SLURM, PBS or MPI environment, so the same script runs unchanged from a workstation to a multi-node GPU allocation. Self-describing checkpoints serve directly as ASE calculators, as ensembles reporting uncertainties, or as TorchScript models run inside LAMMPS through bundled C++ pair styles with single- and multi-GPU inference. Trained on a common dataset of millions of structures, the architectures can be compared under identical conditions. We further release PaiNN foundation models trained on 41.9 million curated DFT structures from MPtrj, Alexandria, OMat24, MatPES, OC20, OC22, OC25, MPr2SCAN and MatPESr2SCAN, spanning the PBE, RPBE and r2SCAN functionals. Additionally, IANN provides an agent interface to facilitate integration with autonomous agents.

items.title: Mixed-Sign Kitaev Exchange in Jahn-Teller-Distorted CrI$_2$
authors: Shiyan Gao, Zekuo Yang, Chuanhang Chen, Zefeng Chen, Lianchuang Li, Hongjun Xiang, Changsong Xu
items.summary: Kitaev couplings with ferromagnetic (FM) or antiferromagnetic (AFM) character shape magnetic frustration and phases differently in real materials, yet their coexistence within a single material remains unexplored. Here, we propose Jahn-Teller distortion as a route to realizing such coexistence on inequivalent bonds. First-principles calculations identify monolayer CrI$_2$ as such a system, with AFM and FM Kitaev couplings on the short and long bonds, respectively. These opposite signs are robust against variations in Hubbard $U$, functionals, and strain. A minimal tight-binding model links this sign contrast to Jahn-Teller-split $t_{2g}$ orbitals and their hopping to $e_g$ orbitals. We further adopt the cluster expansion method and develop a realistic machine-learned spin Hamiltonian, which reproduces the experimentally observed proper-screw geometry and propagation direction and reveals highly nonuniform spin rotation, with turning angles ranging from $48.0^\circ$ to $93.9^\circ$. Both proper-screw anisotropy and strong anharmonic spin rotation arise from the mixed-sign Kitaev interaction. These findings not only establish Jahn-Teller distortion as a microscopic route to mixed-sign Kitaev exchange, but also open a new avenue for exploring novel magnetic phases.

items.title: Exact environment checkpointing for memory-limited DMRG and TDVP
items.summary: Finite matrix-product-state sweep algorithms, such as the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP), store one environment tensor per site. At the bond dimensions needed for frustrated and two-dimensional systems this stack, rather than the state itself, exhausts the memory of the device. We adapt checkpointing to these sweeps: every $k$-th environment is kept, with $k\approx\sqrt{N}$ for $N$ sites, and the blocks in between are rebuilt when the sweep returns to them. The rebuild repeats the original contractions, so energies and states are reproduced bit for bit when the contractions are deterministic. Environment memory falls by 4.6-10x on cylinders of 96-384 sites. Bond-dimension searches with an implementation that rebuilds checkpoints at each half-sweep give gains of 1.77 for one level and 2.07 for two levels with eight contraction chunks on a single 141 GB GPU, using a 144-site triangular $J_1$-$J_2$ cylinder and stored baselines with matching chunking. Separate timings with checkpoints retained across half-sweeps give a one-level overhead of 6-15%, depending on the local eigensolver. At $D=1536$ the two-level schedule with eight chunks takes 1.42 times the sweep time of the equally chunked stored baseline, or 1.79 times that of the unchunked stored baseline. Simple models of the memory and the run time reproduce the measurements to within a few per cent. Unlike offloading, the method needs no host memory or disk, and the two can be combined. Implementations are provided for ITensorMPS.jl, TeNPy, MPSKit.jl and quimb.

items.title: Spectroscopic evidence for unconventional surface magnetism in the Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$
authors: Ke-Jun Xu, Erin E. Fleck Jonathan A. Sobota, Nhat Huy M. Tran, Shuyi Li, Youzhe Chen, Soonsang Huh, Takeshi Kondo, Makoto Hashimoto, Dong-Hui Lu, Zhi-Xun Shen, Dung-Hai Lee, Chunjing Jia, Robert J. Birgeneau
items.summary: Kondo insulators have a non-magnetic bulk due to many-body screening of local moment by conduction electrons. However, the surface of these systems has reduced density of itinerant electrons and may experience a Kondo breakdown, leading to recovery of non-zero local moments and possible magnetic order. Here we use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to investigate the (010) surface of a $d$-$p$ electron Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$, which is predicted to host a bulk $d$-wave altermagnetic state in the absence of Kondo screening. We find anisotropic splitting on the surface states with a maximum in the $k_z$ direction and a minimum in the $k_x$ direction. The splitting is apparently suppressed with increasing temperature or with Te doping, suggesting that the splitting arises from a magnetic order rather than Rashba effects. Considering the proximity of the bulk to a $d$-wave altermagnetic state and considering the symmetry of the crystal on the surface, we postulate that our observations may be consistent with an emergent surface altermagnetic order. Such an unconventional 2-dimensional magnetic order naturally hosted on an insulating, non-magnet bulk substrate may offer a promising platform for versatile applications.

items.title: Field-Driven Active Matter Physics and Material Applications
authors: Jing Wang, Shengkai Li, Trung V. Phan, Gao Wang, Huaicheng Chen, Xiaorui Chen, Robert H. Austin, Liyu Liu
items.summary: Active matter consists of energy-consuming units that generate motion, making it a powerful platform for exploring nonequilibrium physics and engineering adaptive materials. Robotic active matter brings this physics into programmable, macroscopic agents with controllable actuation, sensing, and response, but its scalability is limited by onboard power, communication, and control complexity. Field-driven active matter addresses these limitations by shifting part of the control burden from individual agents to external or environmental fields, such as magnetic, electric, acoustic, optical, and fluidic fields, which can power, guide, and couple many agents simultaneously. Beyond applications in targeted navigation, adaptive collaboration, and flexible transport, field-driven robotic active matter offers a controllable testbed for nonequilibrium phenomena that are difficult to isolate in molecular or colloidal active matter, including tunable interactions, programmable phase transitions, solid-fluid switching, hyperuniform order, and reconfigurable collective motion. Here, we present field-driven active matter as a bridge between active matter physics and functional material engineering, organized through a unified field-to-information-to-physics-to-function framework that links field-mediated interactions, information processing, and memory to collective transport, reconfiguration, and mechanical performance. By distributing control between agents and fields, field-driven active matter offers a pathway toward intelligent materials capable of sensing, adaptation, computation, reconfiguration, and performing complex tasks, while expanding both the scientific scope of nonequilibrium physics and the practical capabilities of engineered matter.

items.title: Electrical transport of surface-bound electrons on annealed solid neon
authors: Ka Wing Yip, Tomoyuki Tani, Jui-Yin Lin, Mikhail Belianchikov, Denis Konstantinov
items.summary: We study the dc transport of electrons bound to the surface of solid neon using the conventional Sommer-Tanner method. First, we find that the capacitive cross-talk for the thickness of solid samples on the order of a millimeter varies substantially with the temperature and is strongly affected by the sample annealing. Second, we find that, even for the annealed samples, the observed response of electrons differs significantly from that of the surface-bound electrons on liquid helium and cannot be satisfactorily described by conventional models. Despite this, we managed to extract the resistance of the electron system from its in-phase response and investigate the temperature dependence in a wide range between 1.4 and 20 K. In a high-temperature range between 16 and 20 K, the resistance behavior is found to agree very well with the vapor-atom scattering mechanism, while at lower temperatures it is consistent with temperature-dependent scattering by surface roughness. Our analysis indicates a high electron mobility of electrons on solid neon but two orders of magnitude lower density than expected. These results suggest surface electrons as a suitable probe for studying the morphology of the neon surface but call for a better understanding of the experimental method applicable to such systems.

items.title: Velocity weakening and stick-slip in mean-field depinning with stress overshoots
items.summary: We study a fully connected depinning model with transient stress overshoots of strength $M$, driven through a spring of stiffness $k_0$. Combining exact stationary relations, linear stability analysis, direct simulations, and population dynamics, we connect the force--velocity characteristic to stick-slip motion and quasistatic avalanche statistics. For $M>1$, two distinct stiffness scales organize the response. At $k_0=k_{\rm w}\equiv M-1$, the stationary characteristic first develops a velocity-weakening branch, whereas $k_0=k_{\rm q}\equiv(M-1)^2/(4M)$ marks the onset of finite-amplitude stick-slip in the quasistatic limit. Their separation produces an intermediate regime in which the quasistatic force converges to a stationary value, whereas finite-velocity driving produces stick-slip below a critical velocity. Quasistatic avalanches in this regime undergo transient amplification and display an excess of large, asymmetric events---"ghost kings"---that remain finite. By contrast, at and below $k_{\rm q}$ the same amplification produces system-spanning "genuine kings" and a finite quasistatic force cycle. These results show how elastic loading dynamically selects among the branches of a reentrant force--velocity relation and clarify the connection between velocity weakening, stick-slip, and runaway avalanches.

items.title: Theory of anisotropic magnetotransport beyond the constant relaxation-time approximation in multi-Weyl semimetals
authors: Azaz Ahmad, Shantanu Mukherjee, Mohd Hashim Raza, Gautham Varma K., Takami Tohyama
items.summary: Multi-Weyl semimetals, characterized by Weyl nodes carrying higher monopole charges, provide a platform for exploring topological magnetotransport beyond the conventional Weyl paradigm. Here, we develop a generalized semiclassical Boltzmann framework for multi-Weyl semimetals with arbitrary monopole charge $N$, incorporating the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) into the quasiparticle dispersion and Berry-curvature-modified dynamics, together with a momentum-dependent collision integral accounting for intra- and intervalley scattering. We investigate the longitudinal magnetoconductivity (LMC) and planar Hall conductivity (PHC) for $N=1$, $2$, and $3$, considering both nonmagnetic and magnetic impurity scattering. In the absence of OMM, the LMC remains positive and quadratic in the magnetic field throughout the investigated scattering regime, consistent with conventional chiral-anomaly-assisted transport. Including OMM, however, leads to a sign reversal of the LMC under sufficiently strong intervalley scattering for the $\sigma_0$ and $\sigma_z$ impurity channels. Remarkably, the critical intervalley scattering strength decreases systematically with increasing monopole charge, indicating an enhanced tendency toward negative LMC in higher-charge Weyl systems. Furthermore, we find that the PHC also undergoes a sign reversal for $N=2$ and $N=3$ in the same impurity channels, while remaining positive for $N=1$ within the investigated parameter range. The angular dependences retain their characteristic $\sin^2\gamma$-like and $\sin2\gamma$ profiles for LMC and PHC, respectively, even across the sign reversal. Our results demonstrate that the interplay of Berry curvature, OMM, monopole charge, and impurity scattering can produce qualitatively distinct weak-field magnetotransport responses beyond the conventional chiral-anomaly picture.

items.title: Free energy profile computations for force-induced melting of a short B-DNA using Jarzynski equality
authors: S. Siva Nasarayya Chari, Prabal K. Maiti
items.summary: We initially equilibrate a system of solvated 12-base pair canonical B-DNA of a specified sequence in a state of no external force acting on it (state $A: f=0$). A switching experiment is then performed by pulling one end of the DNA while restraining its other end. The pulling force is taken up to a maximum of 400 pN (state $B$), at a specified constant rate. The non-equilibrium work done W associated with this finite-time process is determined by integrating the extension of the DNA molecule with respect to the applied force. The distribution of the work values $P(W)$ is obtained by repeating the pulling process several times, wherein each time, the process is started with macroscopic state $A$. The free energy profile $\Phi(f)$ is obtained by a suitably devised method from the Jarzynski equality. The conformational space of the DNA is also sampled in an equilibrium method of umbrella sampling by considering the end-to-end length $\xi$ as the reaction coordinate. The associated potential of mean force (PMF) $\Phi(\xi)$ is then computed by invoking the weighted histogram analysis method (WHAM). From the results, we observe that the equilibrium free energy difference between two states, $A$ and $B$, $\Delta F_{AB} ~(=F_B -F_A)$ obtained through both methods, is in close agreement with each other, despite the differences along the profiles $\Phi(f)$ and $\Phi(\xi)$, attributed to their distinct pathways of unzipping.

items.title: Automating literature screening and knowledge synthesis with large language models
authors: Zhanzhao Li, Qiyao He, Weiqiang Chen, Kengran Yang, Kai Gong
items.summary: Scientific literature is expanding rapidly, yet much of its knowledge remains difficult to organize and reuse due to the substantial workload needed to navigate large, heterogeneous literature corpora. Here, we develop a generalizable large language model (LLM)-powered framework that automates literature screening, structured information extraction, and knowledge synthesis within a unified workflow. We benchmarked 11 state-of-the-art proprietary and open-weight LLMs across three materials science screening tasks differing in scope, corpus size, and class imbalance. Seven LLMs achieved balanced accuracies above 0.90 across all tasks, with the best-performing LLM reaching 0.96--0.98, demonstrating the potential of LLMs to accurately screen large, highly imbalanced scientific corpora. The framework also substantially reduces manual effort, screening 10,000 records within four minutes compared with approximately 83 person-hours for manual screening. Beyond literature screening, the framework extracts structured information from full-text articles, enabling content-level quantification of research landscapes that extends traditional bibliometric analysis based on publication metadata. This capability reveals methodological trends and underexplored directions, as shown for machine learning in concrete materials science. We further demonstrate its utility for information and data discovery by identifying publications containing silicate glass density data that are difficult to retrieve using conventional search strategies, which can support downstream hypothesis development, research design, and data-driven scientific discovery. Overall, these results demonstrate the broad applicability of LLM-powered literature analysis across scientific domains and its potential to transform large, unstructured literature corpora into structured, analyzable knowledge at scale.

items.title: Exact mean first-passage time and a Poisson-smoothing crossover in renewal shot noise
items.summary: Threshold crossings in exponentially relaxing shot noise depend on the interplay between incoming impulses and the residual signal left by earlier arrivals. For renewal input, existing high-threshold product approximations of the mean first-passage time (MFPT) leave open when evaluation at a single index preserves the mean with vanishing relative error. Here we derive an exact finite-threshold MFPT series for exponentially marked renewal shot noise and recast it as an average over an auxiliary Poisson index. When the waiting-time density exhibits short-time power-law behavior, $w(t)\sim ct^{\kappa-1}$, the dominant series contributions shift from the Poisson center by an amount of order $x^{1-\kappa}$, whereas the averaging kernel has a fluctuation width of order $\sqrt{x}$, with $x=\lambda b$. The competition between these scales yields a crossover at $\kappa=1/2$, where the deterministic-index product is asymptotically exact in ratio above this boundary, requires a finite multiplicative correction at criticality, and exhibits a growing logarithmic discrepancy below it. A moving-saddle approximation also yields an asymptotically exact MFPT ratio under general strictly positive, finite-mean waiting times. Numerical comparisons across Gamma, Weibull, and generalized-Gamma renewal laws illustrate the approximation regimes and their finite-threshold accuracy. Together, these results provide an exact finite-threshold benchmark for the mean first-passage time and reveal how short-gap renewal statistics determine the asymptotic accuracy of high-threshold approximations.

items.title: Dissipative many-body theory of electron-phonon-photon systems
authors: Zhenlin Zhang, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci
items.summary: Optical cavities offer opportunities to control quantum materials, but radiative leakage and vibrational relaxation call for microscopic theories that treat interactions and dissipation on equal footing. We develop a Keldysh-Lindblad nonequilibrium Green's function framework for interacting electrons coupled to quantized photon and phonon fields. The formulation accommodates boson-number-nonconserving Hamiltonians and dissipative channels that combine electronic transitions with bosonic processes. We derive the mixed electron-boson diagrammatic expansion and the corresponding Kadanoff-Baym equations, retaining environmental noise, initial correlations, and interaction-induced memory. The equal-time equations govern the electronic density matrix and the bosonic covariance. As an illustration, we construct jump operators that preserve a semiconductor with filled valence bands and an empty photon field. Within a mean-field treatment, this state remains stationary although its two-time propagators exhibit dissipative broadening. The framework opens new avenues for studying correlated dynamics in lossy cavities and vibrational environments.

items.title: Real-time dynamics with bead-Fourier path integrals. III. Atomistic condensed-phase simulations
items.summary: Accurately accounting for nuclear quantum effects (NQEs), including zero-point energy and nuclear tunneling, is essential for a reliable prediction of the structural, thermodynamic, and dynamical properties of chemical systems, particularly those involving light atoms. However, incorporating NQEs could render simulations of large-scale chemical systems computationally prohibitive, particularly when combined with expensive electronic-structure calculations. One potential avenue for reducing cost is to use bead-Fourier path integrals (BF-PIs). In Paper I, we introduced the BF centroid molecular dynamics (BF-CMD) method, in which BF-PIs were used to compute an effective potential for CMD, and in Paper II, we introduced BF ring polymer MD (BF-RPMD), taking the BF-PI and using it for approximate real-time dynamics. Both papers featured a series of model systems and were able to reduce the number of beads needed to converge dynamical properties by a factor of 2 to 4, depending on the system. In this work, we report the first implementation and application of the BF-PI framework to atomistic simulations using liquid bulk water and hexagonal ice as test cases. As in our previous papers, we find that adding just a single Fourier component to the path yields a 4- and 8-fold reduction in the number of beads while achieving results that agree with reference PI simulations for liquid water and ice, respectively. We also demonstrate that we can reduce simulation costs by up to 5.5x compared to standard PIs by reducing the number of force calculations and normal-mode transformations.

items.title: A Beginner's Guide to Physical Networks
items.summary: Network theory studies entities (nodes) and the relationships between them (edges). While these entities and their relationships may be abstract in general, this tutorial focuses on the special case of physical networks: spatially embedded networks that carry physical quantities such as electric charge, fluid volume, or momentum. The underlying structure is described mathematically by a graph (Section I), with the incidence matrix playing a central role in the analysis. Viewing a graph as a special case of a cell complex reveals the topological structure of the incidence matrix and its relation to familiar operators from calculus (Section II). Because these networks are physical, flows are conserved at each node and often derive from the gradient of a potential. Models that satisfy these principles behave analogously to circuits; accordingly, we first review circuit theory (Section III), then examine related fluid flow (Section IV) and mechanical (Section V) networks. Briefly, the topics of random walkers (Section VI) and nonlinear networks (Section VII) will be discussed, followed by concluding remarks (Section VIII). Analytical examples and Python implementations, in lieu of pseudocode, are included throughout. Exercises are included as footnotes. This tutorial is based on a short course taught at the Boulder School for Condensed Matter in 2019 and a course taught at the University of Pennsylvania in Spring 2024. It should be a useful resource for students, teachers, and researchers applying graph theory to physical networks. Knowledge of linear algebra is assumed, but no prior knowledge of graph theory or physics is necessary.

items.title: Rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising models from a tetrality web
authors: Ant\'onio Antunes, Jin Chen, Junchen Rong
items.summary: We construct rational conformal interfaces between the Ising and tricritical Ising (TIM) models by using different chiral symmetries to prepare their folded boundary states. We use a moving up procedure which extends the product theory to an auxiliary coset with an $S_3$ automorphism group, where permutations give twisted Cardy states. We complement this with a moving down approach which reduces to the $S_3$ invariant algebra. Overall, these procedures uncover a tetrality web relating four different theories. Pulling back ordinary Cardy states of the smallest theory in the web to the physical tensor product system gives eighteen factorized interfaces and six transmitting interfaces. The latter agree with four transposition and two 3-cycle twisted boundaries in the largest theory. They include Gaiotto's RG wall and the interface obtained by fusing an Ising duality line into it. The six interfaces carry the regular action of the TIM fusion ring and have the same energy transmission coefficient, $35/48$. Their boundary entropies, bulk correlations and operator spectra distinguish them. We calculate these observables and the complete annulus amplitudes between the twenty four boundaries.

items.title: Non-Topological Chiral Anomaly: The Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect
authors: R\'emy Larue, Amaury Marchon, J\'er\'emie Quevillon, Diego Saviot
items.summary: We derive the chiral anomaly in a thermal medium and show that, in addition to the well-established topological piece, the anomaly acquires a previously overlooked non-topological contribution, relevant for non-gauged axial symmetries. Remarkably, this modification of the continuity equation is independent of the electromagnetic fields, thereby giving rise to novel transport effects in relativistic hydrodynamics. We further propose an experimentally accessible new effect in Weyl semimetals which we call the Chiral Magnetoelectric Effect: an electric field proportional to the magnetic field is generated by the non-topological anomaly, even in the absence of an externally applied electric field. Beyond this concrete prediction, our results establish a broader hydrodynamic framework for non-topological chiral anomalies, opening the door to a range of previously unexplored anomaly-induced transport phenomena across condensed-matter and high-energy systems.

items.title: Gate tunable spin splitting for Andreev spin qubits in Ge quantum well heterostructures
authors: Avani Vivrekar, Benjamin D. Woods, Mark Friesen
items.summary: Ge-based super-semi heterostructures are a promising platform for implementing Andreev spin qubits (ASQs). For example, they can be isotopically purified to eliminate nuclear spins that cause decoherence. However, spin-orbit coupling (SOC), which is a key ingredient for ASQs, is cubic in momentum for hole-based materials like Ge, in contrast with more-conventional ASQ materials (e.g., InAs wires), for which the SOC is linear in momentum. In this work, we study the interplay between geometrical properties like the channel width, and gate-tunable properties like the chemical potential, on ASQ operations. Intriguingly, we find that the spin splitting in a planar Ge Josephson junction does not depend on the junction width, in contrast with InAs nanowires. We explore the possibility of exploiting this property to suppress the harmful effects of charge traps. However, this prospect is spoiled by the fact that charge traps also affect the chemical potential, in addition to the channel width. Our results provide insights into the fundamental mechanisms governing spin splitting in ASQs and offer guidance for optimizing ASQs in other materials with cubic SOC.

items.title: Hidden Momenta due to Magneto-Electric Coupling in Non-Reciprocal Media
authors: William S. McGregor, Niclas Westerberg, Robert Bennett
items.summary: From a canonical quantisation approach of macroscopic quantum electrodynamics, we derive the interaction Hamiltonian due to a dipole emitter interacting with a time-symmetry-broken topological insulator (TSB-TI), described by an axionic coupling Lagrangian. This provides an additional interaction term dependent on the magneto-electric coupling strength inherent to the TSB-TI which will modify measurements on related observables. The spontaneous decay rate is calculated in the Born-Markov approximation for a general electromagnetic Green's tensor, and then specifically for the case of a planar parallel-plate cavity.

items.title: Tunable Multi-Frequency-Band Generator and Detector of AC Signals Based on a Spin Hall Device with Two Antiferromagnetic Layers
authors: Oleh Shtanko, Volodymyr Prokopenko, Oleksandr Prokopenko
items.summary: Antiferromagnetic (AFM) spin Hall oscillators offer an electrical route to compact terahertz sources, while AFM spin Hall diodes can be used as a promising detectors of terahertz signals, however, their attainable frequency and the redout efficiency are constrained by the dynamics of a single AFM layer. We theoretically and numerically investigate a spin Hall multilayer junction Pt/AFM/Pt/AFM/Pt comprising two canted AFM layers, driven by independent drive DC currents flowing in the outer platinum (Pt) layers. Using a model based on the coupled Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert-Slonczewski equations for four AFM sublattices and a phase-dependent two-interface spin Hall magnetoresistance model, we show that the device manifests itself as a DC current-driven oscillating spin Hall magnetoresistance. When an additional DC (AC) signal current is applied to the junction, the device generates an output AC (DC) voltage. Our model predicts current-driven, locked, co- and counter-rotational states of the net magnetization at Neel-vector frequencies in the top and bottom AFM layers, respectively. These states result in a multi-frequency response of the spin Hall magnetoresistance at the sum and difference frequencies. The counter-rotation regime additionally activates the phase-sensitive mixing contribution, producing a fourth harmonic. In contrast, the co-rotation regime provides a difference-frequency channel on the order of 100 GHz, although mutual locking prevents this output from being tuned continuously toward zero. Our estimations show that the device matched to an external load can generate output AC power of 1.2 nW at the second harmonic and 0.8 pW at the fourth harmonic, and can produce a DC voltage of about 1 mV for a 6 mA input signal current.

items.title: Stochastic gauge fixing from the holographic renormalization group
items.summary: We extend the dictionary between stochastic quantization and holographic Wilsonian renormalization to Yang-Mills theory in four-dimensional anti-de Sitter space at tree level. The radial component of the bulk gauge field is Zwanziger's gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization, whose random walk of gauge modes is the longitudinal bulk propagator. We obtain the triple- and quadruple-trace couplings of gluons at finite cutoff in closed form. On transverse data, their dependence on the bulk gauge resides in a single zero mode, which drops out of the flat-space limit.

items.title: The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere from multi-target density matrix renormalization group
items.summary: The fuzzy-sphere regularization provides a powerful framework for studying three-dimensional (3D) conformal field theories (CFTs) through radial quantization, but conformal defects have so far been studied with it only by exact diagonalization (ED) of small systems. In this work we realize the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ twist line defect of the 3D Ising CFT on the fuzzy sphere by imposing antiperiodic boundary conditions on the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-odd fermion flavor, and solve it with a multi-target density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) algorithm that optimizes several low-lying states of each symmetry sector in a common matrix-product basis. This gives the defect spectrum at system sizes well beyond the reach of ED (up to $2s+1=25$, or $49$ spinless orbitals). The spectrum obeys the spin-parity selection rule of the twist line and organizes into conformal multiplets along the line. Using the displacement operator as an intrinsic ruler, its protected descendant as a test, and the bulk stress tensor as an independent cross-check, we identify the leading finite-size corrections and obtain controlled continuum extrapolations, which sharpen the dimensions of several known defect primaries and resolve four higher-lying ones. This study establishes the fuzzy sphere combined with multi-target DMRG as a framework for precision studies of conformal defects.

items.title: Finding Low-Energy States of the Bernasconi Model via Simulated Transverse-Field Quantum Dynamics
items.summary: The Low-Autocorrelation Binary Sequence (LABS) problem, the ground-state problem of the Bernasconi model, has a rugged landscape with deep, isolated local minima. We study real-time transverse-field dynamics initialized in these minima as a means of reaching lower-energy configurations. Using GPU statevector simulation for N = 20-30 spins, we compare the escape probability per verified quantum sample with the success rate per energy evaluation of steepest-descent kicks, random restarts and tabu search. Using the same field and sampling window across all system sizes, we find that, relative to the best classical baseline, the sampler achieves a factor of 11.9-35.2 for the deepest traps and 13.4-27.2 for the next energy tier. These ratios describe a constant-factor improvement in sample efficiency over the sizes studied. At the adopted field, broad Hamming-space spreading coexists with a strong preference for low-energy states. This regime follows a sharp increase in displacement as the field is raised. To connect this behaviour to the landscape, a short-time expansion relates the onset of escape to target distance and intermediate energies. Bounds on isotropic spin flips and on the free transverse mixer quantify the role of the Bernasconi potential in the observed transfer. At N = 28, the ground-state probability at t = 30 exceeds a canonical cost prediction fitted to the same mean energy by a factor of about 1.9. The cost of generating each quantum sample is assessed separately through a hardware estimate, which places a direct circuit implementation two to three orders of magnitude beyond present processor capabilities.

items.title: Hydration-induced local diffusivity heterogeneity modulates aqueous $H_2+OH$ reaction kinetics
authors: Ming-Gen Li, Shi-Yuan Zhang, Alessio Zaccone
items.summary: At room temperature, a Kramers reaction rate calculated with homogeneous solvent friction exceeds the measured rate of the aqueous reaction $H_2 + OH -> H + H_2O$ by about an order of magnitude. We show that spatially correlated hydration-induced diffusivity fluctuations increase effective friction and suppress the predicted escape rate. Estimates based on hydration-shell properties bring the theoretical rate closer to experiment. The suppression weakens with increasing temperature, linking local solvent heterogeneity to activated aqueous reaction kinetics.

items.title: Dressed higher-form symmetries in mixed state quantum matter
authors: Tibor Rakovszky, Sarang Gopalakrishnan, Curt von Keyserlingk
items.summary: We describe how to construct emergent strong higher-form symmetries in mixed quantum states that act unitarily on Hilbert space. Our construction uses (quasi-)local recovery channels from quantum error correction to some nearby simple (stabilizer) model. We prove that when the recovery is done in an appropriate (deterministic) manner, the resulting operators continue to be unitary. When applied to operators acting on topologically non-trivial sub-manifolds (loops, surfaces), the resulting unitaries inherit the logical algebra of the fixed point model. More generally, the unitarity of the emergent symmetries allows one to define emergent excitations whose statistics follow those of the fixed point limit.

items.title: The Goldstone--Wilczek Charge on the Rim
items.summary: A solenoid flux $\Phi=2\pi\alpha$ threaded through the center of the Kaplan--Sen lattice disk binds a ground-state charge $Q_{\rm core}=\alpha-\mathrm{round}(\alpha)$, and the edge carries exactly the opposite charge. The edge charge is the Goldstone--Wilczek charge of the edge ladder, $Q_{\rm edge}=-\tfrac12\eta$, with $\eta$ its spectral asymmetry. At $\Phi=\pi$ one unit of charge crosses the disk. We ask how the rim operator, the Schur complement of the disk Hamiltonian on its boundary sites, registers this transfer. Its count of negative eigenvalues never changes over the flux cycle. Instead, the unit of charge enters the rim through a simple pole: the extremal eigenvalue of the rim operator passes through infinity in the same flux interval as the charge jump, with $\Delta Q_{\rm edge}=\tfrac12\Delta\,\mathrm{sign}\,\lambda_{\rm ext}$. The residue factorizes into the coupling of the inner edge mode to the rim and the inverse slope of that mode's level, and grows linearly with the radius. All statements are checked numerically on disks of radius $R=11$, $19$ and $34$.

items.title: Computing rare events in L\'evy-driven systems via optimal control
items.summary: We extend the optimal control formulation of sample path large deviation theory, which has proven effective for numerical computation of instantons and sharp probability estimates in stochastic differential equations with Gaussian noise, to systems with light-tailed L\'evy noise. In the scaling limit of small jumps and high intensity, such systems satisfy a large deviation principle of Freidlin-Wentzell type, with a running cost given by the Legendre transform of the noise cumulant generating function. We propose to numerically minimize this cost over noise realizations subject to the system dynamics, which yields the instanton without having to solve Hamilton's equations, and naturally handles degenerate and multiplicative noise. When the cumulant generating function has a bounded domain, the cost grows only linearly for large noise, and instantons can contain jumps. We analyze when jumps are not only admissible but optimal, depending on the subleading behavior of the cost and on the drift, and show how jumps can be resolved numerically through a time reparameterization that freezes physical time. For continuous instantons, we derive Riccati and Fredholm determinant expressions for the leading-order prefactor, and we discuss the modifications needed when the instanton jumps. We illustrate and validate our methods against Monte Carlo simulations in several examples: a two-dimensional nonlinear model, an active run-and-tumble particle with non-Gaussian tumbling noise, and the Ghil-Sellers energy balance climate model with L\'evy-perturbed solar forcing.

items.title: Galerkin methods for unconventional superconductors with long-range interactions on 3D lattices
authors: Andreas A. Buchheit, Torsten Ke{\ss}ler, Sergej Rjasanow
items.summary: We develop an analysis and a B-spline Galerkin method for the matrix-valued Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) gap equation of unconventional superconductors with general long-range interaction kernels on arbitrary Bravais lattices. We define the BCS free energy functional on lattices, show that it is bounded from below, and characterise solutions of the gap equation as its stationary points. For non-repulsive kernels, we prove that fixed-point iteration never increases the free energy and drives the residual to zero. The algebraically decaying tails of the interaction are described by Epstein zeta functions, so the method applies to any power-law exponent $\nu>0$, including exponents at or below the lattice dimension such as dipolar interactions in three-dimensional lattices. In the B-spline Galerkin basis, the singular convolutions correspond to block-circulant matrices whose eigenvalues are lattice sums, applied without quadrature at FFT cost. Each iteration takes log-linear work and linear memory, and Broyden updates accelerate convergence. By engineering a suitable dispersion for a prescribed gap, we obtain non-trivial analytic singlet and triplet solutions of the gap equation with power-law interactions on the integer lattice at zero temperature, to our knowledge the first ones. Benchmarks against these solutions and against highly resolved numerical data show convergence rates determined by the B-spline degree and the regularity of the solution. Finally, we compute a nodal superconductor with long-range interactions on the three-dimensional fcc lattice: a chiral state with a line node and two topologically non-trivial Weyl point nodes. On 16 cores, the method reaches a residual of $1.5\times10^{-13}$ for 6.3 million complex unknowns in less than two minutes.

items.title: A Compact Single-Flange Low-Energy Inverse Photoemission Spectrometer with Elliptical-Mirror Photon Collection
authors: Jong-Am Hong, Min-Jae Maeng, Kyu-Myung Lee, Seunggu Lee, In-Sung Park, Yongsup Park
items.summary: Low-energy inverse photoemission spectroscopy (LEIPS) is limited by weak photon emission, so photon collection optics largely determine its sensitivity. We compare four photon-collection configurations, each addressing a limitation of its predecessor: a detector beside the sample without collection optics (no-mirror), an off-axis parabolic (OAP) mirror delivering a collimated beam to a head-on photomultiplier tube (PMT), external optics coupling the OAP output to a side-on PMT with about twice the quantum efficiency (OAP-external), and an in-vacuum elliptical mirror focusing the emitted light onto the detector (elliptical). Ray-tracing shows that the elliptical mirror delivers 91.9% of the emitted photons to the detector, compared with 63.3% for the OAP mirror and 3.06% without a mirror, while a plane mirror folding the light path by about 90$^\circ$ allows the electron gun, collection optics and detector to fit on a single 8-inch flange. For C$_{60}$ films, the elliptical configuration gives the highest lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) intensity of the four, 271 counts per second per $\mu$A of sample current, 1.74 and 3.23 times those of the OAP and OAP-external configurations and about 45 times that of the no-mirror configuration. The gain over the OAP configuration is comparable to the 1.45-fold increase predicted by ray-tracing, but the filter and detector also differed, so the geometric contribution could not be isolated. The OAP-external configuration gave only 0.54 times the OAP signal despite its higher quantum efficiency. High sensitivity therefore requires both a large collection solid angle and a short optical path kept inside the vacuum.

items.title: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
items.summary: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistently across diverse business scenarios. This paper presents a statistical framework for evaluating uncertainty and reliability in agentic systems. We define a hierarchy of scenarios, instances, and samples to assess model performance and variability systematically. We apply this framework to common metrics found in the literature: mean pass rate, $pass@k$, and $passhat^k$, with uncertainty estimates for each metric. Aggregating metrics at different levels of the hierarchy reveals different structures and properties of the policy model; we connect this hierarchical aggregation with the known process of \emph{coarse-graining} as intended in the physics and statistical literature. We independently derive exact finite-sample expressions for the sampling variances of the unbiased $pass@k$ and $passhatk$ estimators; related results also appear in recent submissions. Our central contribution is a constructive derivation of hierarchical uncertainty propagation, making explicit its correspondence with coarse-graining and separating execution noise from task heterogeneity.

items.title: Formulation of Brownian chain molecular dynamics and the path-resolved quasi-density operator
items.summary: Brownian chain molecular dynamics (BCMD) [M. Shiga, J. Comput. Chem. 43, 1864 (2022)] was introduced as a practical path-integral-based approach to approximate quantum vibrational dynamics in molecular and condensed-phase systems. Its equations of motion combine Newtonian dynamics of the centroid variables with overdamped Brownian dynamics of the non-centroid path variables. Here, we introduce a path-resolved quasi-density-operator (path-QDO) representation by extending the QDO construction underlying centroid molecular dynamics to the full discretized imaginary-time path. For two position-diagonal observables, this representation gives an exact expression for the Kubo-transformed correlation function in the fine-discretization limit, without requiring either observable to be linear. BCMD can be viewed as a phenomenological, time-homogeneous Markov approximation to the exact reduced propagation in these path variables, although its generator is not derived from the path-QDO formulation. We also formulate and validate a multiple-time-step algorithm that allows pseudo-Hamiltonian errors in the deterministic propagation to be controlled by separating the Brownian refresh interval from the inner integration time step. We test the path-QDO representation on one-dimensional models and present BCMD infrared spectra of q-TIP4P/F ice, ambient water, and hot water, comparing them with published results from other approximate quantum-dynamics methods.

items.title: Mesoscale Neural Operators: Learning Nonlinear Constitutive Laws from Molecular Dynamics for Scalable Fracture Predictions
authors: Yue Yu, Jihong Wang, Stewart Silling, Ziwei Yang
items.summary: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can capture the nanoscale physics of fracture at the atomistic level, but their computational cost prohibits predictions at the length scales and time scales needed for many applications. Machine learning approaches, on the other hand, have been proposed as heuristic surrogates for material fracture, yet they cannot guarantee the physical consistency of the predicted response. To address this shortcoming, we propose the mesoscale neural operator (MNO): a data-driven nonlocal constitutive model that is learned directly from MD loading and displacement data. After training, it can be used in continuum fracture simulations on much larger domains and grid sizes. The key idea of the MNO is to exploit the built-in characteristic length of a nonlocal model, called the horizon, to travel across scales. Physical consistency across scales is obtained by building two structural ingredients into the MNO: a normalized kernel that renders the strain energy density invariant under horizon rescaling, and a rescaled critical bond stretch that keeps the energy release rate consistent across scales. Through tests on synthetic data, we show that the MNO and its learning workflow indeed discover the nonlocal continuum multiscale model in the form of the nonlocal kernel and the nonlinear constitutive relation. We then apply the framework to coarse-grained MD data and find that in a test problem, the learned model matches the MD strain energy density and critical energy release rate within 3%. It also predicts the peak transmitted forces within 6% in out-of-distribution tension tests. As a further demonstration, the model is applied to a plate with 4000 times the area of the training specimens and containing an initial defect. In this problem, the model reproduces the main features of dynamic brittle fracture, including branch and cascading branch networks.

items.title: A phase diagram for training and inference in language models
authors: Zhuo-Yang Song, Zeyu Li, Qing-Hong Cao, Ming-xing Luo, Hua Xing Zhu
items.summary: A language model is a complex system whose behavior is determined jointly by the Transformer and the corpus, yet how the representation geometry in the Transformer relates to the actual behavior of language models remains open. We analyze how the representation geometry changes along the forward propagation of actual language models and characterize the representation geometry of a document at a given layer by two collective coordinates, document distinguishability and document dimension. On the phase diagram spanned by these collective coordinates, inference is represented as a flow along depth. We find that, for untrained models, depending on their initialization scale, most of the 156 inference flows move toward the collapse and noise regions of the phase diagram. By contrast, the inference flows of 8 trained models from 5 architecture families all enter and reside in the central region of the phase diagram. Describing the evolution of the flows with a discrete Langevin equation, we find that the difference between the inference flows of untrained runs and those of trained models reduces to whether the effective force on the flows in this region is of saddle or stable-node type. On Pythia-1.4B, we interpret the training process as a phase transition. These results give a unified gateway to the relation between representation geometry and language-model behavior.

items.title: Effect of Mangosteen Peel (Garcinia mangostana L.) and Grass Jelly Leaf (Cyclea barbata L. Miers) Natural Dye Mixing Ratio on the Optical, Morphological, and Photovoltaic Properties of Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells (DSSC)
authors: Eka Nurfani, Haifa Salsabila, Dwiky I. Bakhtiar, Wahyu S. Sipahutar, M Alvien Ghifari, Rishal Asri, Meqorry Yusfi, Tarmizi Taher, Aditya Rianjanu, Robi Kurniawan
items.summary: Dye-sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) are promising low-cost and environmentally friendly photovoltaic devices. This study explores the effect of the mixing ratio of natural dyes extracted from mangosteen peel (MP) and grass jelly leaves (GJL) on the optical, chemical, morphological, and photovoltaic properties of DSSCs. Dye solutions were prepared from crude extracts at a fixed concentration of 0.6 g/mL, with MP:GJL volume ratios varied from 3:1 to 1:3. UV-Vis absorption spectra showed that MP contributes to the UV-blue region (350-450 nm) and GJL to the red region (600-700 nm), giving the mixtures a broader, more panchromatic absorption. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectra confirmed that both extracts share hydroxyl (-OH) and carbonyl/carboxyl (C=O, C-O) groups capable of anchoring the pigments onto TiO$_2$, with a stronger glycosidic C-O-C band for MP. Optical and FESEM imaging revealed that balanced and GJL-rich mixtures form more uniform, crack-free films than single dyes. Current-voltage (J-V) measurements of three independently fabricated cells per composition (n=3) under identical white-light illumination showed that the 1:3 (MP:GJL) ratio gave the highest apparent power conversion efficiency, about 1.3 and 1.7 times that of the single MP and GJL dyes, respectively. Because the input power was estimated photometrically (lux) rather than with a calibrated AM1.5G source, these efficiencies are apparent (relative) indicators for comparing samples, not absolute values. The improvement is attributed to the complementary absorption of the two pigments, while direct electrochemical confirmation of the charge-transfer mechanism remains for future work.

items.title: A General-Purpose and Efficient Machine-Learned Potential for SiC from Ambient to Extreme Environments
authors: Jintong Wu, Zhuang Shao, Junlei Zhao, Flyura Djurabekova, Kai Nordlund, Fredric Granberg, Qingmin Zhang, and Jesper Byggm\"astar
items.summary: Silicon carbide (SiC) polymorphs are widely employed as nuclear materials, mechanical components, and wide-bandgap semiconductors. The rapid advancement of SiC-based applications has been complemented by computational modeling studies, including both ab initio and classical atomistic approaches. In this work, we develop a computationally efficient, general-purpose machine-learned interatomic potential (ML-IAP) capable of multimillion-atom molecular dynamics simulations. Building on the tabulated Gaussian approximation potential (tabGAP) framework, we introduce an additional embedding term that captures local atomic coordination, improving accuracy and generality, while retaining high computational efficiency. Using this ML-tabGAP model, we map a broad pressure-temperature phase diagram, simulate the threshold displacement energy distributions for the 2H and 3C polymorphs, and simulate primary irradiation damage in 3C. Across a benchmark covering conditions from ambient to extreme, including high-pressure/high-temperature states and high-energy cascade damage, tabGAP provides a favorable balance of accuracy, robustness, transferability, and computational cost among the tested empirical and ML-IAPs.

items.title: Pseudospin order of the Bogoliubov de Gennes Hamiltonian
items.summary: We investigate a two-dimensional superconducting system with a smoothly and periodically varying order parameter, which is modulated along one direction while remaining uniform in the perpendicular direction, leading to a spatially periodic superconducting phase. It is known that the phase of the order parameter determines the relative phaseof the quasiparticle components. Here we demonstrate that the latter becomes observable through the associated Bloch vector, which provides a topological invariant that links the Bloch vector to an integer winding number. The Bloch vector can be understood as the expectation value of the pseudospin, for which the physical manifestation of the winding number is a helical ordering. For the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian with an edge we have both plane-wave solutions describing bulk states and exponentially localized solutions that correspond to edge modes. The analytic bulk-edge connection is employed to identify the conditions under which the edge states emerge from the bulk spectrum. The pseudospin ordering rotates under the energy change of the edge modes but is energy-independent for the bulk modes, except for the opposite sign in the upper and the lower band. These results establish a direct connection between the spatial modulation of the order parameter, the topological structure of the Bloch vector, as well as the relation between the order parameter phase and the pseudospin orientation of the edge modes.

items.title: Towards superior van der Waals density functionals for molecular crystals
authors: Dmitry V. Fedorov, Nikita E. Rybin, Mikhail A. Averyanov, Alexander V. Shapeev, Artem R. Oganov, Carlo Nervi
items.summary: Ubiquitous van der Waals (vdW) interactions play a subtle yet crucial role in determining the precise atomic arrangements in solids, particularly in molecular crystals where these weak forces are the primary link between constituent building blocks. Within density functional (DF) theory, the most natural approach to address them is the use of vdW-inclusive density functionals. Through a detailed analysis of the underlying formalism, we have developed a computational scheme that combines vdW functionals of type DF1 and DF2 providing a readily tunable framework to improve the theoretical description and prediction of molecular crystals and other sparse materials. The proof of principle is demonstrated by benchmarking our method on the X23 dataset of molecular crystals.

items.title: Approximate Surface Tension of Phase Separating Interfaces using Residual Forces
items.summary: Extending methods that have been successful in determining the surface tension of equilibrium interfaces to active Brownian particle systems have resulted in negative and/or unusually large values of the interfacial tension, raising questions about the applicability of these frameworks to nonequilibrium interfaces. The absence of a general framework for understanding interfacial tension independently of equilibrium thermodynamics makes this problem particularly challenging. Here, I develop a new framework that provides an order-of-magnitude estimate of the interfacial tension using average force densities that are accessible even when the system is not in thermodynamic equilibrium. Applying this framework to active interfaces yields estimates that differ substantially in both sign and magnitude from previously reported results, highlighting the need to reassess existing approaches to interfacial tension in active matter.

items.title: A Quantum Many-Body Approach for Orbital Magnetism in Correlated Multiband Electron Systems
items.summary: Orbital magnetism is a purely quantum phenomenon that reflects intrinsic electronic properties of solids, yet its microscopic description in interacting multiband systems remains incomplete. We develop a general quantum many-body framework for orbital magnetic responses based on the Luttinger--Ward functional. Starting from the Dyson equation, we reformulate the thermodynamic potential in a weak magnetic field and construct a controlled expansion in powers of $B$ applicable to correlated electron systems. A key technical advance is a modified ``Fourier'' representation using noncommutative coordinates, which allows the thermodynamic potential to be expressed in an effective momentum space where the magnetic field acts perturbatively. This formulation makes analytic progress possible within the Moyal algebra. As an application, we derive the spontaneous orbital magnetization for approximations whose skeleton diagrams contain no fermion loop enclosing magnetic flux (e.g., Hartree--Fock, self-consistent RPA, and single-site dynamical mean-field theory). Vertex corrections consistent with the self-energy are included automatically, without a separate diagrammatic analysis, and the result is expressed entirely in terms of the zero-field Hamiltonian renormalized by the self-energy. For frequency-dependent but Hermitian self-energies, we generalize the orbital magnetic moment and Berry curvature to momentum-frequency space and identify two gauge-invariant contributions built from these quantities. For frequency-independent self-energies the result reduces to the familiar geometric formula for noninteracting systems. This framework provides a unified foundation for computing orbital magnetic responses in correlated multiband materials.

items.title: Band splitting in the altermagnet CrSb
items.summary: Altermagnets are a class of metallic magnets characterized by spin-split electron bands. Like an- tiferromagnets they lack spontaneous bulk magnetisation. The initial description of the momentum dependent spin splitting of electron bands in altermagnets was based on the spin groups approach, which is valid when relativistic interactions are neglected. Then the spin-orbit coupling has been taken into account according with time-reversal-odd, even-parity irreducible representations of cen- trosymmetric point groups formally considered by R.M.Fernandes et al, Phys.Rev.B 109, 024404 (2024). The problem of electron band splitting should be discussed based on crystal symmetry of concrete altermagnet material. Here, the band spin-splitting in hexagonal altermagnet CrSb is established using magnetic groups formalism that allows to find the additional spin splitting missed in frame of exchange approximation. Another type of spin splitting takes place in so called hidden altermagnets. This type materials do not possess symmetry in respect of space and time inversion but are symmetric in respect of the product of these operations known as toroid symmetry. There is demonstrated the real space spin splitting in materials with toroid symmetry.

items.title: Linear response of the Chern insulator MnBi$_2$Te$_4$: A Wannier function approach
authors: Matthew Albert, Javier Sivianes, Jason G. Kattan, Julen Iba\~nez-Azpiroz, J. E. Sipe
items.summary: Recent work demonstrated that in the long wavelength limit the linear response of a Chern insulator to finite-frequency electric fields is the sum of two terms: A general frequency-dependent Kubo contribution that is present irrespective of band topology, and a topological Hall term that vanishes for topologically trivial insulators. Motivated by recent experiments and theoretical predictions, we use these expressions to calculate the optical conductivity and susceptibility of intrinsically magnetic MnBi$_2$Te$_4$ thin films with one, four, five, and eleven septuple layers by combining density functional theory with "single-shot" Wannier functions. To characterize the underlying topology of these systems, we compute the two-dimensional Chern number of these films using recently derived global expressions formulated in terms of Bloch energies and velocity matrix elements; the use of these expressions allows us to circumvent numerical issues at band crossings. Films with eleven septuple layers are of particular interest. We find that they have the same Chern number as five septuple layer films, in contrast to the reported "higher Chern-number phase" of these systems in other studies; we discuss a few possible reasons for the discrepancy. A layer-resolved decomposition of the static reactive susceptibility reveals a non-uniform spatial distribution, with interlayer contributions dominating over intralayer contributions and the bulk layers accounting for nearly 70% of the total response. We also identify spin-orbit coupling-driven band inversions as a possible indicator of these topological phases.

items.title: Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in $PT$ antiferromagnets
items.summary: Surface altermagnetism extends spin splitting beyond bulk altermagnets through symmetry reduction at surfaces and interfaces. An existing classification applies to the local symmetry of atomically flat surface terraces. Here we address the symmetry of macroscopic spin-momentum correlations that survive averaging over compensated rough surfaces. These correlations are governed by the surface antisymmetry Laue class. Because rough-surface altermagnetism is forbidden at any surface of a magnet with antitranslations, the classification reduces to $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets. By restoring all symmetries leaving the surface normal invariant, roughness can generate compensated surface altermagnets from uncompensated flat terminations or suppress spin splitting. Roughness-robust surface altermagnetism in $PT$-symmetric antiferromagnets offers a route to combine bulk electrical switchability with altermagnetic surface transport.

items.title: Gate-Controlled Spin Qubits in Confined Altermagnets
items.summary: We propose gate-defined spin qubits in electrostatically confined altermagnetic quantum dots, together with an electrical spin-drive channel that requires neither spin-orbit coupling (SOC) nor micromagnets or field gradients. Elliptical confinement projects the $d$-wave altermagnetic spin splitting onto the discrete dot spectrum, producing a low-energy qubit doublet whose splitting follows the gate geometry, with a microwave-range qubit gap and a meV-range leakage gap over the parameter ranges studied. Because the projected splitting tracks the confinement anisotropy, a phase-controlled resonant quadrupolar gate drive implements $X_{\pi/2}$ and $X_\pi$ rotations in time-dependent simulations. The drive matrix element is set by the non-relativistic altermagnetic hopping rather than by an SOC coefficient, with a static in-plane field of a few tenths of a tesla supplying the transverse mixing. The qubit has no first-order coupling to uniform electric-field noise, and its first-order quadrupolar charge-noise sensitivity vanishes at the circular point, where the drive is strongest. Two-electron configuration-interaction calculations of a double dot yield an isolated logical two-qubit manifold with a nonzero nonlocal Pauli block, and resonant central-barrier modulation implements a perfectly entangling fSim gate. Within this model, confined altermagnets thus provide the ingredients for universal gate-based control from local electrostatic gates; we identify the material and device conditions that a realization must meet.

items.title: Phase-field modeling of elastically driven abnormal grain growth
authors: Yazhuo Liu, Yin Zhang, Kunqing Ding, Yichen Yang, Alejandro Barrios, Xavier Maeder, Olivier Pierron, Xing Liu, Ting Zhu
items.summary: Grain-refined metals offer high strength, yet their engineering applications are often constrained by grain coarsening under mechanical loading. Recent experiments have revealed room-temperature abnormal grain growth (AGG) in ultrafine-grained Ni thin films subjected to cyclic loading. This phenomenon occurs in the regime of macroscopic elastic deformation, unlike conventional AGG, which generally requires substantial plastic deformation or high temperatures. The AGG process is characterized by the preferential growth of grains whose in-plane <100> orientations are aligned with the loading direction. Here, we investigate the underlying physical mechanisms by combining phase-field simulations with micromechanical analysis. The results indicate that a reduction in elastic energy provides a thermodynamic driving force for orientation-selective grain growth. Phase-field simulations reveal the kinetic evolution of AGG and demonstrate that local grain geometry and stress state influence grain growth pathways. By applying this framework to materials with varying degrees of elastic anisotropy, we establish a general approach for investigating elastically driven AGG in polycrystalline systems.

items.title: Interface-Confined Superconductivity with Thickness-Independent Superfluid Stiffness in (Pb,Sn)Te/FeTe Bilayers
authors: Zi-Jie Yan, Hongtao Rong, Yiyuan Luo, Yufei Zhao, Pu Xiao, Cequn Li, Zihao Wang, Lok-Kan Lai, Annie G. Wang, Zhiyuan Xi, Yanxing Li, Xiaoyu Wei, Ke Wang, Katja C. Nowack, Binghai Yan, Chih-Kang Shih, Cui-Zu Chang
items.summary: Interface-induced superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures provides a promising route toward topological superconductivity, yet the roles of the neighboring layers topology, symmetry, and electronic structure remain unresolved. In this work, we employ molecular beam epitaxy to grow Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers and use angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to track the evolution of the Pb1-xSnxTe layer from a trivial insulator to a topological crystalline insulator hosting multiple Dirac surface states. Electrical transport measurements reveal robust superconductivity throughout the entire composition range, with a nearly constant superconducting transition temperature of ~12 K despite substantial changes in the electronic structure and topology of Pb1-xSnxTe. Double-coil mutual-inductance measurements further reveal comparable superfluid stiffness across the topological phase transition and nearly thickness-independent superfluid stiffness despite large variations in the constituent-layer thicknesses, demonstrating that superconductivity is confined near the interface. These results establish that superconductivity in FeTe-based heterostructures is largely insensitive to the topology, crystal symmetry, and detailed electronic structure of the neighboring layer, supporting a primary origin in modifications to the FeTe layer. The coexistence of interface-confined superconductivity and tunable multiple Dirac surface states in Pb1-xSnxTe/FeTe bilayers provides a versatile platform for exploring topological superconductivity and interactions among multiple Majorana zero modes.

items.title: Model inference from fluid flow in continuum theories of active matter
authors: Aditya Mohapatra, Sagarika Adhikary, Rajesh Singh
items.summary: Active matter systems are driven out of thermodynamic equilibrium by localized, microscale energy dissipation. While active field theories are highly successful at simulating these non-equilibrium phenomena (the forward problem), characterizing real-world active materials is fundamentally bottle-necked by the difficulty of measuring active stresses directly. This paper addresses the inverse problem using deep learning: model inference and model selection from observable flow field data of active fluids.
