We formulate an inversion framework applied to two cornerstone paradigms of active continuum physics: Active Model H (representing scalar active matter) and Active Nematics (representing active systems with orientational order). We demonstrate that the kinetic energy spectrum obtained from the fluid flow field preserves a high-fidelity signature of activity to infer parameters of active model H and active nematics. The classification of the models requires comparison using conventional numerical work against predicted parameters. Our deep learning method presents a principled way to bear upon questions of model inference and selection given the flow field data in continuum models of active matter.

items.title: Valley-controlled chiral magnetism in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers
authors: Igor S. Krivenko, Vladimir N. Mantsevich, Dmitry S. Smirnov
items.summary: We put forward the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida (RKKY) interaction in transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers as a tool to create and control a chiral magnetic texture. We show that in the spin-valley locking regime, the RKKY interaction acts as a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya coupling with an effective spin rotation period exactly equal to the tripled lattice constant. Using mean field theory and classical Monte Carlo simulations, we demonstrate that this interaction qualitatively reshapes the phase diagram of atomically thin antiferromagnets. It destroys the chirality-related phase transition by selecting a single chirality value even when the RKKY interaction is small. At the same time, it shifts the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition associated with spins orientation to higher temperatures. We argue that the valley degree of freedom of electrons mediating the RKKY interaction provides a powerful control knob for exploring non-universal phase transitions and quantum spin liquid states in two-dimensional van der Waals heterostructures.

items.title: Thermal Stability of Two-Dimensional Crystals with Extended OH Hydrogen-Bonded Chains
items.summary: Numerical simulations of the dynamics of monolayer structures of molecules deposited on a sheet of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) have been performed. It is shown that molecules containing benzene rings and hydroxyl groups can form stable two-dimensional crystals with linear hydrogen-bonded chains OH$\cdots$OH$\cdots$OH$\cdots$. Such structures are formed by the following molecules: phenol (C$_6$H$_5$OH), hydroquinone (C$_6$H$_4$(OH)$_2$), 4-phenylphenol (C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_4$OH), 4-(4-phenylphenyl)phenol (C$_6$H$_5$-C$_6$H$_4$-C$_6$H$_4$OH), paracetamol (CH$_3$C(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH), 4-hydroxybenzanilide (C$_6$H$_5$C(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH) and 4,4$^\prime$-dihydroxybenzanilide (C$_6$H$_4$OHC(O)NHC$_6$H$_4$OH). On the one hand, the benzene rings in these molecules ensure their strong interaction with the flat substrate; on the other hand, they do not hinder the formation of long hydrogen-bonded chains. The monolayer structures of these molecules exhibit high thermal stability: the onset melting temperatures of their 2D crystals are 112, 257, 237, 337, 277, 407, and 483$^\circ$C, respectively. The simulations suggest that structures composed of h-BN sheets and molecules of hydroquinone, paracetamol, 4-hydroxybenzanilide and 4,4$^\prime$-dihydroxybenzanilide can be used for the development of novel proton-exchange membranes capable of operating at elevated temperatures.

items.title: Kinetic Lifshitz invariants and dynamics of nonreciprocal fluctuations in superconductors
authors: Tony Liu, Joaquim Telles de Miranda, Daniel Shaffer, Alex Levchenko
items.summary: We derive the generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau theory of a disordered noncentrosymmetric superconductor from the Keldysh nonlinear sigma model, using a two-dimensional electron gas with Rashba spin-orbit coupling and an in-plane Zeeman field as a minimal model. On the thermodynamic side we construct the Lifshitz invariants of the free energy, the linear and cubic gradient terms and the momentum-odd part of the quartic vertex, and trace their dependence on disorder. The couplings of the quadratic sector are governed by a single closed-form kernel controlled by the ratio of the Dyakonov-Perel spin-relaxation rate to temperature. It interpolates between the weak-relaxation regime, where the invariants are suppressed, and the relaxation-dominated regime, where the helical modulation of the order parameter saturates at a universal, disorder-independent value. This crossover reconciles known results for the magnetoelectric couplings of disordered Rashba superconductors. Because the theory is formulated on the Keldysh contour, it also determines the dissipative dynamics: the relaxation rate of a fluctuation with pair momentum $q$, and hence the Langevin noise power, acquires a term odd in $q$ and odd in the magnetic field. The structure of this kinetic Lifshitz invariant is dictated by Onsager reciprocity: friction and noise change together, so that equal-time fluctuations remain Gibbsian while the relaxation dynamics becomes nonreciprocal. As applications we compute the superconducting diode efficiency near $T_c$, where the cubic invariant competes with the quartic vertex and with higher-gradient terms, reversing the sign of the diode coefficient. We also consider fluctuation-induced magnetochiral anisotropy above $T_c$, which grows as the inverse square of the distance to $T_c$ and is suppressed in the relaxation-dominated regime.

items.title: Optical Voltage Profiling of 2D Semiconductors via Proximal Exciton Sensing
authors: Ha-Leem Kim, Hyungbin Lim, Yuanyi Yang, Ruishi Qi, Ruichen Xia, Can Uzundal, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Feng Wang
items.summary: High contact resistances in atomically thin semiconductors often mask intrinsic electrical transport properties, particularly at low carrier densities where exotic correlated states emerge. We introduce optical voltage profiling, a noninvasive wide-field technique that replaces local voltage probes with a proximal monolayer MoSe$_2$ exciton sensor. Isolated by thin hexagonal boron nitride, this sensor converts the target's local voltage into spatially resolved modulations of exciton reflectance. Through pixel-wise in situ calibration, these signals yield quantitative two-dimensional voltage maps of an actively biased semiconductor device. Using this method, we demonstrate the carrier-density-driven metal-insulator transition in bilayer MoSe$_2$ and obtain channel resistances of a few k$\Omega$ despite M$\Omega$-scale two-terminal resistances in the metallic region. The optically derived resistance exhibits a metal-insulator crossover, and the voltage maps and reconstructed local conductivity reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity in both insulating and metallic regimes. Beyond resolving channel resistance under high contact-resistance conditions, the technique provides spatially resolved access to microscopic transport heterogeneity in functional van der Waals devices.

items.title: Dynamic Pseudogap Model
authors: E. Z. Kuchinskii, M. V. Sadovskii
items.summary: We formulate a theory of pseudogap formation generated by dynamic finite nesting vector ${\bf Q}$ fluctuations with characteristic oscillation frequency $\omega_0$, and damping $\gamma$. Starting from a Hamiltonian describing electrons coupled to a classical Gaussian random field, we introduce the double - series representations of the single - particle Green's function within an Abelian (commuting) approximation to the exact SU(2) time evolution of the pseudogap problem. The resulting propagator naturally acquires a generalized Bogoliubov structure in which every stochastic scattering history is characterized by an effective dynamic gap, leading to a coherent superposition of dynamically broadened sidebands with complex Poisson weights. A central result of the theory is the emergence of a dynamically generated decoherence scale $\Gamma_{\rm eff}$ governing the crossover between two qualitatively different pseudogap regimes. For $\omega_0>\Gamma_{\rm eff}$ the fluctuating field is resolved coherently and the double-series representation provides a controlled description of dynamic sideband formation. Conversely, when $\Gamma_{\rm eff}\gtrsim\omega_0$, coherence is progressively lost and the theory crosses over to the quasistatic fluctuating - gap regime described by the exact continued-fraction solution. The coherent and quasistatic descriptions are therefore interpreted as two complementary asymptotic limits of the same microscopic dynamic pseudogap model. The detailed results of numerical calculations for electron spectral density and density of states supporting our approach are presented for different sets of model parameters confirming the general picture of this crossover.

items.title: Exact autoregressive sampling of planar Ising spin glasses via the Kac--Ward theory
authors: Jing Liu, Tao Chen, Tianrui Che, Lei Wang, Youjin Deng, Pan Zhang
items.summary: Independent samples from the Boltzmann distribution are valuable for estimating spin-glass observables and evaluating approximate sampling methods. Local Markov chain Monte Carlo methods typically generate temporally correlated samples and can encounter critical slowing down or metastable trapping, while neural autoregressive samplers such as variational autoregressive networks generate independent but approximate samples. Here we present an exact autoregressive sampling algorithm for planar Ising spin glasses based on the Kac--Ward theory. Under the chain-rule factorization, sequentially fixing spins induces boundary-localized external fields, which destroy the zero-field structure required for exact evaluation. By encoding these fields with a planarity-preserving auxiliary spin construction, the conditional partition functions are mapped to an extended zero-field Ising model and exactly evaluated using the Kac--Ward determinant formula. The method generates strictly independent and identically distributed samples with exact normalized likelihoods at a computational cost of $\mathcal{O}(N^{5/2})$ for $N$ spins, thereby providing an exact baseline for benchmarking neural autoregressive samplers.

items.title: Coexistence of polariton bound states in the continuum and 2D radiative excitons
authors: Simone Zanotti, Marco Liscidini, Dario Gerace, Lucio C. Andreani
items.summary: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable optical modes with ideally infinite radiative lifetimes despite lying within the radiation continuum. Radiation-matter interaction in periodically patterned planar waveguides embedding two-dimensional (2D) optically active excitations can be described quantum mechanically by diagonalizing a non-Hermitian operator, known as the Hopfield matrix, which can be generalized to incorporate independent photonic and excitonic losses into the polaritonic states. However, since 2D excitons undergo intrinsic wavevector-dependent radiative decay within the light cone, whether the Hopfield formalism can consistently account for this process while preserving polariton BICs has remained an open question. Here we show that a non-Hermitian Hopfield formalism incorporating excitonic radiative losses correctly captures the existence of genuine $k=0$ polariton BICs with diverging radiative lifetimes. The theory provides a unified microscopic framework for radiative excitons and polariton BICs, and an efficient predictive tool for designing photonic-crystal platforms coupled to quantum wells, transition-metal dichalcogenides, and other 2D excitonic materials.

items.title: Prescreening Point Defects in Semiconductors With Machine Learning
authors: Paul Karlsson, Joel Davidsson, Rickard Armiento
items.summary: High-throughput calculations using density-functional theory (DFT) are commonly used to explore point defects for applications in power electronics and quantum technologies. There is currently a major shift away from these traditional simulation techniques towards machine learning (ML) methods. We explore a class of physics-guided ML models for predicting defect formation energies and zero-phonon lines (ZPL) to identify point defects for quantum applications. The models are specifically targeted for use in a prescreening step for accelerated high-throughput workflows, and are therefore designed to avoid the costly relaxation step typically present with ML interatomic potentials (MLIPs). We compare performance for single and double point defect systems in 4H-SiC with ridge, kernel ridge, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) models using three different descriptors representing the defect systems. For vacancies and substitutions, the optimized models give mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 0.478 eV for the formation energy and 0.202 eV for ZPLs, which is just above the level at which such predictions can be useful even beyond the targeted prescreening, i.e., in some applications they may completely replace the need for costly DFT calculations. For interstitials the MAEs are larger, 1.123 eV for the formation energy and 0.230 eV for the ZPL, which, while still useful for prescreening, will not generally be useful for more detailed characterization. Hence, while the results may be further improved by model design and optimization, the models presented in this work are already useful for prescreening in high-throughput characterization of point defects.

items.title: Spin-Exchange Induced Confinement of Correlated Bound States in the Continuum
authors: Kai Chen, Junyan Guan, Zhongming Gu, Jie Zhu
items.summary: Repulsively bound doublons are two-particle composites formed by strong interactions and are usually separated from the scattering continuum. Introducing spin-exchange coupling (SEC) fundamentally alters the underlying band structure, providing a powerful tuning knob to shift these isolated pairs toward this continuum. However, because entering such a regime typically dictates immediate dissociation, whether this coupling can drive these pairs inside while preserving their bound nature constitutes a fundamental unresolved challenge. Here we show that spin-exchange coupling in the one-dimensional extended Fermi-Hubbard model can drive doublons into the two-particle scattering continuum. Most of these states hybridize with extended channels and decay, whereas a subset remains decoupled and spatially bound, forming many-body bound states in the continuum (BICs). We map the interacting two-particle problem onto a two-dimensional lattice of coupled acoustic cavities, and experimentally observe both the radiating doublon continuum and the confined BIC states. These results demonstrate that spin-exchange coupling can turn selected doublons into interaction-induced BICs, deepening the understanding of continuum physics for interaction-bound pairs.

items.title: Memory-induced optimal switching in a dynamic Ising-Kuramoto model
items.summary: We study how internal spin switching competes with phase decorrelation in a globally coupled dynamic Ising--Kuramoto model. Linear response about the nonmagnetic incoherent state gives $K_c=[(\mu+\beta_s\gamma)\chi_\gamma]^{-1}$, where $\chi_\gamma$ is a switching-weighted Laplace transform of the free phase correlation. Under explicit assumptions on that correlation, we establish sufficient conditions for the mean-field linear instability threshold to attain a global minimum at a finite positive switching rate, strictly below both endpoint thresholds. The criterion separates low-rate integrated phase memory from high-rate short-time correlation structure. Finite-correlation-time Ornstein--Uhlenbeck forcing satisfies the high-rate condition; applying the sufficient criterion still requires checking the low-rate moment condition. The white-noise threshold is monotone or exactly flat. Finite-system simulations exhibit appreciable spin-weighted coherence, weak ordinary coherence and a strong antiphase sector bias. On a magnetized background, amplitude ratios are quantitatively consistent with the predicted linear-mode composition locally near onset. Direct finite-size tests of the nonmagnetic threshold minimum remain unresolved under the prespecified support rule, despite the predicted conditional contrast signs at two tested OU times.

items.title: Large-Tiny Spin-Stripe SDW Order in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ via $^{139}$La-NQR Spectroscopy: Reconsideration Based on the $Am2m$ Structure
authors: Mitsuharu Yashima, Hongnam Lee, Takumi Ino, Nina Seto, Masataka Kakoi, Hiroya Sakurai, Yoshihiko Takano, Hidekazu Mukuda
items.summary: The lower-symmetry $Am2m$ structure was recently proposed as the intrinsic ambient-pressure phase of La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ based on synchrotron x-ray diffraction, whereas earlier studies investigated its properties assuming the commonly accepted $Amam$ structure. Here, we reexamine the crystal structure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and the spin configuration of spin-density-wave (SDW) state via $^{139}$La nuclear quadrupole resonance (NQR). The observation of two distinct La(2) sites in the NQR spectra is naturally accounted for by the $Am2m$ structure without any special assumptions, whereas it cannot be reconciled within the $Amam$ framework. Within the $Am2m$ framework, we reanalyze the spin configuration of the SDW phase and identify it as a large-tiny spin-stripe structure, arising naturally from two inequivalent Ni sites with large and tiny magnetic moments. These results establish the itinerant nature of the SDW order at ambient pressure in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$, providing a basis for understanding its relationship to the emergence of high-$T_c$ superconductivity under high pressure.

items.title: Resonant-pair energy return beyond the early Green-Kubo plateau in a quartic chain
authors: Julian Olszewski, Zijian Liu, Jie Xu
items.summary: The Green-Kubo formula gives the thermal conductivity as the long-time limit of the running Green-Kubo integral, the time integral of the equilibrium heat-current autocorrelation function. In simulations, this integral often approaches a plateau at finite time. We study how it evolves after such an early plateau in a weakly coupled chain of quartic oscillators, where the plateau value is close to the rate at which independent neighboring cells exchange energy. Two neighboring cells with nearly equal frequencies form a resonant pair: their relative phase oscillates like a pendulum, and energy that has crossed the bond between them flows back. We show that, at weak coupling, the running integral of such a pair follows the pendulum trapping response of nonlinear Landau damping. For the quartic potential, the small-oscillation period of this pendulum, $T_{\rm lib}\propto\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ with intercell coupling $\varepsilon$, does not depend on energy, so all resonant pairs share one time scale. Without fitted parameters, the theory predicts that the running integral of an isolated pair falls to a negative first minimum of $-0.74$ times the plateau value at $0.952\,T_{\rm lib}$. Simulations of isolated pairs approach this prediction as the coupling decreases. In chains, the first minimum occurs on the same time scale but is shallower, and a small positive value can remain much later. Chains of strongly chaotic cells show no comparable decrease, and energy-conserving noise much faster than $1/T_{\rm lib}$ largely removes the decrease. The pair response provides a quantitative finite-time reference for interpreting early Green-Kubo plateaus in such chains.

items.title: Topology of Wannierizable Insulators
items.summary: We study the freedom in choosing Wannier centers and the associated symmetry representations in noninteracting Wannierizable insulators. We compare Wyckoff deformations of atomic configurations with symmetry-preserving adiabatic deformations of occupied states, both with and without adding common occupied atomic orbitals. Explicit examples show that stable Wyckoff equivalence and adiabatic equivalence at fixed filling do not imply each other. In spinless $Fm'm'm'$, an Euler class distinguishes stably Wyckoff-equivalent configurations. In spinless $P\overline1'$, adiabatically equivalent configurations remain distinct under stable Wyckoff deformations. We also classify when stable Wyckoff and stable adiabatic equivalence coincide. They agree in two or fewer dimensions and in three-dimensional spinful systems. For three-dimensional spinless systems, Chern insulator pumps give additional equivalences in 134 magnetic space groups. These groups preserve spacetime orientation and have a point whose site-symmetry group contains $222$, $\overline1'$, or $\overline4'$.

items.title: Transport in spinful non-Hermitian gauge lattices
authors: Hamed Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Shahram Dehdashti, Janis N\"otzel
items.summary: We extend the generalized transfer-matrix method introduced in [H. Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Phys.\ Rev.\ B \textbf{107}, 125155 (2023)] to one-dimensional spinful non-Hermitian tight-binding lattices with matrix-valued Abelian and non-Abelian gauge couplings. We derive a minimal channel-resolved transfer matrix and identify its eigenvalues with the generalized Bloch factors. The same transfer matrix determines the periodic- and open-boundary spectra, generalized Brillouin zone, skin localization, and finite-sample scattering conditions. In the Abelian limit, the model separates into fixed spin sectors, yielding exact spectral results and closed finite-length transport expressions in terms of Chebyshev polynomials. These results reveal bipolar spin-dependent skin localization and distinguish the reciprocal hopping scale, which governs poles, zeros, and reflectionlessness, from the directed-amplification factor controlling transmission asymmetry, transparency, and invisibility. For non-Abelian gauge fields, noncommuting link matrices coherently mix the spin sectors, such that four transfer eigenmodes jointly determine the non-Bloch spectrum and transport eigenchannels. We show that this mixing produces spin-hybridized lasing and coherent-perfect-absorption channels, Zeeman-tunable lasing thresholds, and direction-dependent reflectionless transport accompanied by pronounced spin conversion. The resulting boundary-condition criteria describe lasing, coherent perfect absorption, reflectionlessness, transparency, and invisibility, while identifying spin polarization and conversion as experimentally accessible signatures that distinguish Abelian from non-Abelian non-Hermitian transport.

items.title: Quantum 3xplorer: AI-Native Engine for Next-Generation Quantum Materials Modeling
authors: Vsevolod Biryukov, Sergey V. Barabash, Pranab Kumar Das, Jack Deslippe, Mauro Del Ben, Felipe H. da Jornada, Yuming Shi, Johannes Voss, Zhenglu Li, Kamal Choudhary, Ruth Pachter, Steven G. Louie, Marvin L. Cohen, Timur Bazhirov
items.summary: Quantum-mechanical approaches, such as density functional theory (DFT), underpin much of modern computational materials science and are the primary source of data for AI-driven discovery. Yet the established electronic-structure codes today represent decades-old software architectures, making new physical models slow and costly to implement, validate, and deploy on emerging hardware. We present Quantum 3xplorer (Q3, pronounced "Quantum Explorer"), an AI-native quantum simulation engine written from scratch by AI coding agents under the direction and supervision of domain scientists. As a first and demanding validation case, we implement plane-wave pseudopotential DFT end to end: norm-conserving, ultrasoft, and projector-augmented-wave formalisms, spin polarization, DFT+U, and dispersion corrections, together with forces, stresses, structural relaxation, and electronic-structure analysis. Q3 reproduces established reference implementations, runs faster on a single core in representative benchmarks, and scales across GPU-accelerated supercomputers. It was developed in weeks rather than years. Its layered, physics-first architecture separates abstract quantum-mechanical concepts from their numerical representations, making its framework extendable beyond plane waves to other basis sets and levels of theory. Its inputs and outputs follow structured, schema-validated data standards, making every result AI-ready. Q3 is open source under Apache 2.0 and built to be reused, extended, and improved by the research community. Q3 points to a paradigm shift in how computational quantum science is done. Scientists define the physics, formulate the models, and set the criteria for validation; AI agents write, test, and optimize the code. The decades-long path from a new theory to a trusted, high-performance implementation can thus collapse to days, significantly accelerating scientific discovery.

items.title: Nonlinear Physics and Self-Organized Criticality in Astrophysics
items.summary: Since standard photon statistics is not applicable to nonlinear physics processes, it is of utmost importance to properly include the nonlinearity in astrophysical instabilities and emission processes. Bak et al.~(1987) postulated sandpile avalanches and called the underlying principle ``self-organized criticality'' (SOC), but its definition remained ambiguous and controversial. Here we discuss the nonlinear physics of six basic SOC definitions, such as: (i) phase transitions, (ii) fractal structures, (iii) power laws, (iv) SOC contingency, (v) exponential growth, and (vi) diffusive decay. Statistics of SOC events or avalanche processes can be inferred from their size distributions, or from their spatio-temporal evolution, described with the logistic equation. Here we quantify each nonlinear process in terms of quantitative scaling laws.

items.title: Ab Initio strain-dependent vibrational analysis of different silicene structures for 2D devices
items.summary: We report first-principles phonon dynamics studies in isotropically strained mono-layer silicene films of various topologies by density functional theory and density functional perturbation theory methods. The strain introduced in the sheets are of both tensile and compressive nature and its effect on the thermal transport properties are analysed using the Boltzmann Transport Equation (BTE) reported. We performed electronic and vibrational analysis of each silicene topology and concluded that hhk-silicene is a potential candidate for next generation electro-thermal devices due its molecular stability, bulk-Si like bandgap and tolerable thermal performance that can be engineered by strain. The novel hhk-silicene topology offers excellent thermal and electronic capabilities that are sensitive to strain along with the band gap following a near-linear monotonically decreasing trend making it suitable for strain-tronics applications.

items.title: Strain-Glass Dynamics in the Superionic Conductor Na3PS4
authors: Erik S. Lamb, Nicol\`o D'Anna, Phillip Ridley, Nelson Hua, Ivan Zaluzhnyy, James Burrow, Emilio Escauriza, Robin Glefke, Boyan K. Stoychev, Mingze Wan, Zhe Ren, Fabian Westermeier, Michael Sprung, Alex Fra\~n\'o, Ying Shirley Meng, Oleg G. Shpyrko
items.summary: Ionic conduction in solid-state electrolytes is conventionally described as cations migrating through a static host lattice. Yet the fastest conductors are often the most disordered, and how disorder shapes mesoscale transport remains unresolved. Using Bragg X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy on a micrometer-sized ball-milled Na3PS4 particle, we find that the host is not static. The cubic phase behaves as a strain glass of three degenerate tetragonal variants whose domain walls move under residual milling stress, crossing over irreversibly to thermally activated dynamics on annealing. Rearrangements occur as scale-free avalanches, as in ferroelastic martensites but without external driving, while the tetragonal polymorph shows none of these features and relaxes fifty times more slowly. These dynamics evolve on timescales comparable to ionic diffusion across the particle. This work introduces a probe of dynamics in locally frustrated solid electrolytes, revealing that mechanochemical synthesis yields not merely a metastable polymorph, but a stress-driven strain glass.

items.title: Statistical approach of random packing of polydisperse hyperspheres: with application to binomial and lognormal size distributions
items.summary: This paper addresses the packing fraction of polydisperse similar hyperspheres with a discrete binomial and continuous lognormal particle size distribution. First, a closed form expression is derived of a mix consisting of multiple discrete particles in D-dimensional Euclidean space R^D with small size differences. A recently developed analytical model for binary packings with small size ratio u is used, here applying it to the statistically probable particle pairs in the multi-sized mix. The new model is subsequently applied to discretely sized particles with a binomial number distribution and a constant size ratio u between each subsequent particle size. By taking the limit of u -> 1 and an infinite number of particles sizes, the binomial particle distribution is transformed into a continuous lognormal distribution. The resulting expression for the packing fraction can be solved in closed form, resulting in an original expression for the packing fraction of mixtures of hyperparticles with a lognormal distribution. This explicit expression is governed by the standard deviation, the Euclidean dimension D, and the monosized packing fraction of the considered particle shape. For a number of particle shapes and their packing modes (from looser to denser) the scaled expression is thoroughly compared with data reported in the literature. They concern packed particles with small standard deviations and in Euclidean dimensions D = 2 and 3, and good agreement is found. For large standard deviations the scaled packing fraction approaches a limiting value, which appears not to depend on the Euclidean dimension. Based on the insight, a closed form expression is put forward for the packing fraction that matches the small standard deviation solution, and the large standard deviation asymptote, so covering arbitrary standard deviations, Euclidean dimensions, particle types, and their mode of packing.

items.title: The Outer Eshelby Problem in Amorphous Solids with Odd Dipole Screening
authors: Avanish Kumar, Jin Shang, Itamar Procaccia
items.summary: The so-called "2-dimensional Eshelby problem" was defined by JD Eshelby, where a circle is cut out of an elastic sheet, deformed into an ellipse, and forced back into the material. This creates a quadrupolar response which turned out to be very relevant for describing plastic deformations in amorphous solids. Moreover, the resulting strain field has been used to describe how elasto-plastic models respond to external strains. It is thus important to examine carefully the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids, especially when anomalous elasticity is at play. Here we solve the Eshelby problem in amorphous solids with both even and odd dipole screening and a complete analytical result is obtained for the displacement and strain fields. The analytical results are crucial for understanding the anomalous responses in displacement fields measured directly from experiments and numerical simulations. The computation of strain fields clearly demonstrates the deviations from their classical counterparts for perfectly elastic solids. The decomposition of the displacement field shows the excitation of higher-order Fourier modes. The presence of higher excitations other than the imposed Eshelby geometry therefore suggests the possible nonlinear mode coupling that can influence and modify the anomalous responses.

items.title: Quantum inverse scattering for the 20-vertex model up to Dynkin automorphism: 3D Poisson structure, triangular height functions, weak integrability
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We initiate a novel application of the quantum inverse scattering method for the 20-vertex model, building upon seminal work from Faddeev and Takhtajan on the study of Hamiltonian systems. In comparison to a previous work of the author in late 2023 which characterized integrability of a Hamiltonian flow for the 6-vertex model from integrability of inhomogeneous limit shapes, formalized in a work of Keating, Reshetikhin and Sridhar, notions similar to those of integrability can be realized for the 20-vertex model by studying new classes of higher-dimensional L-operators. Such L-operators provided by Boos and colleagues have algebraic, combinatorial, and geometric, qualities, all of which impact leading order approximations of correlations, products of L-operators, the transfer matrix, and the quantum monodromy matrix.

items.title: Observation of an anomaly in the statistics of Kibble-Zurek defects
authors: Jan Balewski, Alexey Khudorozhkov, Siva Darbha, Omar A. Ashour, Fangli Liu, Ermal Rrapaj, Sheng-Tao Wang, Pedro L. S. Lopes, Katherine Klymko, Milan Kornja\v{c}a, Daan Camps
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The Kibble-Zurek mechanism quantifies defect formation during finite-rate passage across a continuous phase transition, providing key insights into universality in quantum many-body systems. We explore counting statistics of defects in finite-rate ramp experiments on long 1D Rydberg atom chains. The experiments reveal an anomaly in the defect number distribution at long ramp times, challenging the hypothesis of defect formation through independent domain mergers. Numerical simulations reproduce the anomaly and support an interpretation in terms of post-critical coarsening during the ramp, while prepare-and-hold experiments reveal no subsequent secular growth of the measured correlations. Our results show the limits of classical or integrable system descriptions of Kibble-Zurek defect formation for interacting quantum systems.

items.title: Quantum Algorithm Framework for Phase-Contrast Transmission Electron Microscopy Image Simulation
authors: Sean D. Lam, Roberto dos Reis
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We present a quantum algorithmic framework for simulating phase-contrast transmission electron microscopy (CTEM) image formation using a fault-tolerant, gate-based quantum circuit model. The electron wavefield on an $N\times N$ grid is amplitude-encoded into a $2\log_2 N$-qubit register. Free-space propagation and objective-lens aberrations are implemented via two-dimensional quantum Fourier transforms (QFTs) and diagonal phase operators in reciprocal space, while specimen interaction is modeled under the phase-object approximation (POA) in a single-slice multislice formulation as a position-dependent phase grating. We validate projected potentials, contrast transfer function (CTF) behavior, and image contrast trends against classical multislice simulations for MoS$_2$ over experimentally relevant parameters, and provide resource estimates and key assumptions that determine end-to-end runtime. Extracting a complete $N\times N$ intensity image by direct sampling requires $O(N^2/\epsilon^2)$ repetitions, which rules out a generic polylogarithmic-cost image-generation algorithm. We therefore analyze end-to-end cost, including state preparation, repeated execution, measurement precision, and the best classical calculation of the same output, and identify the conditions under which limited-output tasks could be candidates for quantum advantage; the present benchmarks establish implementation agreement and do not demonstrate such an advantage. This framework provides a physics-grounded mapping from CTEM theory to quantum circuits and establishes a baseline for extending toward full multislice and inelastic scattering models.

items.title: Topological initial state independence in Boundary Time Crystals
authors: Dominik Nemeth, Ahsan Nazir, Alessandro Principi, Robert-Jan Slager
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Boundary time crystals (BTCs) break time-translation symmetry and exhibit long-lived, robust oscillations insensitive to initial conditions. We show that collective spin BTCs can admit emergent topological winding numbers in operator space. Expanding the density operator in a spherical tensor basis, we map the Lindblad dynamics onto an effective local hopping problem, where collective degrees of freedom label sites of an emergent operator space lattice. Whenever the emergent winding number is non-zero, topological obstructions prevent the localization of operator modes on the lattice and instead enforce their delocalization across operator space. This delocalization enables non-unital sourcing from the identity sector to propagate across operator space and continuously feed the observable sector in an initial state independent manner, thereby generating robust oscillatory responses in the time crystal phase. Our results frame BTC dynamics as a form of topologically constrained operator space transport and suggest a close connection to non-Hermitian skin effects.

items.title: Thermodynamics of Coupled Transport: Quantum Dots as a Model System
authors: Shuvadip Ghosh, Sounak Bandyopadhyay, Arnab Ghosh
items.summary: -cross Abstract: This review presents a thermodynamic perspective on quantum coupled transport processes in nanoscale systems. Our analysis is formulated within the framework of the entropy production rate, the central quantity governing non-equilibrium processes and expressed through conjugate force-flux pairs. Although thermodynamic laws are universal across classical and quantum domains, the discussion is developed within a microscopic open quantum system framework, focusing on quantum dots (QDs) coupled to electronic reservoirs. We first examine elementary single transport processes and highlight their strong thermodynamic constraints in the near-equilibrium regime. This motivates the study of coupled transport, where multiple force-flux pairs coexist and interact, leading to richer thermodynamic behaviour. Using entropy production as the guiding principle, we analyse coupled energy and particle transport in a minimal two-terminal single-QD setup and show how conventional thermoelectric phenomena, including Seebeck and Peltier effects as well as thermoelectric heat engines and refrigerators, naturally emerge as thermodynamic cross-effects. We then extend the framework to a three-terminal coupled quantum dot (CQD) geometry, which provides a versatile platform for studying coupled transport and reduces, under suitable constraints, to the well-known S\'anchez-B\"uttiker configuration. Beyond standard cross-effects, we discuss the phenomenon of inverse currents in coupled transport (ICC), where a current flows against mutually parallel thermodynamic forces without violating the second law. We show that ICC requires breaking the symmetry between energy and particle transport and identify the conditions for its realization in coupled quantum-dot systems with attractive interdot interactions.

items.title: Interfacial Resistance and Preferential Internal Mixing of Phase-Separated Condensates
authors: Oihan Joyot, Zo\'e Ferrand, Fernando Muzzopappa, Pierre Weiss, Fabian Erdel
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Biomolecular condensates spatially organize biochemical processes. They can selectively partition molecules and enrich them well above their concentration outside. Their function depends on the exchange of molecules with their surroundings, whose kinetics are determined not only by partitioning and diffusion but also by interfacial resistance. The latter can hinder molecules from crossing the condensate boundary, thereby increasing their residence times in the condensate and promoting repeated encounters with interaction partners therein. So far, it has proven difficult to measure the interfacial resistance of condensates experimentally. Here, we combine fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) with fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) and calibrated fluorescence imaging to disentangle partitioning, interfacial resistance, and differences in diffusion inside and outside of condensates. Applying this approach to polyelectrolyte condensates across a range of salt concentrations, we find substantial, salt-dependent interfacial resistance, which causes molecules to undergo multiple rounds of internal mixing before escaping. DDX4-YFP condensates in living cells also exhibit substantial interfacial resistance, although they are more permeable than polyelectrolyte condensates with comparable partition coefficients. Our results indicate that interfacial resistance is a tunable property of condensates that can place them in distinct transport regimes, favoring distinct functions such as dynamic reaction crucibles or insulated molecular sinks.

items.title: Raman optical activity and helicity-dependent phonon splitting in chiral CoSi
authors: Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Kohei Miyazaki, Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Ryotaro Arita, Satoshi Iwasaki, Yoshiki Yasuoka, Yusuke Kousaka, Yoshihiko Togawa, Takuya Satoh
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Circularly polarized Raman scattering in solids provides access to two distinct phenomena: Raman optical activity (ROA), an intensity difference between circular polarization channels, and helicity-dependent frequency splitting of chiral phonons. We observe both in the chiral topological semimetal CoSi and show that they arise through two different symmetry channels, each rendering phonon components with opposite crystal angular momenta inequivalent. Doubly degenerate E phonons exhibit a large ROA, with an approximately fourfold intensity contrast between the two cross-circular channels. The sign of this ROA reverses between the front and back {111} surfaces, while its strong suppression on {110} supports the assignment to the axial electric toroidal octupole. By contrast, triply degenerate T phonons show helicity-dependent frequency splittings, whose mode-dependent signs are reproduced by the calculated dispersion of branches with opposite crystal angular momenta, thus identifying structural chirality as their source. First-principles calculations yield a pronounced E-mode intensity asymmetry in the resonant regime, reproduce the mode-dependent signs of the T-mode splittings, and account for their magnitudes within approximately 40%. These results establish circularly polarized Raman scattering as a symmetry- and angular-momentum-resolved probe of chiral and axial multipolar symmetry in solids.

items.title: Revisiting Stress Analysis in a Three-Dimensional Elastic Hollow Sphere under Uniaxial Compression via the Inverse Laplace Transform Expressions within an Elastodynamic Framework
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The stress analysis of a three-dimensional elastic hollow sphere subjected to uniaxial compression is revisited, employing an elastodynamic framework. Through the application of the Laplace transform, the scalar and vector potentials of displacement are expanded, facilitating a detailed exploration of the system's mechanical behavior. The static solutions for displacement and stress distributions are derived in the long-time limit, which reveal key insights into the response of the elastic hollow sphere. Notably, on the inner surface, certain quantities exhibit a peak at the point where the angle between the compressive force and the point on the surface becomes perpendicular, indicating localized stress concentration. These findings provide a robust analytical approach for understanding and predicting the behavior of elastic hollow spheres under uniaxial loading, with implications for material science and structural engineering.

items.title: Separating perception from reasoning in vision-language models: a model-free render ceiling for crystal structures
authors: Can Polat, Mustafa Kurban, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often predict plausible structural labels from images without recovering the three-dimensional geometry behind them. End-to-end scores cannot tell whether an error comes from ambiguous views, lost visual information, or flawed reasoning. Multi-view 3D reconstruction faces its own trade-off: rigid symmetry priors erase genuine distortions, while unconstrained triangulation absorbs measurement outliers. We separate visual perception from structural reasoning through an inspectable 3D geometric intermediate. Its foundation is a model-free render ceiling: an exact reference for what calibrated, species-labeled projections determine, obtained by ruling out projective phantoms. Across a 1,950-structure census, every tested combination of four or five calibrated views uniquely determined the 3D sites from complete, species-labeled centroids. Against this reference, replacing images with exact text coordinates lowers the error rate of all 17 evaluated VLMs on crystals. The three frontier models gain 10.0-19.5 percentage points yet still miss 8.1-21.0% of cases. To recover geometry from imperfect observations, our symmetry-aware split reconstruction jointly estimates a symmetric base, coherent 3D physical displacements, and view-specific 2D corruption, adaptively selecting between atomic and collective distortion modes. Relative to Huber triangulation, it reduces coordinate error by 36.7% under Gaussian noise and 41.2% under corruption. Adaptive mode selection further cuts collective error up to 30.4% relative to atomic split across two external cohorts without sacrificing localized fidelity. Given reconstructed rather than Huber coordinates, downstream models improve. Geometric recovery thus becomes an explicit, testable foundation for structural understanding.

items.title: Fractional Bose-Einstein Condensate Dark Matter Cores: Numerical GPP Solutions and SPARC Rotation Curves
authors: Akila Labadi, Mohamed Benarous, Ahmed Hocine
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We investigate a fractional Bose Einstein condensate dark matter scenario in which an ultralight bosonic component forms a self gravitating core embedded in a predominantly cold dark matter halo. The stationary GPP system solved numerically beyond the TF approximation leads to energetically bound equilibrium configurations and good phenomenological fits to the selected rotation curves from 30 SPARC galaxies.

items.title: Dynamical, thermal, and ground-state multiparameter quantum metrology: Fundamental limits and their attainability in magnetometry
authors: Riccardo Pedroni, V\'ictor Izquierdo, Advay Burte, Paolo Abiuso, John Calsamiglia, Mart\'i Perarnau-Llobet
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We study the simultaneous estimation of parameters in Hamiltonians $H_{\vec{\theta}}=H_{\vec{\theta}}^P+H^C$, with $H^C$ a control term, for unitary dynamics, thermal equilibrium, and ground states. In each case, we bound the quantum Fisher information matrix by the covariance matrix of the parameter generators, extending single-parameter bounds and identifying the conditions for saturation. At thermal equilibrium, a complementary lower bound quantifies the cost of non-commutativity. For vector magnetometry, we derive asymptotically tight bounds and identify many-body control Hamiltonians that approach them in all three settings.

items.title: From Critical Zero Modes to Interior Dynamics in Holographic Superconductors
items.summary: -cross Abstract: We study how the critical behavior of holographic superconductors controls the interior geometry of charged black holes. Although the exterior condensate vanishes at criticality, the critical zero mode develops logarithmic oscillations near the Reissner--Nordstr\"om Cauchy horizon, rendering the interior critical limit nonuniform. We show that the transmitted critical-mode amplitude, together with local Cauchy-horizon quantities, fixes both the leading Einstein--Rosen collapse $\Delta z_{\rm ER}$ width and the phase $\Theta_J$ in the subsequent Josephson regime. If the condensate obeys $t\equiv1-T/T_c\propto\epsilon^{2r}$, then $\Delta z_{\rm ER}\propto t^{1/r}$ and $\Theta_J\propto t^{-1/r}$. This Josephson phase is transferred to the first Kasner epoch, producing oscillatory Kasner exponents and an accumulation law $t_n\sim n^{-r}$ for successive zeros of the scalar velocity. The critical zero mode fixes the leading collapse and phase coefficients, which are quantitatively confirmed by fully nonlinear solutions in both the ordinary and tricritical cases. At low temperature, the interior instead depends on the infrared completion of the zero-temperature geometry. Thus near-critical scaling is governed by critical-mode transmission, whereas the low-temperature behavior is controlled by the infrared endpoint.

items.title: CRAFT-{\epsilon}: A Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for the Static Relative Permittivity of Pure Organic Liquids
items.summary: -cross Abstract: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-{\epsilon} (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for {\epsilon}), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fr\"ohlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-{\epsilon} reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.

items.title: Surrogate Models for Stochastic Al-Cu Phase-Field Solidification
items.summary: -cross Abstract: Phase-field models resolve microstructural evolution during rapid alloy solidification, but their computational cost limits long trajectories, stochastic ensembles, and studies across process conditions. We compare a deterministic U-Net with conditional flow matching (Flow), conditional diffusion (EDM), and a variance-preserving denoising diffusion bridge (VP-DDBM) for two-dimensional Al-Cu solidification. Given the current phase, concentration, and prescribed temperature fields, each model predicts the subsequent state and is applied autoregressively. At two thermal gradients outside the training range, we compare surrogate rollouts spanning \(48{,}000\) phase-field Euler steps with five phase-field futures generated from a common restart at each gradient. With two network evaluations per transition, Flow achieves the lowest time-averaged fair continuous ranked probability score among the generative surrogates for mean phase, mean Cu concentration, interface length, and leading-tip position at both gradients. Flow also reproduces the cellular morphology and retains sharp solid--liquid interfaces. It generates a single future approximately \(107\times\) faster than the phase-field solver on the reported hardware, showing potential for faster process-condition screening and ensemble-based microstructure studies.

items.title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
authors: Makoto Takamoto, Chaitanya Sampara, Viktor Zaverkin, Daniel O\~noro-Rubio, Mathias Niepert
items.summary: -cross Abstract: It is well established that molecular substructures can contribute unequally to chemical and physical properties, with specific motifs or side chains often playing dominant roles. Fragment-based representations have therefore emerged as an effective strategy for incorporating chemically meaningful inductive biases, as exemplified by molecular fingerprints and fragment-based attention mechanisms. However, many existing fragmentation-based machine learning methods rely on predefined chemical rules, which may yield suboptimal fragmentation for previously unseen or chemically unfamiliar structures and often overlook the importance of multiscale molecular representations. To address these limitations, we formulate molecular fragmentation as a radius-constrained optimization problem inspired by the k-center formulation, where the number of clusters is not fixed a priori but emerges from the specified radius, and propose a geometry-based fragmentation method that partitions arbitrary molecular or material structures using largely geometric information, without relying on predefined chemical fragmentation rules. The method provides flexible control over fragment size, enabling the construction of multiscale fragment representations for scale-adaptive modeling. Building on this framework, we develop a geometric fragment-based attention mechanism that integrates multiscale structural information and incorporate it into a multimodal machine learning model combining p-SMILES representations with three-dimensional (3D) conformational information. Experiments on a benchmark polymer dataset show that incorporating 3D conformational information improves prediction accuracy for several properties over models based exclusively on p-SMILES representations. Explainable artificial intelligence analyses further provide insights into the physical relevance of the learned representations.

items.title: Crystal Orientation Enables Near-Unity Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Resonant Metasurfaces
authors: Chi Wang, Dmitrii Gromyko, Polina Pantiukhina, Lin Wu, and Kirill Koshelev
items.summary: Abstract Achieving near-unity nonlinear circular dichroism (CD) typically requires geometric symmetry breaking, making it challenging to combine helicity selectivity, resonant enhancement, and structural simplicity. We show that crystal orientation enables near-unity third-harmonic (TH) CD in highly symmetric resonant metasurfaces formed by a square lattice of circular holes in a cubic nonlinear material. Under circularly polarized excitation, strong near-field components of both helicities enabled by the rotational symmetry of the metasurface open two symmetry-allowed in-plane TH generation pathways. Crystal orientation controls their nonlinear coupling, selectively enabling destructive interference for one incident helicity. Our nonlinear temporal coupled-mode theory identifies the conditions for near-unity CD, reveals the distinct roles of pump and TH resonances, and explains the 4-fold and 8-fold crystal-orientation dependence. Across silicon, germanium, and diamond, we obtain resonantly enhanced TH CD exceeding 99% in the near-infrared, establishing crystal orientation as a design degree of freedom for nonlinear CD in highly symmetric metasurfaces.

items.title: Thermal-fluctuator-driven decoherence of an oscillator near-resonantly coupled to a two-level system
authors: Thomas J Antolin, Jonas Glatthard and Andrew D Armour
items.summary: Recent experiments on a range of engineered quantum systems have highlighted the important role of interacting two-level systems (TLSs) in modifying device properties and generating fluctuations. Focusing on the case of an oscillator coupled to a single near-resonant TLS, we explore how interactions between the TLS and lower-frequency thermally activated two-level fluctuators (TLFs) degrade the oscillator’s coherence. Depending on the strength of the couplings, a single TLF can give rise to coherence oscillations that appear alongside, or supplant, Rabi oscillations of the oscillator–TLS system. Bath-driven transitions in the TLF cause irreversible coherence decay at a rate that is highly sensitive to both the couplings and the transition rate. For an ensemble of TLFs, we identify and characterise the different regimes of non-exponential phase-averaging-driven coherence decay that the oscillator can display. Using numerical calculations, we examine the extent to which systems with just a few TLFs differ from the limit of a large (continuum) TLF ensemble. Our work provides a theoretical framework for understanding the interplay of coherent TLS interactions and TLF-induced dephasing in quantum devices such as superconducting and phononic resonators.

items.title: Double Cavity Exceptional-Point Enhanced Laser Cooling of Semiconductors
authors: Haonan Chang, 浩男 常, Feilong Song, 飞龙 宋, Jun Zhang and 俊 张
items.summary: Laser cooling of semiconductors requires a high external quantum efficiency for phonon-assisted upconversion while suppressing heat generated by background absorption and non-radiative relaxation. Nanophotonic resonances can strengthen the upconversion channel, but in a single-mode structure may also enhance parasitic pump heating. We introduce a two-cavity non-Hermitian architecture that separates preparation of a lower reservoir state from extraction of the phonon-promoted radiative state. A passive exceptional point, containing no optical gain, is placed in the output branch, where it reshapes the projected final-state optical response; all anti-Hermitian diagonal terms describe radiative leakage, internal absorption, or material decay. For a CdS parameter set, the four-mode calculation gives a 1.23 × 103 enhancement of upconverted photoluminescence relative to a single-mode control, while the pump-induced heat load rises by only 2.8 × 10–3%. The gain consists of a factor of 3.45 × 102 from the independent output resonance and a further factor of 3.56 from exceptional-point tuning.

items.title: Intelligent hydrovoltaic actuation with proactive ion regulation during solar desalination
items.summary: ABSTRACT Solar desalination offers a sustainable approach to freshwater generation, yet it is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation at evaporation interfaces. While common salt-rejecting strategies can mitigate macroscopic fouling, they fail to achieve real-time monitoring and active management of salts at the metastable stage. Local ion enrichment and associated pre-crystallization processes will degrade efficiency through increased mass-transfer resistance and vaporization enthalpy. Herein, we propose active salt management as a proactive system function and fabricate an intelligent dynamic evaporator (IDE) that integrates in-situ sensing, adaptive decision-making, and active regulation. The asymmetrically oxidized PPy/cotton is applied for real-time monitoring of ion concentration evolution within nanochannels via hydrovoltaic actuation. Coupled with deep learning algorithms, IDE dynamically correlates electrical outputs with salt enrichment states, enabling advanced intervention before critical accumulation. Dynamic solar tracking enables uniform interfacial evaporation and ion enrichment, elevating the stability of hydrovoltaic potential signals and the recognition precision (93.8%) of salt enrichment states. Overall, radiation-adaptive and self-cleaning IDE delivers an average daily freshwater production of 12.3 kg m −2 over 100 days. This work shifts salt management from static material design to intelligent adaptive control, providing a scalable framework for robust and sustainable water purification.

items.title: Van der Waals-modulated integration strategy unlocks scalable fabrication of high-density organic electronic and optoelectronic devices
items.summary: Abstract The advancement of organic electronics and optoelectronics fundamentally depends on the development of high-precision integration technologies. However, existing manufacturing approaches for organic semiconductors, particularly conventional photolithography and stencil lithography, are plagued by an intractable trade-off between integration density and device performance. Here we report a van der Waals (vdW)-modulated integration strategy that circumvents this long-standing bottleneck, enabling concurrent high-density and high-performance organic devices. By tailoring the surface chemistry of an ultrathin Parylene shadow mask, we precisely tune interfacial vdW interactions to orchestrate deterministic mask manipulation and high-fidelity patterning. Consequently, organic field-effect transistor (OFET) arrays achieve a device density of 2,500 transistors cm −2 with an average on-state current density of 1.20 μA μm −1 , among the highest reported for integrated organic electronics. Furthermore, this strategy is extended to monolithic OFET-organic light-emitting diode (OLED) integration, yielding efficient light-emitting transistor arrays. This work establishes an integration route that preserves the organic semiconductor interface while avoiding direct photolithographic contact with the active layer, opening a route toward large-scale, multifunctional organic integrated systems.

items.title: Spontaneous N-formylation of amines with carbon monoxide in irradiated water
items.summary: Abstract N -formyl amines are crucial synthetic intermediates, yet their production often relies on methods requiring precious metal catalysts, suffering from activation barrier or generating stoichiometric waste. Concurrently, the astrochemical origin of formamide, a prebiotic precursor, remains debated. Herein, we report a catalyst-free, radical-driven N -formylation strategy that addresses both challenges. Using only water as the solvent and X-ray or electron beam as the energy source, we achieve efficient coupling between carbon monoxide (CO) and amines under ambient conditions. Scaling up with a high-flux electron beam delivers a formamide production rate of 0.35 ± 0.01 mmol L −1 min −1 , with favorable techno-economic analysis indicating industrial potential. The reaction proceeds via the in-situ generation of key radicals ( • CHO from CO and • NR 1 R 2 from amines) generated by species (e aq − , • H, • OH) produced during water radiolysis, followed by spontaneous C–N coupling. This method exhibits superior C–N coupling reactivity for most derivatives including electron-donating and electron-withdrawing group and achieves a notable radiation-chemical yield up to 4.6 × 10 −7 mol J −1 . Beyond synthesis, this work may offer mechanistic insights into the related radiation-driven prebiotic pathway, demonstrating that radiolysis of simple mixtures (H 2 O, CO, NH 3 ) can efficiently yield formamide, thereby bridging green chemistry and astrochemistry.

items.title: Symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient CO2 electroreduction in strong acidic media
items.summary: Abstract Electrocatalytic CO 2 reduction reaction (CO 2 RR) in strong acidic media (pH ≤ 2) offers many unique advantages compared to alkaline electrolytes, but it still remains some significant challenges including the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), low selectivity and poor stability. Herein, we report that symmetry-breaking induced highly active Ni sites incorporated within ultrathin covalent organic polymer nanosheets (p-Ni 1/2 Pc), can simultaneously trigger interfacial hydrogen-bond network reconstruction for efficient acidic CO 2 RR. Direct visualization via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the presence of Ni vacancies and uncoordinated pyrrolic N, which collectively break the local symmetry around Ni sites. This asymmetry not only optimizes the electronic structure of Ni sites to kinetically favor CO 2 RR over HER, but more importantly, it reconfigures the interfacial hydrogen-bond network via uncoordinated pyrrolic N. The reconstructed hydrogen-bond network effectively restricts proton transfer, while symmetry breaking creates a CO 2 -enriched local microenvironment. Consequently, p-Ni 1/2 Pc catalyst exhibits a remarkable 97.5% CO Faraday efficiency (FE) and a maximum 402.9 mA cm −2 partial current density ( j CO ) in strong acidic electrolytes (pH = 1), while maintaining stable operation for 85 h without salt precipitation. This work highlights the critical role of symmetry-breaking in simultaneously engineering active sites and interfacial microenvironments for robust CO 2 RR in acidic media.

items.title: Hyperkagome antiferromagnetism in the iron garnet Almandine Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$
items.summary: Antiferromagnets on the hyperkagome lattice provide a three-dimensional route to strong magnetic frustration, but experimentally accessible realizations with well-established microscopic Hamiltonians remain scarce. Garnets are a broad family of materials in which magnetic ions can form two interpenetrating hyperkagome lattices, giving rise to spin glass, spin-liquid and hidden-order physics. Here we identify the iron aluminosilicate garnet almandine, Fe$_3$Al$_2$Si$_3$O$_{12}$, as a spin-$2$ hyperkagome antiferromagnet. Using density functional theory energy mapping, we determine a Heisenberg Hamiltonian for the high-spin Fe$^{2+}$ moments and find dominant nearest-neighbor antiferromagnetic exchange, as well as significant longer-range interactions. Classical Monte Carlo simulations of this Hamiltonian, combined with quantum-to-classical rescaling of the spin length, show a transition to antiferromagnetic order at $T_{\rm N}\approx9.8$K, in excellent agreement with specific heat experiments. The resulting non-collinear magnetic state is naturally described by magnetic toroidal octupolar order, which we connect to known results for the highly frustrated hyperkagome antiferromagnet gadolinium gallium garnet, Gd$_3$Ga$_5$O$_{12}$. We also calculate magnetic neutron diffraction amplitudes as well as static and dynamic structure factors using semiclassical dynamics, providing quantitative predictions for future neutron scattering experiments. Our results establish almandine as a chemically accessible realization of frustrated hyperkagome magnetism in the garnet family.

items.title: Double quantum dots as dynamical impurities in one-dimensional transport
items.summary: We study single-electron scattering in a tight-binding chain capacitively coupled to double quantum dots, which act as dynamical two-level-system impurities with electrically tunable level splittings. For a single impurity, we solve the scattering problem exactly and show Feshbach-like perfect elastic reflection, whose resonant condition distinguishes the initial two-level state. For several impurities in a strongly reflecting chain, transmission peaks at an intermediate mean level splitting. At small splittings, energy exchange with the impurities can weaken constructive interference between backscattered paths, consistent with the initial rise in transmission. As excitation channels close, virtual transitions can enhance reflection and drive transmission below its purely elastic value $T_0$. At larger splittings, these virtual processes weaken and transmission approaches $T_0$. We discuss how gate-controlled transmission measurements in quantum-dot arrays could test these predictions.

items.title: Electrostatic and magnetic control of the anomalous Josephson phase in ferromagnetic hybrid junctions
items.summary: We report phase-sensitive measurements of Josephson junctions formed in InAs nanowires with epitaxial ferromagnetic EuS and superconducting Al shells. Using a superconducting interferometer, we observe a continuous, hysteretic anomalous phase shift under axial magnetic-field sweeps. A remanent phase bias persists at zero applied field and depends on magnetic history. Electrostatic gating strongly modifies the magnitude of the phase response, revealing its sensitivity to the transverse electronic structure of the nanowire. Self-consistent electrostatic simulations show that the effective Rashba spin-orbit coupling follows the measured gate-dependent phase response, suggesting its central role in the electrostatic control of the anomalous Josephson phase.

items.title: Connectivity from activity in spiking neural networks
items.summary: We show that a wide range of recurrent neural network models obey a simple set of equations tying synaptic connectivity and single-cell response properties to neural correlations. Our modeling framework considers networks in a stationary, asynchronous state and contains a broad class of synaptic filters, spiking nonlinearities, and random-plus-structured connectivity. The resulting equations naturally decompose into contributions from monosynaptic, disynaptic, and higher order paths through the network. We leverage this decomposition to express the effective monosynaptic connection between two neurons in terms of experimentally measurable statistics of the activity, and in particular, their high-frequency correlations. In this way, we show that it is possible to recover network connectivity from neural activity.

items.title: Escaping Alignment: A Physical Trap Model of Best-of-N Jailbreaking
items.summary: Best-of-$N$ jailbreaking (BoN) bypasses safeguards of aligned models by drawing $N$ independent augmentations of an unsafe prompt and sampling $M$ completions of each. Previous works have shown that the attack success rate (ASR) seems to follow a power-law in $N$, which we challenge. The exponent drifts with $N$, and the reported exponential crossover is consistent with a finite-size effect of the adversarial dataset. Little work has been done to explore the entire two-budget ($N, M$) attack surface as well as its dependence on the generation temperature $T$. We introduce a simple barrier model where each prompt has a baseline safety level and each augmentation a random thermally activated barrier. Then five numbers, each backed by an interpretable safety mechanism, determine the entire ($N, M$) attack surface. They extrapolate predictions from $N \leq 100$ to $N = 10^4$, collapse five distinct models on the same scaling function and predict ASR at different temperatures from the one they were fitted at. The extrapolation holds under two automated judges and on held-out prompts.

items.title: Emptiness formation in quantum fluids: a hydrodynamic solution
items.summary: We develop an auxiliary-kernel method for constructing the hydrodynamic instantons that govern macroscopic emptiness formation in one-dimensional Galilean quantum fluids. The key step is to represent the equation of state by an auxiliary integral kernel inspired by the Bethe ansatz. For equations of state admitting such a representation, we reduce the imaginary-time hydrodynamic problem to a single integral equation. Its solution determines the full density and current profiles, the vacuum boundary, and the leading emptiness rate. Notably, the construction does not require microscopic integrability. For the Lieb--Liniger gas, we derive the previously conjectured integral equation for the leading rate and use a known elliptic solution to obtain explicit expressions for the rate and vacuum boundary. Direct hydrodynamic numerics support the predicted boundary. We also recover known instanton solutions for a family of polytropic fluids.

items.title: Foundation Tensor Networks Generalize Across Lattice Hamiltonians
items.summary: Neural quantum states and tensor networks have emerged as leading techniques for simulating quantum many-body systems. However, disordered systems remain extremely challenging in both frameworks as they require computation of the ground state for every realization of the disorder. Recently, neural quantum states have been used to construct foundation models that generate the ground state directly from the Hamiltonian. Still, they are hindered by the need to perform extensive sampling to estimate observables. To address these difficulties, we introduce the foundation tensor network (FTN), which uses a neural network to generate the tensor network representation of the ground-state wavefunction from the Hamiltonian. To accelerate training, we develop a technique, called \texttt{GridBP}, based on iterated one-dimensional belief propagation that reduces the cost of computing the energy expectation value to just two tensor contractions. We use FTNs to calculate the critical parameters of the glass transition in the quantum Edwards-Anderson model via finite-size scaling analysis. To facilitate rapid averaging, we use a moment-generating function to evaluate the order parameter, lowering the cost to a single tensor contraction. We obtain high-fidelity estimates for the critical parameters by averaging over 500,000 disorder realizations.

items.title: Bode-Fano Limits to Broadband Absorption by Small Particles
items.summary: Subwavelength nanostructures can absorb light efficiently at resonance, but causality and passivity fundamentally limit the bandwidth over which strong absorption can be maintained. We derive Bode-Fano-type limits for electrically small scatterers dominated by a single mode, assuming linear, time-invariant materials with rational dispersion. The derivation maps electromagnetic absorption onto an equivalent impedance-matching problem and provides a constructive method for synthesizing material dispersion that approaches these bounds while satisfying the same physical constraints. Our results guide the design of passive nanoparticles for broadband absorption, with potential applications in nanoscale light harvesting and dissipation.

items.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
items.summary: We seek an extension to Schrodinger's equation that incorporates the macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse phenomenon. We find that a suitable hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in a way that is consistent with Born's rule. Our theory posits that the Bohmian particle is guided by the wavefunction and, conversely, the wavefunction gradually localizes towards the particle's position. As long as the particle can visit any state, as in a typical microscopic system, the localization effect does not favor any particular quantum state and, on average, the usual Schrodinger-like time evolution results. However, when the wavefunction develops spatially well-separated lobes, as would happen during a macroscopic measurement, the Bohmian particle can remain trapped in one lobe, which causes the wavefunction to eventually localize. This proposed loss of ergodicity mechanism recasts one of the foundational postulate of quantum mechanics as a emergent feature and has important implications regarding the feasibility of large-scale quantum computing.

items.title: Failure of Mean-Field Critical Scaling and Two Distinct Dissipation Regimes in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_{7-δ}$
items.summary: Recently, superconductivity with an onset transition temperature ($T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}$) up to 96 K has been observed in the $\mathrm{La}_{2-x}\mathrm{Sm}_{1+x}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-δ}$ system under pressure, providing an attractive platform for investigating superconducting mechanisms in nickelates. Here, we systematically analyzed the critical scaling and vortex dynamics for the $\mathrm{La}_2\mathrm{Sm}\mathrm{Ni}_2\mathrm{O}_{7-δ}$ single crystal with $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{onset}}=92.5$ K under pressure. Within the Ullah--Dorsey framework, neither the two-dimensional nor three-dimensional scaling provides a good collapse near $T_{\mathrm{c}}^{\mathrm{MF}}$. This failure may be associated with the multiband composite order parameter of bilayer nickelates, in which pairing is mainly driven by antiferromagnetic exchange in the $d_{z^2}$ orbital, whereas the superfluid stiffness is mainly governed by the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. The two-step decrease in the logarithmic resistivity reveals two distinct dissipative regimes. The low-temperature regime is well described by the thermally assisted flux flow (TAFF) model, whereas the high-temperature regime cannot be explained by the vortex dynamics involved with the superconducting fluctuation. The crossover between the two regimes may be associated with the orbital-dependent evolution of vortex cores. These results suggest the significant role of the composite order parameter in critical fluctuations and vortex-motion dissipation in nickelates.

items.title: Krylov meets Fock: Complementary lenses on quantum dynamics
items.summary: Quantum dynamics in Krylov space can be represented by a particle hopping on a chain whose sites are the Krylov basis vectors. The goal of this work is to extend this idea to the Fock basis, which in turn allows the description of a generic dynamics in terms of a more general, possibly higher-dimensional lattice. This construction has been dubbed the Fock state lattice (FSL), since its sites are identified with Fock states. To analyze the dynamics on the FSL we introduce various measures of the spread of a state, comparing them among themselves and with their Krylov counterparts. We apply our analysis to two models of light-matter interaction studied in quantum optics: the multi-mode Jaynes-Cummings and the Dicke models. We find that, whenever the FSL is not a chain, the corresponding dynamics provides insights complementary to the Krylov space analysis and, in some instances, greater analytical control. For example, we obtain analytical results for the FSL spread measures of the Dicke model in the thermodynamic limit and determine that their scaling in time detects the superradiant phase transition.

items.title: Renormalization group study of critical behavior of $O(m)$ model with cubic anisotropy and extended defects: two-loop approximation
items.summary: We study the impact of quenched extended defects correlated in $ε_d$ dimensions and randomly distributed in the remaining $d - ε_d$ dimensions on the critical properties of a $d$-dimensional $O(m)$-symmetric system with cubic anisotropy. Exploiting the field-theoretic renormalization-group approach within the minimal subtraction scheme, we compute the two-loop renormalization-group functions. Applying resummation techniques to analyze the asymptotic series, we estimate the marginal values of $ε_d$ above which disorder becomes relevant for the physically important cases $m = 2$ and $m = 3$ in $d = 3$. We report numerical values of the critical exponents for the disorder-induced universality classes.

items.title: Energy spectrum of trions in semiconductors
items.summary: Energy levels of trions in a bulk semiconductor crystal are calculated by two different numerical methods. On the one hand, we construct the finite-element solution of the Schrödinger equation in the total angular momentum representation. On the other hand, we use the Gaussian expansion method (GEM), applied to each of the three Faddeev components of the wave function. The results for the total angular momenta $J=0$ and $J=1$ of the trion were obtained for a wide range of the hole-to-electron mass ratios covering most existing semiconductor compounds.
