The dependencies of the energies on the mass ratio for trions in a bulk crystal qualitatively agree with the results for a simplified model of a trion in a 1D quantum wire, for which the three-body energies can be calculated with arbitrary precision as well as easily approximated using Born-Oppenheimer potential-energy curves. A comparison of our results with data from other publicly available three-body codes as well as with the energies of well-known atomic counterparts, in particular, with vibrational energy levels of the molecular hydrogen ion, shows a good agreement and confirms the accuracy of the numerical data. We found that GEM significantly improves the precision of the obtained trion energies compared to previous calculations. Our calculations demonstrate that, for most semiconductor compounds, only one trion state with zero total angular momentum exists.

items.title: Structure-Property Correlation of Cr/Cu-MnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloys for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
items.summary: High-entropy alloys (HEAs), with their unique compositional-complexity and tunable surface chemistry, have emerged as promising electrocatalysts for energy conversion. The catalytic activity of HEA often arises from the interplay between the intrinsic activity of the individual elements and the synergistic effects generated at the interfaces. Even a single-element substitution in a multicomponent HEA can substantially alter the surface-chemistry and electrochemical kinetics of the active surface. Here we investigated the structure-property relationship of CrMnFeCoNi (HEA-Cr) and MnFeCoNiCu (HEA-Cu) HEAs by comparing the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity. Under the same experimental condition, HEA-Cu outperforms HEA-Cr towards both HER and OER. Substituting Cr with Cu significantly enhances the bifunctional activity, where HEA-Cu achieved a lower overpotential (538 mV) and Tafel slope (165 mVdec-1) when compared with HEA-Cr. Computational analysis corroborates these findings, showing that Cu substitution modulates the electronic-structure to provide favorable binding energies for reaction intermediates (H*, O*, OH*, and OOH*). Interestingly, unlike HER, recovered HEA-Cu after OER showed migration of Cu forming a Cu-rich outer layer shell with a multimetallic core. These findings demonstrate the potential of single-element substitution in HEAs as a strategy for designing high-performance, cost-effective catalysts for efficient water electrolysis.

items.title: Electric-field-controlled altermagnetic spin-momentum locking and ultrahigh tunneling magnetoresistance in Bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO
items.summary: Altermagnets offer a promising platform for spintronics by combining zero net magnetization with nonrelativistic spin splitting, yet efficient electrical manipulation of their spin-dependent transport remains challenging. Here, using first-principles calculations, we show that an out-of-plane electric field induces spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO, gives rise to a magneto-optical Kerr effect, and drives a semiconductor-to-metal transition at sufficiently high field magnitudes. Reversing the field direction switches the spin-momentum-locking pattern, which reverses the sign of the Kerr rotation angle as well as that of the longitudinal and transverse spin conductivities. Leveraging this electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking, we propose a dual-gate altermagnetic tunnel junction in which high- and low-resistance states are realized without reversing the Néel vector. The resistance switching originates from the matching and mismatching of spin-polarized conducting channels in momentum space, yielding a tunneling magnetoresistance ratio on the order of $10^{8}$. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for realizing electric-field-controlled spin-momentum locking in bilayer Cr$_{2}$SeO and developing all-electrically controlled altermagnetic spintronic devices.

items.title: Localization transition in a spin chain with an exact Fock-space tree
items.summary: Many-body localization is often pictured as Anderson localization on the graph of many-body configurations. Strongly correlated disorder and a dense net of loops, however, make this graph hard to analyze. We introduce a local disordered spin-1 chain in which a single domain wall explores an exact binary tree of configurations. Random fields create strongly correlated disorder on this tree, as in generic interacting systems, while the absence of loops keeps the problem tractable. We rigorously bound the spreading of the domain wall at strong disorder, and efficient numerics on exponentially large trees indicate a localization transition at finite disorder strength.

items.title: Quantum annealing through a first-order phase transition: Field theory approach
items.summary: Unlike second-order phase transitions, a first-order transition has a stage, in which a system is trapped in a metastable state. The decay of this state leads to abundant excitations over the ground state. We present a field theory for kinetics of defects emerging during quantum annealing computations. This theory predicts several power laws for the error generation rate during quantum annealing either through or near the first-order phase transition. Sharp changes between the power exponents are predicted for continuous parameter changes. Observation of this behavior would be a signature of first-order critical points and could help identify and avoid them for better computations. The driven Lipkin-Meshkov-Glick model (LMGm) serves as the minimal model of interacting Ising spins that demonstrates this behavior.

items.title: Searching for symmetric mass generation with staggered fermions in four dimensions
items.summary: We conduct numerical simulations to map out the phase diagram and critical behavior of a lattice Higgs model composed of two massless staggered fermion fields forming a doublet under a global $SU(2)$ and coupled to a scalar field in the adjoint representation of the group. The scalar action consists of a potential comprising quadratic and quartic terms and a scalar kinetic term. At fixed quartic coupling we explore a two-dimensional parameter space finding a massless symmetric phase at weak coupling and a massive symmetric phase (SMG phase) at strong coupling. An intermediate anti-ferromagnetic phase separates these two regimes. These results are consistent with leading order weak and strong coupling expansions. We find that the critical lines bounding the intermediate phase merge at a unique point where all fermion bilinear condensates vanish but fermion susceptibilities diverge as non-trivial powers of the lattice size. We conjecture that this merged point corresponds to a multicritical point and may describe a phase consisting of a condensate of certain topological defects.

items.title: Variational and geometric time-dependent density-functional theory of electronic systems
items.summary: A central problem in time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is to construct a time-dependent many-electron wave function that reproduces a prescribed time-dependent electron density. This problem admits a natural geometric interpretation, which in turn leads to at least two distinct formulations of TDDFT. The first is the usual variational formulation of TDDFT, in which the density constraint is enforced with a real-valued local potential. The second is geometric TDDFT, introduced in recent works, in which the same density constraint is enforced with an imaginary local potential, or equivalently with a Hermitian nonlocal potential. In this work, we develop this unified viewpoint for continuous electronic systems and systematically compare the two formulations. We formulate the corresponding time-dependent Kohn-Sham schemes and derive a number of exact conditions for geometric TDDFT, including conditions associated with causality, time-reversal symmetry, uniform-coordinate scaling, translational invariance, energy and momentum equations of motion, one-electron self-interaction, and the adiabatic limit. The paper also contains a mathematical section where we provide a fully rigorous justification of some parts of the text. We particularly discuss the mathematical properties of two operators underlying the two formulations of TDDFT and establish sufficient conditions for their invertibility. We explain the functional-analytic subtleties underlying the geometric interpretation of TDDFT and the two formulations of TDDFT. This unified perspective clarifies the mathematical and conceptual relation between variational and geometric TDDFT and provides a foundation for the development of approximations within geometric TDDFT.

items.title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
items.summary: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $Ω(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

items.title: Atomistic Insights into the All-Optical Switching of GdCo Alloys with Minimal Gd Concentration
items.summary: Single-pulse all-optical helicity-independent switching (AO-HIS) is most commonly observed in Gd-based ferrimagnets near magnetization compensation. Recent experiments, however, demonstrated switching in Pt/Co/Pt-based heterostructures containing only a small amount of Gd at a Co/Pt interface. Here, we use atomistic spin-dynamics simulations to test an effective interfacial GdCo-alloy picture and to determine how species-dependent spin-bath coupling controls the minimum Gd concentration required for reversal. We compare a three-monolayer Co film with Gd confined to the surface layer and a three-dimensional uniformly alloyed GdCo model. Within the present uniform-heating model, robust transient toggle-like reversal is obtained far from compensation when the Gd coupling to the thermal bath is substantially weaker than that of Co; for λCo = 0.02 and λCo = 0.001, reversal occurs down to 1.5 at. % total Gd for selected pulse parameters. Increasing the Gd content accelerates reversal, consistent with the interpretation of Gd as an angular-momentum reservoir, whereas dilute interfacial Gd produces slower and more stochastic dynamics. These results show that compensation is not a fundamental requirement for ultrafast AO-HIS and identify the effective Gd spin-bath coupling as a key control parameter. Quantitative comparison with experiment will require explicit optical absorption, stack-dependent heat flow, dipolar fields, and a stable-final-state switching criterion.

items.title: Self-attention is a Dyson equation for many-body machine learning
items.summary: Why does symmetric sum-pooling (DeepSets) predict ground-state potentials to sub-meV accuracy, yet fail for correlated wavefunctions and excited states? Sum-pooling is a mean-field (Hartree) model: its $O(1/N)$ off-diagonal Jacobian suffices for nearsighted ground-state energies, but erases nonlocal two-body correlations. We show that self-attention is a real-space Dyson iteration whose Boltzmann (softmax) kernel acts as a two-body self-energy. Because physical Hamiltonians act pairwise, Löwdin's 2-RDM theorem and the Galitskii--Migdal relation guarantee that iterating a two-body propagator captures the full energetics of correlated matter. When fitting a fractal backflow determinant, DeepSets blurs the nodal surface onto a mean-field envelope, whereas self-attention recovers the fractal attractor. Seen through this lens, the unreasonable effectiveness of attention is not an accident; in a universe built from pairwise interactions, two-body attention is all you need.

items.title: Quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures: Comparison between dispersively and directly coupled superconducting qubits
items.summary: The Rabi frequency of a two-level system is directly proportional to the electric field amplitude being incident on this system. Taking advantage of this relationship, it is possible to use two-level systems as quantitative sensors of electric fields. Here, we apply this concept to superconducting qubits and use them for quantitative measurement of microwave power at millikelvin temperatures. Our superconducting circuit design includes three transmon qubits directly coupled to the central microwave feedline and three transmon qubits coupled dispersively via readout resonators to the feedline. We compare both coupling schemes to assess their reliability for microwave power sensing. Further, we describe the modeling behind each power-sensing method, including an uncertainty estimation based upon repeated measurements. By combining dispersively coupled and directly coupled qubits on the same device, we are able to explore different power ranges: from $-155\;$dBm to $-130\;$dBm for the directly coupled qubits and from $-95\;$dBm to $-55\;$dBm for the dispersively coupled qubits. When determining the microwave-line attenuation for a frequency of $6.0\;$GHz from room temperature to the millikelvin stage of the cryostat, we obtain best estimates and uncertainties for the directly coupled transmons of $(74.7\pm 0.2) \;$dB and for the dispersively coupled transmons of $(75.4\pm 6.8) \;$dB. The larger uncertainty of the dispersively coupled qubit measurements indicates that these qubits are less reliable for power sensing than the directly coupled qubits, most likely, due to the additional coupling resonator, whose transfer function is difficult to estimate accurately. Our results constitute the first step towards validation of qubit power sensing in dilution fridges, leading towards traceability for cryogenic microwave measurements.

items.title: Continuous superradiant lasing on a narrow optical transition
items.summary: Lasers with ultrastable frequency are at the foundation of optical clocks, which enable precision tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy at the centimetre scale. Such lasers inherit their frequency stability from the length stability of a sophisticated optical resonator, which is hard to maintain outside a well-controlled laboratory environment and limited by thermal and technical noise. Superradiant lasers promise to overcome these limitations by storing their coherence in the atoms making up the laser's gain medium. Superradiant lasing has been demonstrated on narrow optical atomic transitions with pulsed and quasi-continuous operation. However, atom loss has prevented truly continuous operation, which severely limits their suitability for clocks. Here we demonstrate a superradiant laser on a narrow optical transition in $^{88}$Sr that operates truly continuously. We sustain emission for more than eight hours and measure a linewidth of 320(40) Hz, more than 20 times below the natural linewidth. The emission frequency remains anchored to the atomic transition, making the laser itself an atomic frequency reference. Our results provide a route towards a laser that reaches short-term frequency stability comparable to that of the best resonator-stabilized lasers. Furthermore, truly continuous operation gives us access to physics beyond the transient regime, enabling the exploration of robust nonequilibrium steady states and sustained coherent collective dynamics.

items.title: Accessing Electrode Edges: Upright Mounting for Site-Specific Cryogenic Atom Probe Tomography of Lithium-Ion Batteries
items.summary: Cryogenic atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) is increasingly being used to map the three-dimensional distribution of highly reactive species in heterogeneous materials, including those found in battery systems. However, site-specific preparation of localised features and liquid-solid interfaces remains challenging, particularly when regions of interest (ROIs) are concentrated along electrode edges that are difficult to access using conventional mounting geometries. Here, we present a cryo-APT workflow incorporating an upright-mounting procedure that enables targeted specimen preparation of localised regions using plasma focused ion beam (PFIB) microscopy and milling under cryogenic conditions. We first demonstrate the approach using an electrolyte-wetted graphite electrode, successfully preparing and analysing a specimen containing both an edge-localised electrolyte deposit and the underlying graphite and Cu current collector. We then apply the workflow to a cycled graphite electrode, targeting Li dendrites concentrated around the electrode perimeter and successfully preparing and analysing the targeted Li-rich region. Beyond battery systems, this approach offers potential for site-specific cryo-APT of edge-localised features across a broader range of material systems, where conventional specimen preparation geometries may limit access to ROIs.

items.title: Vortex states in submicron titanomagnetite particles
items.summary: Numerical simulation is used to study the magnetic properties of spheroidal titanomagnetite particles Fe(3-x)TixO4 (0.4 < x < 0.6) with semi-axes ratio ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 and transverse diameters D = 100 - 480 nm. It is shown that various vortex micromagnetic states can emerge in the titanomagnetite particles depending on the titanium concentration, aspect ratio and particle diameter. The single-domain particle diameters are determined using the energy diagrams for stationary uniform and vortex states. The remanent magnetization of dilute assemblies of titanomagnetite particles with varying titanium content are calculated as a function of the transverse particle diameter D. It is demonstrated that for submicron-sized titanomagnetite particles, D ~ 500 nm, the normalized remanent magnetization of the assembly reaches very low values, M/Ms < 0.01, where Ms is the saturation magnetization of the particles.

items.title: A Free Energy Approach to Modelling Disordered Hyperuniform Patterns
items.summary: We present a free-energy-based approach for modelling disordered hyperuniform patterns. Specifically, we devise a phase-field crystal model with a correlation kernel that simultaneously selects for a continuous range of degenerate wave modes. At small wave vectors, we construct the correlation function by inverting the Ornstein-Zernike relation to approximate the structure factor of a hyperuniform pattern. Our model demonstrates a crossover between liquid, crystalline, quasicrystalline, and long-lived disordered states depending on the specified free energy parameter and driving force. We show that, for a fixed driving force, the specific structures and wave vectors selected by the density field can be controlled by modulating the width of the correlation kernel. Furthermore, we show that the scaling of the low-wave-vector region of the correlation function can accurately reproduce a specified hyperuniform exponent, independently of the structural properties at larger wave numbers. Our results establish a free-energy-based framework for describing disordered hyperuniform states, demonstrating and enabling independent control over structural selection and long-wavelength density correlations.

items.title: Quantum adiabatic and diabatic optimization: A Hilbert space engineering strategy with Rydberg arrays
items.summary: Neutral-atom arrays provide a versatile platform for encoding combinatorial optimization problems with arbitrary graph connectivity [Nguyen et al., PRX Quantum 4, 010316 (2023)]. Although the dynamics of individual encoding gadgets has been studied [Bombieri et al., PRX Quantum 6, 020306 (2025)], understanding annealing bottlenecks in larger networks remains challenging. We investigate how engineering the Hilbert-space geometry controls quantum annealing in a family of blockaded-chain models motivated by these encodings. While boundary terms encode the target maximum independent set problem, the bulk geometry induces an auxiliary optimization problem associated with independent sets of cliques. Spectrally, the energetics of the quantum system can be approximated by physically derived clique weights. When the target problem and the auxiliary problems are consistent, the low-energy modes lie predominantly within the target subspace. This spectral structure motivates a diabatic annealing strategy that exploits target-compatible excited states, as tested on the diamond-chain graph family. These results provide a framework for predicting annealing bottlenecks, and demonstrate Hilbert-space engineering as a strategy for improving neutral-atom quantum optimization protocols.

items.title: Experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity in discrete time crystals
items.summary: Discrete time crystals (DTCs) are almost always analyzed under the Born-Markov approximation, in which the environment is memoryless. We show that a reservoir with a finite correlation time $τ_m$ leaves an exact and strikingly simple imprint on the stroboscopic dynamics of DTCs, which can be used as an experimentally relevant witness for non-Markovianity. By analyzing a post-Markovian master equation we prove that the Floquet spectrum splits into the ordinary Markovian spectrum plus a replica of the purely unitary Floquet spectrum, uniformly contracted by $e^{-T/τ_m}$, where $T$ is the drive period. Consequently, the DTC signal decay rate becomes independent of any system parameter once $τ_m$ exceeds the Markovian lifetime of the DTC. The measured decay, and in particular its insensitivity to tunable system parameters, thus becomes a direct read-out of the reservoir correlation time. Below this threshold the dynamics is already non-Markovian, but the memory remains hidden in the decay. We confirm this in two structurally unrelated DTCs, a collective long-range model with incoherent pumping and a disorder-free Ising chain with dephasing, where a single estimator recovers $τ_m$. The time crystal thereby witnesses the non-Markovianity of its own environment.

items.title: Storage and Learning phase transitions in the Random-Features Hopfield Model
items.summary: The Hopfield model is a paradigmatic model of neural networks that has been analyzed for many decades in the statistical physics, neuroscience, and machine learning communities. Inspired by the manifold hypothesis in machine learning, we propose and investigate a generalization of the standard setting that we name Random-Features Hopfield Model. Here $P$ binary patterns of length $N$ are generated by applying to Gaussian vectors sampled in a latent space of dimension $D$ a random projection followed by a non-linearity. Using the replica method from statistical physics, we derive the phase diagram of the model in the limit $P,N,D\to\infty$ with fixed ratios $α=P/N$ and $α_D=D/N$. Besides the usual retrieval phase, where the patterns can be dynamically recovered from some initial corruption, we uncover a new phase where the features characterizing the projection can be recovered instead. We call this phenomena the learning phase transition, as the features are not explicitly given to the model but rather are inferred from the patterns in an unsupervised fashion.

items.title: Spectral Softening and the Structural Breakdown of Thermodynamic Equilibrium
items.summary: Reversible quasistatic thermodynamics requires normalizable instantaneous equilibrium states and dynamics allowing their attainment or tracking. We examine these requirements in a driven two-dimensional quadratic Hamiltonian with an angular-momentum coupling and a spatially uniform momentum shift $p_c(t)$, representable by a time-dependent vector potential. Its undriven part has normal-mode frequencies $ω_\pm=ω_1\pmω_2$ and the Fock--Darwin structure of a charged oscillator in a perpendicular magnetic field. At the exact soft-mode endpoint $ω_-=0$, confinement is lost in one normal-mode sector. For every strictly positive $ω_-$, the canonical Gibbs state remains normalizable; only at the endpoint does the canonical trace cease to be finite. In the quasi-soft regime, where $ω_-\to0^+$, exact adjacent-level couplings yield a dimensionless adiabatic parameter proportional to $|\dot p_c|/ω_-^2$. The standard adiabatic criterion requires this parameter to remain much smaller than unity. At a fixed occupation and a fixed nonzero driving rate, however small, this parameter grows without bound as $ω_-\to0^+$, eventually violating this criterion. In an open system, thermal tracking additionally depends on relaxation relative to the driving timescale. An explicit linear system--bath coupling illustrates why the relaxation rate cannot be inferred from the soft-mode spacing alone. Finally, the thermal Wigner function and its classical limit show that phase-space confinement is lost in both descriptions at the soft-mode endpoint. Taken together, our results show that canonical equilibrium is lost at $ω_-=0$. For $ω_->0$, the Gibbs state exists, while the ability to track it dynamically depends on the driving and dissipation.

items.title: Spin-current rectifier and linear magnon Edelstein effect in $p$-wave antialtermagnets
items.summary: We show that $p$-wave magnetic insulators efficiently generate magnetization via a linear thermal magnon Edelstein effect. Furthermore, they can generate perfectly nonreciprocal spin currents through a purely even-order nonlinear response. This makes them promising candidates for spin-current rectification. More generally, we find that odd-parity-wave magnets with coplanar ground states host magnons with zero magnetic moment in the plane. Instead the magnons carry a colinear, out-of-plane magnetic moment, placing coplanar odd-parity-wave magnets within the class of antialtermagnets. We establish these general results using symmetry arguments and demonstrate them explicitly for a two-dimensional model with a coplanar ground state containing the minimal number of sublattices, inspired by the ground state of CeNiAsO. Our conclusions hold both in the absence and in the presence of spin-orbit coupling.

items.title: PLECTA: Overlap-aware instance segmentation of dense strand networks from binary masks
items.summary: Many materials and tissues, including carbon-nanotube sheets, collagen and paper, comprise overlapping strands whose arrangement influences their effective properties. Measuring this geometry from micrographs requires individual strands to be traced through crossings and signal gaps, which merge distinct strands or split one strand into disconnected fragments. We present PLECTA (from Latin plecta, a braid), a deterministic method that segments individual strands using only a binary image whose foreground pixels mark strand centrelines. At each junction, PLECTA selects which strand segments continue into one another while allowing segments to terminate. It formulates this decision as an exact maximum-weight partial-matching problem, with an explicit penalty for unpaired segments and no restriction on the number of segments entering a junction. The output permits crossing pixels to belong to multiple strands. On synthetic scenes, PLECTA resolved strand identities more accurately than three released alternatives at every density tested. The same ranking held on an independently published generator run at its own settings. A separate stage uses the corresponding greyscale micrograph to estimate which strand lies on top at each crossing. The complete workflow is demonstrated on scanning electron micrographs of carbon nanotube sheets, from raw images to individual strand instances with estimated crossing order, without manual annotations for training or as pipeline inputs.

items.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
items.summary: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight. Equilibrium temperatures are given for both a theoretical lumped body and for a slab body, in which thermal conduction is considered. All data are limited to the solid state, up to a material-specific upper temperature limit. Currently, the database applies to extraterrestrial (AM0) sunlight only. A graphical App is also provided for exploring and visualizing the database.

items.title: Ultra-small-angle graphene twistronics with monolayer spacers: From interlayer hybridisation and moiré effects to high-temperature magnetotransport oscillations
items.summary: Based on the analysis of moiré superlattice characteristics and interlayer hybridisation in small-angle twisted graphene multilayers with a monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) spacer, we predict spectral features and quantum transport effects in these systems. Here, we consider both a twisted bilayer and double bilayers with a spacer, discuss double bilayers in two stacking orders - with and without inversion symmetry - and also compare the results obtained with self-consistent Hartree calculations with and without in-plane periodic charge distribution, offering computationally efficient models for these graphene/hBN/graphene moiré systems. We note parametric intervals where the appearance of minibands can be enhanced by tuning with an out-of-plane displacement field, and identify the miniband edges and van Hove singularities across a broad range of densities and displacement fields. These system host Lifshitz transitions at which the Fermi lines form a network across moiré Brillouin zones, and to which Brown-Zak oscillations converge at low magnetic field and elevated temperatures. We analyse interlayer hybridisation across the same parameter space, discuss how hybridisation affects in-plane magneto-transport in ultra-high-mobility structures, and predict that semiclassical magneto-oscillations of interlayer hybridisation can lead to 1/B-periodic quantum oscillations of resistivity persistent to high temperature.

items.title: Spatial Cost of Recovering a Fusion Qubit in a Critical Spin Chain
items.summary: Four Kramers--Wannier defects in a critical Ising chain encode a qubit over a common pure bulk ground state in a fixed symmetry sector. We determine the spatial cost of recovering it from arbitrary preselected physical spins, allowing unrestricted joint decoding. In the infinite-chain limit followed by increasing defect separation, vanishing error under linear spin budgets requires filling the central gap and at least one outer gap in density. The shorter three-defect interval attains the sharp leading cost through single-spin measurements and classical feedforward. Near-minimal successful supports approach a shortest such span in density. Below this cost, a benchmark finite-ring budget window separates entanglement-breaking connected access from entanglement-preserving single-gap perforations. For a selected two-component family, single-spin Pauli measurements and a one-way classical message yield a scale-stable Bell recovery advantage. The output channel supports positive transmission rates over independently prepared blocks, with coding performed at fixed geometry before the ordered spatial limits. Collective fusion records in discarded spins bound recovery from above, while conjugate retained records certify coherence. Finite-ring examples show that Bell-optimal one-qubit compression can reduce the full output's capacity. On two uncoupled chains with independent bulk states, a repetition embedding raises the leading cost. A matched interacting Ashkin--Teller ladder retains finite-ring geometric separation at every finite nonnegative coupling. The results distinguish useful quantum access from vanishing-error recovery and connect both to critical many-body statistics.

items.title: AI-Enabled Qubit Loss Detection and Replenishment Strategy for Atom Array Quantum Computing
items.summary: Qubit loss is a major source of error in atom-array quantum computing and invalidates the algebraic structure of the standard stabilizer formalism for quantum error-correcting codes. On the one hand, it complicates decoding; on the other hand, it introduces tochastic flicker patterns in stabilizers as a hallmark of qubit loss. Here, we develop an artificial-intelligence-enabled decoder based on a spatiotemporal graph neural network (STGNN) architecture to extract spatial and temporal correlations from syndrome histories. Our decoder performs a dual-head task, simultaneously correcting standard Pauli errors and identifying the locations of qubit loss. Our decoder achieves significantly higher logical accuracy than both the traditional minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) algorithm and even delayed-erasure MWPM decoders that use qubit-loss information from the final round as input. Furthermore, we integrate the decoder into a sliding-window framework for dynamic qubit replenishment. We emphasize that our approach does not involve any additional physical measurements beyond stabilizer measurements, and detects qubit loss and determines its replacement strategy through a purely software-based AI policy. We demonstrate that our approach bounds the accumulation of lost qubits and fully restores the fault-tolerant scaling behavior. For realistic near-term error rates, this work provides a robust and scalable framework for correcting qubit-loss errors, paving the way for more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation.

items.title: Reframing the coupling force of adaptive resolution simulation in terms of the Liouville-type hierarchy for open systems
items.summary: In this work, we present a novel perspective on the coupling force employed to compensate the interface artifacts prevalent in adaptive resolution simulations (AdResS) of open many-particle systems. We show that a substantial part of this "thermodynamic force" can be framed in terms of the theoretical model of the Liouville-type hierarchy for open systems. The correspondence is made explicit for the case of a simple atomistic fluid, for which a one-dimensional integral expression is derived. This enables the analysis for dependencies of the thermodynamic force on important simulation parameters, which is taken to inspire both simplifications for the numerical calculation of the thermodynamic force and new criteria for its validation that are adequate to the interfacial nature of the problem. The theoretical claims are then verified in a simulation study of the atomistic supercritical Lennard-Jones fluid at different thermodynamic states.

items.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
items.summary: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points. We then demonstrate the transferability of our model to bismuth properties not included in our training data through determination of the rhombohedral phase phonon density of states and energetic ordering of additional bismuth solid phases. Finally, we have validated our topological predictions through comparison to DFT results for the optimized bilayer geometries, a band inversion order parameter, and the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant as a function of monolayer unit cell length. Our efforts establish DFTB as a rigorous approach for topological characterization while yielding approximately three orders of magnitude increase in computational efficiency relative to DFT. Our model can thus serve as a computational tool for topological materials discovery by enabling large-scale computational screening to address the potentially complex relationship between physical-chemical properties and the resulting topological classification.

items.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
items.summary: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}. Despite the drastic approximation we reveal the boson QSE scheme provides practically useful accuracy in the ground state energy. Our results support its applicability to realistic quasi-two- and three-dimensional electronic systems.

items.title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
items.summary: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Martínez {\it et al.} [Phys. Rev. Res. {\bf 8}, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

items.title: Moiré Excitons in a Chern Ferromagnet
items.summary: Recent experiments have established excitonic optical resonances as powerful probes and control knobs of moiré Chern ferromagnets. However, the microscopic nature of excitons formed on such interaction-driven, time-reversal-symmetry-broken ground states remains largely unexplored. In this paper, using a Gutzwiller plus Bethe-Salpeter equation framework, we investigate twisted bilayer MoTe2 at hole filling ν_h=1 and identify two near-infrared Chern-ferromagnet excitons (CFEs) selectively coupled to opposite circular polarizations. Strong electron-hole interactions markedly enhance their energy separation and drive a pronounced momentum-space reconstruction of the emergent X- state, beyond the quasiparticle-transition picture. We further find that this reconstruction enhances the interlayer electron-hole character of X-, giving rise to a giant quadratic Stark response. These findings reveal the nontrivial interplay between electron-electron correlations and electron-hole interactions underlying CFE formation, providing optical fingerprints of moiré Chern-ferromagnetic order and a microscopic basis for its optical control.

items.title: Torsional Hall Viscosity of Massive Chern Insulators: Finite Temperature and Chemical Potential
items.summary: We study the torsional Hall viscosity $ζ_{\rm H}$ of Chern insulators at finite temperature and chemical potential. Our analysis considers the massive Dirac fermion and two deformations: a constant out-of-plane magnetic field and a momentum-dependent mass described by the single-block Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang (BHZ) Hamiltonian. For the massive Dirac theory, we show that temperature and chemical potential lead to UV-finite corrections and that a chemical potential outside the bulk gap modifies $ζ_{\rm H}$ even at zero temperature. In a constant magnetic field, the response of massive Dirac fermions is dictated by the relativistic Landau-level spectrum, leading to a plateau structure at zero temperature that is smoothed at finite temperature. The jumps are proportional to the Dirac mass and inversely proportional to the squared magnetic length and the newly occupied Landau-level energy. Finally, we present a detailed study of the correction to $ζ_{\rm H}$ in the single-block BHZ continuum model due to temperature and chemical potential. For parameters relevant to (Hg,Mn)Te quantum wells, the magnitude of the jump across a mass domain wall retains its vacuum enhancement due to the BHZ deformation as long as the chemical potential lies sufficiently deep inside the gap compared with the thermal energy. Our results extend the theory of torsional Hall viscosity to experimentally relevant conditions and may facilitate its future detection.

items.title: Multi-Fidelity Machine Learning for Predicting Startup Stress Growth and Strain Hardening in Wormlike Micellar Solutions
items.summary: Wormlike micellar solutions exhibit formulation-dependent nonlinear startup responses, including stress overshoot, undershoot, and strain hardening, making prediction across compositions and shear rates challenging. We developed a multi-fidelity machine-learning framework to predict stress-growth curves in cetylpyridinium chloride (CPyCl)-based wormlike micelles from sparse experimental measurements. The framework combines a low-fidelity analytical model describing the overall startup response with high-fidelity experimental data capturing formulation-specific nonlinear features. This approach addresses the limited and uneven coverage of salt chemistry, concentration, and shear rate without relying solely on data-intensive neural-network training. The trained model predicts complete stress-growth responses at untested shear rates and enables extraction of strain-hardening characteristics from interpolated curves. By augmenting sparse rheological measurements, the framework provides a basis for exploring relationships among formulation variables, linear viscoelastic properties, and nonlinear startup behavior, while supporting more efficient characterization of wormlike micellar solutions.

items.title: jahn-teller-dynamics: Python package to determine vibronic interaction demonstrated on molecules and trigonal defect qubits
items.summary: Trigonal solid-state defects are often subjects of spontaneous symmetry breaking driven by the $E\otimes e$ Jahn-Teller effect, reflecting strong electron-phonon coupling. These systems, particularly paramagnetic defect qubits in solids are central for quantum technology applications, where accurate knowledge of their fine-structure parameters - shaped by the complex interplay of spin-orbit and electron-phonon interactions - is essential. We introduce the $\mathtt{jahn {\text -} teller {\text -} dynamics}$ package, a Python code that implements the first-principles approach of [Phys. Rev. X 8, 021063 (2018)] to accurately compute the spin-orbit-phonon entanglement in trigonal defects utilizing the output from density functional theory calculations (DFT) to predict fine-structure parameters of zero-phonon lines (ZPLs), including Zeeman shifts under external magnetic fields. We demonstrate its capabilities on negatively charged Group-IV-vacancy (G4V) defects in diamond: SiV$^-$, GeV$^-$, SnV$^-$, PbV$^-$ and the neutral N$_3$V$^0$ defect in diamond, and the CH$_3$O$^0$ methoxy radical. Additionally, we implement a generic electron-phonon code that is capable entangling an arbitrary amount of (i) vibration modes and (ii) electronic levels by (iii) arbitrarily high order of vibronic interaction terms. Exemplarily, we demonstrate the Jahn-Teller multimode problem on the CH$_3$O$^0$ methoxy radical and the Pseudo Jahn-Teller case on the $C_4H_4^+$ butatrien cation.

items.title: Dephasing-Induced Universal Spin Fluctuations in a Localized Hubbard Chain
items.summary: Decoherence usually washes out quantum effects. We show that in a disordered chain it can instead switch on universal fluctuations. In the infinite-$U$ Hubbard chain, particles cannot pass one another, so the spin crossing a cut is fixed by the number of particles that cross. Without an environment, disorder localizes the charge and the spin fluctuations stop growing. Dephasing restores diffusion: the spin width grows again as $t^{1/8}$, fastest at an intermediate dephasing rate, and the spin distribution takes the same non-Gaussian M-Wright form as in the clean chain.

items.title: First-principles calculation of electron-phonon spectral functions for defects using phonon interpolation
items.summary: Accurate optical lineshapes of point defects require dense sampling of lattice vibrations, which is challenging for direct first-principles supercell calculations. We introduce a phonon-interpolation method for calculating Huang-Rhys spectral densities and optical lineshapes within the harmonic Franck-Condon framework. By exploiting the spatial localization of transition-induced forces, the method obtains electron-phonon coupling from a tractable defect supercell and samples its vibrational response on dense reciprocal-space grids, avoiding explicit construction and diagonalization of large hypercell dynamical matrices. Applied to the negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy center in diamond, the method resolves low-energy acoustic contributions, the dominant phonon sideband structure, and finer optical-phonon features. The resulting temperature-dependent photoluminescence lineshapes reproduce the main features of experimental spectra after accounting for additional broadening. The approach offers an efficient route to high-resolution defect spectra and can, in principle, complement embedding and machine-learning methods.

items.title: Interaction Landscapes of Structurally Distorted Toroidal Classical Spin Textures
items.summary: We develop a classical discrete magnetostatic model of localized magnetic moments arranged in a toroidal texture, where the moments are represented by static current loops and study the behavior of the magnetic dipole-dipole interaction under several types of structural deformations. The purpose is to disentangle effects due to geometric and magnetic deformations, including elliptical, lopsided, alternating, and tilted configurations. In particular, we investigate how distortions modify the toroidal moment and the interaction energy between pairs of toroidal structures. The resulting interaction landscapes exhibit characteristic symmetry patterns and anisotropies that are highly sensitive to the underlying deformation. As a separate proof-of-concept comparison, first-principles calculations on a molecular spin-toroidal system reveal qualitatively similar orientation-dependent behavior. The calculated interaction is microscopically the conventional pairwise magnetic dipole-dipole interaction between localized moments arranged in a spin-toroidal texture; the toroidal moment characterizes the collective texture and should not be interpreted as introducing an additional elementary interaction term. Our results provide a platform for exploring orientation-dependent interactions of spin-toroidal textures in molecular magnets and related nanoscale magnetic systems that are essential to understand the role of toroidal order.

items.title: Quantum sensing of weak ferromagnetism in a phase-separated Mn-doped CaFe$_3$O$_5$
items.summary: Doping of transition metal oxides such as CaFe$_3$O$_5$ offers a controlled way to tune the interplay of charge, spin, and lattice degrees of freedom, yet local-probe studies remain difficult because strong correlations and dynamic charge-spin fluctuations obscure fine spectroscopic features in powder samples. Here, we employ quantum magnetometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in nanodiamonds impressed into an Mn-doped CaFe$_3$O$_5$ powder pellet to probe static and dynamic magnetic fields across the weak ferromagnetic transition. The splitting and broadening of the optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) spectra exhibit an order-parameter-like increase by $\sim 15 ~{\rm MHz}$ upon cooling below the critical temperature, $T_{\rm c}$. Concomitantly, the spin-lattice relaxation rate, $1/T_1$, exhibits a pronounced enhancement at $T_\mathrm{c}$, increasing approximately fivefold from its high-temperature value. Moreover, detailed lineshape fits of ODMR spectra together with the stretched-exponential NV magnetization recovery curves corroborate the proposed electronic phase segregation in charge-ordered and charge-averaged phases at the microscale. The presented study demonstrates the viability of using nanodiamonds as a platform for local magnetic probing of strongly correlated matter, including phenomena such as electronic phase separation.

items.title: Noise-Induced Thermalization in Quantum Systems
items.summary: In the current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum era, noise is widely regarded as the primary obstacle to achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, certain stages of the quantum computing pipeline can, in fact, benefit from this noise. In this work, we exploit the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis to show that noise generically accelerates a fundamental task in quantum computing -- the preparation of Gibbs states. We demonstrate this behavior using classical and quantum simulations with Haar-random and phase-flip noise, respectively, on a spin-1/2 chain with a local Hamiltonian. Our non-integrable model sees ~3.5x faster thermalization in the presence of noise, while our integrable model, which would not otherwise thermalize, reaches a thermal state due to noise. Since certifying a local Gibbs state is relatively easy on a quantum computer, our approach provides a new practical solution to a key problem in quantum computing. More broadly, these results establish a new paradigm in which noise can be harnessed on quantum computers, enabling practical advantages before the years of fault-tolerance.

items.title: A Breakdown Case Study of the Lindblad Approach via Entanglement and Purity
items.summary: The Lindblad master equation is widely used to describe the reduced dynamics of open quantum systems under Markovian assumptions. Here, we investigate its ability to reproduce the reduced evolution emerging from a microscopic many-body model in which two interacting two-level subsystems are embedded in a larger environment and evolve under fully unitary dynamics. The exact evolution exhibits a clear separation of timescales. At short times, decoherence arises from environmentally induced dephasing, leading to a Gaussian suppression of coherences and a quadratic decay of purity. At intermediate times, collective decoherence channels saturate and a slower, still Gaussian, decay driven by relative environmental fluctuations dominates. At later times the system settles in a complete decohered state. The first two behaviors cannot be reproduced by a Lindblad dynamics with constant coefficients, which always results in an exponential decay: Our work provides a simple example of the breakdown of the effective description relevant in many realistic settings.

items.title: Giant enhancement of attosecond tunnel ionization competes with disorder-driven decoherence in amorphized silicon
items.summary: High-harmonic generation (HHG) and tunnel ionization in solids are strong-field phenomena sensitive to the attosecond dynamics of laser-driven electron-hole pairs. While HHG has been used extensively as a spectroscopic probe in crystalline systems, its potential as a probe of disorder on the length scale of electron-hole trajectories remains relatively unexplored. Furthermore, with the advent of petahertz electronics, there is a growing need for controlling ionization on the nanoscale. Here, we show how focused-ion beam driven amorphization of silicon leads to a giant enhancement ($>$250 times) of yield for lower-order harmonics and quenching of higher-order harmonics, consistent with a dramatically enhanced tunnel ionization yield and disorder-induced decoherence, respectively. Modelling the real-space quantum dynamics, we show how electron-hole coherence in the amorphous phase is lost over a characteristic length of approximately five lattice sites. HHG spectroscopy also reveals remnant order inherited from the original cubic structure. Our results establish HHG spectroscopy as a probe of medium-range order and pave the way for new opportunities in lightwave nanoelectronics.

items.title: Harmonic origin of local symmetry breaking in PbTe revealed using machine-learned potentials
items.summary: We use machine-learned interatomic potentials combined with higher-order interatomic force constant models to show that finite-range polar correlations in PbTe are driven by long-range harmonic interactions rather than lattice anharmonicity. Our molecular dynamics simulations reveal a spatial polar correlation range exceeding 50 Å at low temperatures and decreasing with increasing temperature. Selective interatomic force constant mapping demonstrates that crystal anharmonicity usually associated with the formation of polar nanoregions suppresses polar correlations. Instead, long-range harmonic interactions extending to 13 Å are necessary to reproduce the spatial coherence of local dipoles. In reciprocal space, these extended harmonic interactions correspond to high curvature of the transverse optical (TO) phonon branch at the $Γ$ point. Comparison with isostructural NaCl connects these extended interactions to local underscreening of predominantly Coulombic forces. Our results provide a key microscopic description of finite-range polar correlations and a framework for understanding local symmetry breaking in centrosymmetric materials.

items.title: Gappy Reconstruction of Bubbly Flows by Guided Diffusion Models
items.summary: Experiments in multiphase flows are often limited in their ability to simultaneously obtain velocity measurements in different phases. At the same time, flow reconstruction from phase-limited measurements is a challenging problem due to the substantially different velocity statistics across the phases. We address this problem for buoyancy-driven bubbly flows in the pseudo-turbulence regime by using a guided diffusion model. We train the model using two-dimensional slices of the velocity field extracted from fully resolved three-dimensional direct numerical simulations. The model generates physically realistic velocity fields both unconditionally and when conditioned on the surrounding liquid flow. The reconstructed bubble-phase velocity field accurately reproduces key statistical features of the flow. We further show that a simple stacking procedure for adjacent two-dimensional slices enables a reasonable reconstruction of the three-dimensional flow inside a bubble. These results establish the potential of diffusion models to serve as generative priors for three-dimensional turbulent multiphase flows, opening a route toward the reconstruction of unobserved or experimentally inaccessible velocity fields from sparse, partial, or phase-limited measurements.

items.title: Large-scale Monte Carlo/Molecular Dynamics simulations with Atomic Cluster Expansion potentials in LAMMPS
items.summary: Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics (MCMD) simulations are widely used to study the properties of materials at the mesoscale. Simulations with hundreds of thousands of atoms usually rely on empirical potentials because MCMD with machine-learning interatomic potentials is impractical at this scale in existing implementations. Here, we introduce a hybrid MPI/OpenMP scheme for MCMD with Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) potentials in LAMMPS. Monte Carlo moves are evaluated from local energy changes and carried out in parallel over MPI ranks, while molecular dynamics is parallelized over OpenMP threads. At a fixed number of CPUs, the wall time of the Monte Carlo moves decreases by a factor equal to the number of MPI ranks. Larger simulation cells also reduce the statistical errors of free energy calculations because thermal fluctuations decrease with system size. We demonstrate the scheme by calculating free energies of the HCP and BCC phases in the strongly anharmonic Hf--Ti system and by simulating zirconium segregation in a nanocrystalline copper sample of 670,000 atoms. For Cu--Zr, an ACE potential and an empirical potential predict similar grain boundary compositions but different amounts of zirconium dissolved in the grains. The scheme makes MCMD simulations with machine-learning interatomic potentials practical at the length scales of microstructure.

items.title: Motility-Induced Phase Separation of Run-and-Tumble Particles under Local Stochastic Resetting
items.summary: We investigate the non-equilibrium stationary states of a one-dimensional active gas composed of run-and-tumble particles (RTPs) undergoing motility-induced phase separation (MIPS) and subjected to local stochastic resetting at the origin. Unlike global resetting, local resetting maintains a mass-injection flux at the origin while preserving large-scale spatial self-organization. We demonstrate that above a critical resetting rate $r_c$, the active system undergoes a transition toward a stationary two-phase state featuring a dense liquid droplet centered at the origin coexisting with a surrounding gas phase. Using kinetic evolution equations, we derive the exact steady-state density profile expressed in terms of the Lambert function. The size of the droplet has a non-monotonic dependence on the resetting rate $r$, and attains its maximum. Furthermore, we analyze the dynamical stability of the supersaturated gas phase and show that a nucleated droplet relaxes exponentially toward its steady-state size with a relaxation timescale of $1/r$. We extend our framework to model a finite resetting velocity, proving that the stationary droplet size is invariant with respect to the resetting velocity.

items.title: Orbital-dependent electronic correlations and single-band character in layered palladates
items.summary: Layered palladates provide a $4d$ platform for examining electronic correlations in materials with cuprate-like structural and orbital characteristics. Using fully charge-self-consistent density functional theory plus dynamical mean-field theory, we investigate the orbital- and layer-resolved electronic structures of LaPdO$_2$, RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$, La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$, and La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$. Under the conditions studied, all compounds remain metallic, with low-energy states dominated by the Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital. This orbital exhibits stronger mass renormalization than the Pd-$d_{z^2}$ orbital. LaPdO$_2$ and BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ show moderate correlations, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ is more weakly correlated. Both the trilayer La$_4$Pd$_3$O$_8$ and quadlayer La$_5$Pd$_4$O$_{10}$ remain weakly correlated, with similar Pd-$d_{x^2-y^2}$ mass enhancements and little difference between inner- and outer-layer Pd sites. Among the structures studied, BaLaPdO$_2$Cl$_2$ is closest to a cuprate-like single-band description, whereas RbSr$_2$PdO$_3$ retains an additional electron pocket with Pd-$d_{z^2}$ character. These results establish a comparative picture of weak to moderate, orbital-dependent electronic correlations in layered palladates.

items.title: Skin-like Prototissues Integrating Pro-Angiogenic Signaling with Antibacterial Barrier Function
authors: Zefeng Wang, Qiyi Li, Xiaohong Zhou, Yan Zhou, Yanwen Zhang, Tianhong Chen, Dinggeng He, Kemin Wang, and Jianbo Liu
items.summary: Abstract The bottom-up assembly of prototissues from synthetic protocells provides a promising route for bridging artificial cell engineering with tissue-level functionality; however, integrating biochemical signaling with adaptive barrier properties within such systems remains challenging. Here, we construct skin-like prototissues by embedding catalytically active coacervate vesicle protocells within a gelatin–hydroxypropyltrimethylammonium chloride chitosan hydrogel. Within this architecture, spatially organized protocells act as confined microreactors that convert endogenous glucose into nitric oxide (NO), establishing a self-sustained pro-angiogenic NO signaling cascade. Concurrently, evaporation-driven surface reorganization generates an epidermis-like hydrophobic interface with antibacterial barrier function. The integration of protocell-mediated NO signaling with matrix-driven antibacterial barrier function yields emergent skin-like functionality. Leveraging this integrated design, the prototissues are configured as bioactive patches that markedly accelerate healing of bacterially infected diabetic wounds by promoting neovascularization while suppressing bacterial colonization. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for translating prototissue architectures into functional therapeutic interfaces.

items.title: Three New Phases in the Two-Dimensional Potts Model at Complex Temperature
items.summary: The complex-temperature phase structure of the two-dimensional Potts model has remained largely unresolved despite decades of study. Here we determine the complex-temperature phase diagram of the 3-state Potts model, and uncover three gapless phases beyond the familiar ferromagnetic and paramagnetic phases. This is done by combining tensor-network free energies with the Poisson equation to compute the Fisher zero density in the thermodynamic limit. The resulting zero distribution unifies and revises long-standing conjectures on the zero loci, and outlines each phase. One is a non-conformal gapless phase, with an exponentially growing number of low-lying transfer-matrix levels distributed across all momentum sectors. The other two are Luttinger-liquid phases with complex-valued Luttinger parameters related by the Kramers-Wannier duality. At the antiferromagnetic critical point, the Luttinger parameter equals 3, while its limit from the adjacent Luttinger-liquid phase is 6. These findings reveal rich phase structures and unconventional critical behavior in a classical textbook model.

items.title: Out-of-training properties in frozen interatomic potential embeddings are decodable and ordered by physical scale
items.summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are trained on energies, forces and stresses, yet their frozen representations can predict other materials properties. We probe ORB-v3 and UMA-S across layers, read-outs and equivariant channels for nine properties of 154,875 Materials Project crystals. Both models outperform composition-only descriptors on all targets, including five outside their training objectives; errors in physical units help assess potential screening applications. Optimal depth varies by property, consistent with a physical-scale ordering. Random-weight controls reveal strongly property-dependent benefits of pretraining. UMA-S's rotation-invariant angular channels improve crystal-system classification, while higher scores from its full tensor disappear under rotation; matched-model controls do not isolate equivariance as the explanation. Accuracy varies across different probes, but nearest-neighbour prediction often approaches XGBoost performance, even though materials do not form distinct clusters according to their properties. We also test whether a linear predictor trained on one model's embeddings can predict properties using the other model's embeddings after a learned linear transformation. Predictive accuracy is largely preserved, despite differences in which atoms the two models place close together. These results guide the reuse of frozen MLIP representations for materials prediction.

items.title: Reversal of dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven multimode optomechanical resonators
items.summary: Dynamical backaction describes how a driven cavity field responds with delay to mechanical motion, and can be used to cool that motion toward its quantum ground state or amplify it into self-oscillation. Control over this interaction underpins laser cooling, high-fidelity state preparation, quantum transduction, and phonon lasing. In conventional cavity optomechanics, both the sign and the magnitude of the optical damping are dictated by the laser detuning, and cooling is bounded by quantum backaction (QBA), the optomechanical analogue of the Doppler limit in cold atoms. We show, in theory and experiment, that dynamical backaction can be strongly enhanced in multimode optomechanical resonators driven by time-varying (Floquet) optical fields. A modulated drive couples a sideband-unresolved MHz mode to a sideband-resolved GHz mode through the shared cavity, replacing the QBA limit of the target mode by the occupancy of the auxiliary mode. Experimentally, we cool the MHz mode to $47 \pm 13$ phonons, about half its single-mode QBA limit and an order of magnitude below what single-tone backaction reaches at the same intracavity photon number. The character of the interaction can moreover be completely inverted at fixed laser detuning, turning cooling into amplification and vice versa, controlled solely by the modulation frequency. Floquet driving thus extends open-loop quantum control, which requires no measurement or feedback, to mechanical resonators outside the resolved-sideband regime.

items.title: Monte Carlo Sampling for Wave Functions Requiring (Anti)Symmetrization
items.summary: Many strongly correlated states, such as those arising in the fractional quantum Hall effect and spin liquids, are described by wave functions obtained by dividing particles into multiple clusters, constructing a readily evaluable wave function in each cluster, and (anti)symmetrizing across these clusters. We introduce a method to compute quantities such as energies and correlators, using Monte Carlo simulations for these states. Our framework overcomes the factorial scaling of explicit (anti)symmetrization, allowing for studies of systems beyond the reach of exact diagonalization.

items.title: Electronic structure, phase stability, and transport properties of the AlTiVCr lightweight high-entropy alloy: A computational study
items.summary: We investigate the thermodynamics and phase stability of the AlTiVCr lightweight high-entropy alloy using a combination of ab initio electronic structure calculations, a concentration wave analysis, and atomistic Monte Carlo simulations. In alignment both with experimental data and with results obtained using other computational approaches, we predict a $\textrm{B2}$ (CsCl) chemical ordering emerging in this alloy at comparatively high temperatures, which is driven by Al and Ti moving to separate sublattices, while V and Cr express weaker site preferences. The impact of this $\textrm{B2}$ chemical ordering on the electronic transport properties of the alloy is investigated within a Kubo--Greenwood linear response framework and it is found that, counter-intuitively, the alloy's residual resistivity increases as the material transitions from the $\textrm{A2}$ (disordered bcc) phase to our predicted $\textrm{B2}$ (partially) ordered structure. Our results give fresh insight into the atomic-scale structure and consequent physical properties of this well-studied, technologically relevant material.

items.title: Nonlocality relates cuprate photoemission $ω/T$ scaling to a broad dielectric loss peak
items.summary: Photoemission spectroscopy on high $T_c$ cuprates reveals a puzzling nodal self-energy with $ω/T$ scaling and an exponent varying continuously with doping. Meanwhile, electron energy loss spectroscopy finds a broad $\sim 1$eV peak whose physical origin remains debated. We propose they share a common origin by introducing a phenomenological model of nonlocal screening in a many-body charged fluid. The model's key feature is spatially nonlocal effective repulsions between carriers $V_α(r) \sim 1/r^α$, with doping-dependent $α$. The model predicts a falsifiable relationship between independently measured self-energy exponent $γ$ and loss function peak dispersion exponent $α$, as $γ= 2-\frac{1}α$. This can be tested using modern ARPES and EELS. Nonlocality provides an alternative route to $ω/T$ scaling in observables, although it is conventionally regarded as a signature of quantum criticality.

items.title: Experimental Evidence of Elastic Instability in Viscoelastic Kolmogorov Flow
items.summary: Inertialess elastic instabilities can profoundly affect transport in complex-fluid flows, from mixing in microfluidic devices and displacement through porous media to polymer processing. While such instabilities are well understood in flows with curved streamlines, their origin in rectilinear flows like the prototypical Kolmogorov flow remains unresolved. Here, we report the first experimental evidence of the center-mode elastic instability, at vanishing inertia, in a confined quasi-two-dimensional viscoelastic Kolmogorov flow, driven by electromagnetic forcing. The instability is characterized by the emergence of "arrow-shaped" structures in the velocity field, which fluctuates chaotically as the forcing strength increases. We reproduce these observations in simulations of the Oldroyd-B model and trace the dynamics in the confined flow to the travelling arrowhead structures that emerge from the center-mode instability of unbounded Kolmogorov flow. Our work establishes a generic route to purely elastic instability in rectilinear flows, broadening the conditions under which elastic turbulence and enhanced mixing can arise.

items.title: The $N$-channel white-noise Schrödinger operator in all three Dyson classes. I. Explicit stationary admittance distribution, density of states and outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals
items.summary: We obtain an explicit stationary distribution of the matrix Riccati variable---the boundary admittance---for an $N$-channel Schrödinger operator with Gaussian white-noise disorder, in all three Dyson symmetry classes $β=1,2,4$. Uniform absorption regularizes the Riccati dynamics, and the distribution's normalization factorizes into outgoing Kontsevich matrix Airy integrals. This gives a common route to the density of states and the sum of Lyapunov exponents, extending Halperin's scalar solution to coupled channels. Exact finite-$N$ formulas connect two spectral regimes: the Lifshitz tail, including its symmetry-dependent prefactor, and the collective large-$N$ edge. We reduce the $β=4$ and even-$N$ $β=1$ problems to unitary orthogonal polynomials and an auxiliary recursion. Their critical double-scaling limit yields edge profiles on the $N^{-4/5}$ energy scale, governed by a complex Painlevé-I tritronquée solution and a linear auxiliary equation. We conjecture that these profiles describe a universal edge regime of random band matrices.

items.title: Large pseudo-orbital magnetic moment of magnons in CrI$_3$ nanotubes
items.summary: Recently discovered CrI$_3$ nanotubes are expected to host unusual radial magnetic order states, on account of the strong out-of-plane magnetic anisotropy of the two-dimensional parent material. The detection of these peculiar magnetic states is challenging, and motivates the quest for unique features that can be probed experimentally. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show that an axial magnetic field tilts the radial phase into a conical one that threads the tube with an Aharonov-Bohm flux for magnons. This flux endows magnons with a pseudo-orbital magnetic moment, reaching approximately six Bohr magnetons, three times conventional magnon spin moment, and therefore detectable through magnon spectroscopy, providing a smoking gun for the radial and conical magnetic order in CrI$_3$ nanotubes.

items.title: Reconfigurable Dysprosium Isotope Mixtures with Selectable Quantum Statistics
items.summary: Dipolar quantum mixtures offer new opportunities to explore many-body phenomena shaped by long-range anisotropic interactions, intercomponent coupling, and quantum statistics. Here we develop a reconfigurable platform for bosonic and fermionic dysprosium isotope mixtures using a single-isotope-like optical layout. We time-multiplex the 421-nm light to generate isotope-selective slow-atom fluxes, while spectrally engineered 626-nm light provides simultaneous common-path narrow-line cooling and trapping. By reconfiguring optical frequencies, we prepare seven isotope pairs spanning Bose--Bose, Bose--Fermi, and Fermi--Fermi combinations, with continuous population-balance control through the 421-nm dwell-time allocation. Systematic comparisons with sequence-matched single-isotope references, from magneto-optical-trap loading and compression to optical-dipole-trap transfer, reveal nearly single-isotope-like performance for most combinations. The larger deviations occur only for certain isotope pairs and preparation stages, with controlled measurements revealing optical sensitivities during loading and additional losses under high-density conditions. Our results make isotope composition and quantum statistics selectable within a strongly dipolar system while largely preserving single-isotope preparation simplicity and performance, opening new possibilities for exploring multicomponent dipolar quantum matter.

items.title: Bias Conditioning and Long-Range Electrostatics for Consistent Machine-Learning Potentials of Electrified Interfaces
items.summary: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) of electrified interfaces need the bias as input, but it is unclear whether a scalar electrode charge suffices and whether short-range models capture the non-local response. We add charge and field conditioning to short- and long-range MLIPs. State-of-the-art field-conditioned short-range models overpolarize thick water films nearly twofold and miss work-function shifts at stepped Pt. Our long-range model captures both, needs only the electrode charge at metals as input, and reproduces ab initio simulations of the Pt(111)--water interface.

items.title: Hund physics in the quarter-filled two-band Hubbard-Kanamori model: Crystal-field splitting and non-local Correlations
items.summary: We address the effect of crystal-field splitting and non-local correlations in the quarter-filled two-orbital Hubbard-Kanamori model. The role of the Hund's coupling in this configuration is not obvious since the atomic ground state has only one electron per site. Yet, previous works identified fingerprints of the Hund's coupling defining a weak Hund's metal at least at finite temperature. Using single-site dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) and two-site cellular DMFT based on a selected configuration-interaction solver we investigate the zero-temperature properties of the weak Hund's metal. Within DMFT we draw the boundary for the weak Hund's metal, which is consistent with previous finite-temperature results. Interestingly, we find that the fingerprints of the Hund's coupling are quite robust to the lifting of the orbital degeneracy and they survive up to splittings of a quarter of the bandwidth, well beyond those at which a two-stage Kondo screening disappears. Including non-local correlations in cluster DMFT demonstrates the robustness of the single-site DMFT picture, even if Mott localization occurs at smaller interactions. In the metal the intersite correlations are weak and insensitive to $J$, while in the localized state we find nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic, antiferro-orbital correlations that are manifest also in the mutual information between sites.

items.title: A tunable multi-gated platform for superlattice engineering in bilayer graphene
items.summary: Periodic potentials with length scales much larger than crystal lattice constants can generate low-energy electronic minibands. While small-angle twisted van der Waals heterostructures have been widely used to realize such physics, correlated phases are often limited by twist-angle inhomogeneity, strain, and disorder. Here, we investigate high-quality Bernal bilayer graphene placed on a patterned graphite gate, featuring a triangular array of holes, forming a new class of "gate-engineered" superlattices tunable through three independent electrostatic gates. Near the charge neutrality point, we observe insulating states characteristic of miniband formation. Temperature-dependent transport reveals activated gaps consistent with theory, and Hall measurements indicate charge-carrier inversion. Notably, the superlattice can be reconfigured electrostatically using various gate combinations, enabling flexible band-structure design without mechanical twisting. The results highlight a new route to band engineering, potentially extendable to complex periodic structures that are untenable in natural materials.

items.title: Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift
items.summary: We study a class of discrete-time random walks in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose conditional drift decays polynomially in time and grows polynomially with the distance from the origin to the current position. This class is related to several models of self-interacting random processes.
