This unified machine-learning workflow eliminates computationally expensive multi-physics runtime bottlenecks for real-time laser processing control and inverse photonic thin-film design.

items.title: Feedback-induced mechanical bistability and perpendicular-domain formation in active elastic tissues
items.summary: Contractile fibers in muscle tissues are highly aligned over the scale of many cells. Muscle layers surrounding organs with an inner lumen are often arranged in orthogonal directions. Here, we study a minimal mechanism of how structural order and its patterning into orthogonally aligned domains can emerge from mechanical feedback alone. The central idea is that contractile fibers align in the direction of the local active and elastic stresses, a feedback motivated by the maturation of muscle fibers under tension. We thus model muscle tissue as an active nematic solid with stress feedback: an elastic medium with embedded contractile fibers that are reinforced along the directions of the local tissue stresses. We find that the feedback from the contractile fiber stress is self-amplifying and drives spontaneous fiber alignment. Feedback from the elastic stress couples the alignment to the mechanical boundary conditions and tissue geometry. Depending on the mechanical boundary conditions, the elastic-stress feedback stabilizes two orthogonally aligned tissue states, resulting in a structurally and mechanically bistable tissue that shows a hysteretic stress-strain response. In spatially extended tissues, this bistability gives rise to orthogonally aligned domains separated by domain walls. Our results show that stress feedback can pattern structural order by coupling spontaneous alignment to the tissue geometry. Our mechanism thus provides a purely mechanical route to orthogonal fiber patterning in muscle tissues.

items.title: Self-doped correlated adatom lattices on cubic boron nitride
items.summary: We survey triangular adatom lattices on the (111) surfaces of cubic boron nitride (cBN) for strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems. Using density functional theory combined with the constrained random phase approximation and charge self-consistent dynamical mean-field theory, we identify twelve promising candidates. Group-III (group-V) adatoms on the N- (B-)termination realize clean one-band Hubbard systems, while group-III and transition-metal (V, Cr, Mn) adatoms on the B-termination realize two-band Hubbard systems. Importantly, the polar III-V character of cBN induces self-doping by $\pm 1/4$ electron away from integer filling. With strong Hubbard (and Hund's) interactions and small hoppings, most systems are doped Mott insulators. Heavy quasielectrons with mass renormalizations up to 4 and strong local moments up to 2.5 $μ_B$ put our systems into a regime where unconventional superconductivity on the triangular lattice has been predicted.

items.title: Oxygens breathe, electrons jump
items.summary: Electronic transport in polyanionic battery cathodes proceeds through small-polaron hopping between transition-metal sites and is commonly assumed to be tightly coupled to the motion of charge-compensating mobile ions. Using olivine Li$_x$MnPO$_4$ as a prototypical platform, we use first-principles molecular dynamics with extended Hubbard functionals to follow, in real time and at finite temperature, the adiabatic evolution of Mn oxidation states and atomic sublattices. We find that polaron hopping and cation migration are dynamically decoupled: Mn$^{2+}$/Mn$^{3+}$ valence exchanges occur frequently while the intercalated ions remain confined to their sites, and hopping is gated by the local oxygen framework. Freezing the six oxygen atoms of an individual MnO$_6$ octahedron excludes that site from the hopping network, while increasing the fictitious oxygen mass slows down electronic transport. Each valence exchange coincides with a concerted breathing of the donor and acceptor octahedra ($ΔV \simeq 2$ $Å^3$), with their volume asymmetry crossing zero at the transition, consistent with the Holstein-Marcus coincidence condition. The hopping rate yields an activation energy of $E_a = 0.20 \pm 0.03$ eV, closely matching the elastic energy scale of the two coordination cages ($λ_V/4 \approx 0.20$ eV). These results identify the oxygen coordination cage, not the mobile cation sublattice, as the dynamical gate for small-polaron transport: a site can accept the electron only if its cage can breathe, and the barrier is governed by cage elasticity. Selective constraints and mass scaling applied to first-principles dynamics provide a general route to link electronic and lattice degrees of freedom in redox-active materials, opening the door to framework engineering in intercalation and mixed ionic-electronic conductors.

items.title: CTMRG as a tensor-network message-passing algorithm
items.summary: We formulate the corner transfer matrix equations, and the corner transfer matrix renormalization group built on them, as a set of local equations on general planar graphs. These equations depend only on the local subgraphs of the planar graph and are glued together consistently to describe the whole graph. Solving them yields message tensors and corner matrices, which can be used to construct an MPS environment for any connected subgraph. We test the proposed equations on the ferromagnetic Ising model, on a variety of infinite lattices (including hyperbolic ones) and on finite graphs, and find systematic improvement over belief propagation.

items.title: Logarithmic thermodynamic cost of prediction from rare observations
items.summary: A memory predicting changes in its environment from rare observations must spend energy on sampling and recording. We consider autonomous chemical memories driven by a sample-and-hold sensor observing an environment that switches at rate gamma, with sampling frequency f<<gamma. An ideal observer with access to the full observation history can retain predictive information proportional to f. However, retaining a finite fraction of this information in an autonomous physical memory requires work of order kBT ln(gamma/f) per sensor change. This additional thermodynamic cost arises from the competing requirements of suppressing false records during long intervals between observations and responding rapidly to new observations. We establish a universal low-power bound on predictive information, which grows at most as P/ln(P_ref/P) with power budget P, uniformly over any finite number of memory states and independently of network topology and memory relaxation times. We further demonstrate that memory architecture determines the attainable scaling. With bounded transition rates and readout from the memory alone, two-state memories are limited to P^2 scaling, whereas a three-state memory is sufficient to attain the optimal logarithmic scaling. Our results establish a fundamental thermodynamic distinction between acquiring information and maintaining a useful record of a changing environment.

items.title: Machine Learning the $GW$ Self-Energy Operator for Real Materials
items.summary: Machine learning of $GW$ in solids has largely focused on prediction of scalar quasiparticle energy corrections. Here, we introduce a phase-aware many-body transformer that predicts the full $\mathbf{k}$-resolved complex self-energy matrix. As a proof of principle, we apply the model to predict quasiparticle energies before and after diagonalization of the quasiparticle Hamiltonian, obtaining a test set mean absolute error (MAE) of 29 meV for a dataset of 1745 2D materials in the static COHSEX approximation and 60 meV for a more limited dataset of 433 materials calculated within a plasmon-pole model. COHSEX pretraining followed by finetuning reduces this MAE to 42 meV. The predicted matrices also accurately reproduce QP wavefunctions.

items.title: Optical spin Edelstein response of d-wave altermagnets
items.summary: The momentum-dependent spin splitting and compensated magnetic order in altermagnets offer opportunities for electrical control of spin polarization. We explore the spin Edelstein effect in the frequency domain of a two-dimensional d-wave altermagnet with Rashba spin-orbit coupling. We calculate the spin-velocity susceptibility response function beyond the intraband response regime and find that the interband longitudinal and transverse Edelstein responses are governed by the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature, respectively. The density of states presents a logarithmic van Hove singularity at exactly the negative value of the energy below which four disconnected Fermi contours emerge. This defines three distinctive regions for the position of the Fermi level, through which the Edelstein susceptibility tensor displays characteristic spectral features, reflecting the topological change of the Fermi surface. The resulting spin magnetization shows a strong dependence on the driving frequency and on the orientation of the in-plane external electric field. Our results highlight new possibilities for electrical and optical control of the spin Edelstein effect in altermagnets that could find spintronic applications.

items.title: Spontaneous mechanical patterning in active elastic tissues with stress feedback
items.summary: The active mechanics of biological tissues is often governed by embedded active contractile fibers responding to mechanical feedback. We introduce a minimal model of a solid-like tissue where the mechanics is controlled by feedback of local active and elastic stresses on fiber organization. The resulting tissue generically exhibits a bistable response to external strain and spontaneously segregates into domains of orthogonally aligned fibers. Our theory thus provides a minimal mechanical feedback mechanism generating orthogonal structural alignment ubiquitous in biological tissues.

items.title: Decoding SO(5) Deconfined Multicriticality: Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy-Sphere Spectroscopy
items.summary: The nature of the deconfined quantum critical point (DQCP) remains unsettled: competing explanations invoke a real multicritical conformal field theory (CFT) or pseudocriticality governed by nearby complex fixed points. We use the conformal bootstrap and fuzzy-sphere regularization to compute $SO(5)$ CFT data and compare our results with large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) data to investigate these scenarios. Using mixed correlators of the lowest vector $φ$, singlet $s$, and traceless symmetric scalar $t$, we characterize the bootstrap cone whose tip lies remarkably close to the position indicated by large-scale QMC. We extract an extensive spectrum across $SO(5)$ irreducible representations, together with operator product expansion (OPE) coefficients. We study a fuzzy-sphere realization of the $SO(5)$ nonlinear sigma model with a level-1 Wess--Zumino--Witten term. Using the special conformal generators, we identify 52 conformal primaries in a system with \(N=10\) Landau orbitals, including 31 not previously classified as primaries in the earlier fuzzy-sphere study. Symmetry projection extends fuzzy-sphere exact diagonalization to $N=12$. The bootstrap spectrum and OPE coefficients show close agreement with fuzzy-sphere data, including 16 of the newly identified primaries in channels accessible to the mixed-correlator bootstrap. The lowest $SO(5)$ singlet scalar is relevant in the bootstrap and QMC results; its fuzzy-sphere data is $Δ_s=2.816$ at $N=12$ and decreases with system size. Our results suggest that the mixed-correlator bootstrap solution represents a unitary CFT with a relevant $SO(5)$ singlet scalar and is closely connected to the QMC and fuzzy-sphere data for the DQCP. The conformal bootstrap, fuzzy-sphere, and QMC together provide comprehensive evidence for an $SO(5)$ multicritical CFT and critical data to decode the phases in two-dimensional quantum magnets.

items.title: A feedback-driven central limit theorem with $q$-Gaussian limits
items.summary: We establish a central limit theorem, the feedback-driven central limit theorem, for sums whose summands are independent noise variables multiplied by an amplitude that depends on the preceding normalized sum $y$. The summands are martingale differences whose conditional variance, $c+b\,y^{2}$, depends quadratically on $y$, with feedback strength $b$; unlike in the martingale central limit theorem, this conditional variance does not settle to a constant. The noise has finite variance; for positive feedback we assume, as in Lyapunov's theorem, a finite third moment, and for negative feedback bounded noise, so that the conditional variance stays nonnegative. For positive feedback, the normalized sum converges to a Student law, equivalently a $q$-Gaussian with $1<q<2$, independently of the noise distribution. For negative feedback, it converges to a compactly supported density, which is a $q$-Gaussian with $q<1$ when $-\tfrac12<b<0$. The Gaussian law, $q=1$, is recovered at zero feedback, while the Cauchy law, $q=2$, is obtained only as a limiting case, in a triangular array in which the feedback grows slowly with the number of terms. Thus every $q<2$ is obtained for a fixed feedback strength, and $q=2$ as a limit. We further show that the balance identity behind the theorem singles out quadratic feedback: a $q$-Gaussian with $q<2$ satisfies it only for a quadratic conditional variance, and no $q$-Gaussian with $2\le q<3$ satisfies it for any conditional variance. The proofs use the method of moments for negative feedback and a Wasserstein coupling argument for positive feedback, including cases in which the limiting variance is infinite.

items.title: Interface-Selective Extreme Ultraviolet Second Harmonic Generation Away from Linear Absorption Edges
items.summary: Extreme ultraviolet (XUV) second harmonic generation (SHG) combines interface selectivity with core-level element specificity but has so far been limited to linear absorption edges. Here, we measure XUVSHG from an indium tin oxide capped MoO$_3$/SiO$_2$/Si photovoltaic heterojunction for fundamental energies of 60--76\,eV, below the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge. Where linear absorption is a featureless valence background, we observe a strong, structured XUVSHG response with maxima near 70 and 76\,eV. Layer-resolved first-principles calculations reproduce both maxima and assign them to the Si/SiO$_2$ interface, the 76\,eV peak to the bridging Si monolayer and the 70\,eV peak to the near-interface substrate. Bethe--Salpeter calculations for bulk Si connect the signal to Si 2$p$ excitons at 140--160\,eV. At the Si L$_{2,3}$-edge, the calculated response is instead governed by MoO$_3$-induced asymmetry at the oxide interface. These findings establish off-edge XUV SHG as a powerful approach for selectively probing distinct buried interfaces within complex material heterostructures.

items.title: Exact Scaling Theory of Social Tipping Phenomena in Finite Populations
items.summary: Granovetter's threshold model provides a classical framework for social mobilization, in which collective action spreads through self-reinforcing cascades as individuals join once the movement size reaches their personal threshold. Here, we investigate social tipping points by treating the initial fraction of instigators, $ρ_0$, as a control parameter in a finite population of $N$ agents with activation thresholds drawn from a Beta distribution with shape parameters $α$ and $β$. We characterize the thermodynamic phase diagram, which exhibits both continuous and discontinuous cascade transitions, and develop an exact combinatorial formulation for finite populations. The discontinuous transitions are hybrid, combining a jump in the final active fraction with a square-root critical singularity associated with an interior saddle-node bifurcation. Using the empirical cumulative distribution of quenched thresholds, we develop an asymptotic finite-size scaling theory that identifies the stochastic mechanisms responsible for rounding these transitions. For power-law thresholds ($α>1$, $β=1$), the critical window and the mean inactive fraction at criticality both scale as $N^{-1/3}$. For hybrid transitions governed by an interior saddle-node, the critical window scales as $N^{-1/2}$, while the conditional displacement of stalled cascades from the marginal state scales as $N^{-1/4}$. We further derive an explicit Gaussian scaling function for the probability of complete activation and show that convergence to this limiting function is exceptionally slow, with corrections of order $N^{-1/6}$. These results establish the extensively seeded Granovetter model as a tractable framework for investigating finite-population fluctuations and hybrid criticality in irreversible threshold-driven cascades.

items.title: Calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains from local conserved charges and currents
items.summary: We develop a simple algebraic method for calculating correlation functions in integrable spin chains. We introduce current minors, antisymmetrized products of local conserved charge densities and their currents, and prove that their expectation values are determinants of density and current mean values. Decomposing local operators into current minors, we derive factorized formulas for correlation functions in terms of current mean values, valid in any nondegenerate eigenstate. Applying the method to the spin-$1/2$ XXZ chain and, more generally, to every representation of the Temperley--Lieb algebra, we prove previously conjectured factorized formulas for short-distance correlation functions.

items.title: Stabilization of LaH$_{10}$ with Thorium: Superconductivity in (La,Th)H$_{10}$ up to 232 K near 1 Mbar
items.summary: Ternary lanthanum-based hydrides are among the best high-temperature superconductors. Here we show that substituting La with thorium stabilizes La(Th)H$_{10}$ clathrate structure at $\sim$1 Mbar while only minimally suppressing superconductivity. The resulting cubic (La,Th)H$_{10}$ phase, synthesized from relatively air-stable La$_2$Th, La$_3$Th and La$_5$Th alloys, reaches an onset $\textit{T$_c$}$ = 232 K at 134 GPa, as confirmed by contact resistance measurements. Superconductivity was verified by two independent methods: electrical resistance and contactless radio-frequency measurements under applied magnetic fields at various pressures. Using a record-high pulsed current of 380 mA, we investigated critical phenomena in P6$_3$/mmc-(La,Th)H$_9$ at 173 GPa, which allowed for the experimental determination of a single superconducting gap within the s-wave model: $Δ(0) = 37 \pm 4.5$ meV and $2Δ(0)/kT_c = 4.9 \pm 0.6$. The La-Th-H system is chemically rich: in addition to the decahydride and nonahydride mentioned above, we also identified nanocrystalline I4/mmm-(La,Th)H$_4$ (5-6 nm grain size), (La,Th)H$_6$, as well as $hP13$, $cF80$ and $A15$ phases with compositions of (La,Th)H$_{5.75-6.25}$ and $\textit{T$_c$}$ $\approx$ 83 K at 70-80 GPa, and a possible (La,Th)H$_{16}$ polyhydride.

items.title: Mixed-state topological transitions with hidden long-range correlations
items.summary: We study a decoherence-driven transition from a one-dimensional symmetry-protected topological state to a trivial product state. The decoherence acts onsite while preserving the protecting symmetry on average. Although conventional local correlations remain short-ranged across the transition, we uncover hidden nondecaying long-range correlations in a symmetry-twisted ensemble that weights states according to their symmetry charge. At the transition, the twisted correlation length diverges and the twisted partition function becomes singular. These signatures can be directly extracted from symmetry-resolved measurement outcomes, making the hidden critical behavior accessible on current quantum platforms at mesoscopic system sizes. We demonstrate this through numerical simulations of the measurement process.

items.title: Flexo-Strain Engineering of Phonons and Ferrons in Thin Films of Van der Waals Ferrielectrics
items.summary: The influence of the flexoelectric coupling on the fluctuations of electric polarization and elastic strains can lead to the principal changes of the dispersion law of soft optical and acoustic phonons and ferrons in a bulk van der Waals ferrielectric. Since the size, gradient and strain effects determine phase diagrams and polarization behavior in thin films, it is reasonable to assume that the flexocoupling and mismatch strains should have a strong influence on the dispersion of phonons and ferrons in thin ferroelectric films. Using the Landau-Ginzburg-Devonshire approach, in this work we reveal that the dispersion of soft optical and acoustic phonons and ferrons is strongly dependent on the sign and magnitude of elastic strains, which originate from the lattice constants mismatch in thin strained films of van der Waals ferrielectric CuInP2S6. In particular, the frequency of acoustic phonons and ferrons approaches zero at nonzero wavevectors k>k_cr, where the critical value of the wavevector k_cr is determined by the mismatch strain, flexoelectric coupling strength and temperature. Zeroing of the acoustic phonon frequency, that appears with increase of tensile strains, indicates a dynamic instability induced by the flexo-strain effects, that may evolve into a spatially modulated incommensurate polar phase with increase in the flexocoupling strength. Analytical results, derived in this work, open the way for flexo-strain engineering of soft phonon and ferron dispersion in thin films of van der Waals ferrielectrics.

items.title: The $\mathbb{Z}_N^{\times 3}$ symmetry protected boundary modes in two-dimensional Potts paramagnets
items.summary: We construct and analyze a class of one-dimensional boundary Hamiltonians arising from two-dimensional symmetry-protected topological phases with $\mathbb{Z}_N^{\times 3}$ symmetry on a triangular lattice. Using a cohomology-based transformation, the lattice models for the edge modes are explicitly obtained, and their structure is shown to be governed by the arithmetic properties of $N$. For prime $N$, the boundary theory admits a formulation in terms of mutually commuting Temperley-Lieb algebras. For the composite values of $N$, the models exhibit hierarchical or factorized structures. We demonstrate that the phases can be understood in terms of primary models augmented by local defect degrees of freedom that partition the system into independent segments. Finally, the global symmetry is realized on the boundary in a non-on-site and anomalous manner, directly realizing the corresponding 't Hooft anomaly.

items.title: Higher-dimensional homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic materials
items.summary: Quasiperiodic geometrical arrangements, which exhibit long-range order in the absence of periodicity, have attracted interest in the design of composites and mechanical metamaterials. In this context, direct numerical simulations explicitly resolving the quasiperiodic microstructure become prohibitively expensive for macroscopic problems, motivating the development of homogenized continuum models. However, the absence of a periodic unit cell in physical space hinders the use of conventional homogenization methods. In the present work, we exploit higher-dimensional periodic representations to perform computational homogenization of quasiperiodic elastic composites. Thereby, effective properties are obtained from unit-cell problems solved using the fast Fourier transform in higher-dimensional spaces. Using two-dimensional Penrose tilings and three-dimensional Ammann--Kramer--Neri tilings as paradigmatic examples, we describe the distribution of heterogeneous material properties in the corresponding higher-dimensional unit cells, compute effective elasticity tensors, and assess convergence of fully resolved finite patches to the homogenized limits. We provide open-source implementations of all numerical models.

items.title: Robust Antiferromagnetic Ordering above 500 K in a Family of Bilayer van der Waals Materials
items.summary: Stabilizing magnetic order above room temperature in layered materials is highly desirable for low-dimensional spintronics applications. However, realizing room-temperature antiferromagnetism in layered magnets remains challenging. Here, we present a layered semiconducting oxyhalide material family, Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$ ($X$ = F, Cl, Br), which exhibits robust high-temperature antiferromagnetic ordering. The two-dimensional nature and scalability of this system are demonstrated by atomically resolving the van der Waals gap of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Br$_2$ and synthesizing centimeter-scale single crystals of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$Cl$_2$. Temperature-dependent neutron scattering and magnetization measurements determine their G-type magnetic structure and transition temperature. Remarkably, the Néel temperature of Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$F$_2$ ($\sim$580 K) is the highest among all reported layered antiferromagnets. Density functional theory calculations demonstrate that strong nearest-neighbor superexchange interactions along both out-of-plane and in-plane directions, particularly the magnetic couplings along lattice $c$ direction within the bilayer motif, are primarily responsible for the high Néel temperatures in Sr$_3$Fe$_2$O$_5$X$_2$. In contrast, inter-bilayer spin couplings are negligibly weak, without much influence on the stabilization of the antiferromagnetic order. Therefore, theoretical calculations predict that this robust antiferromagnetic order could persist or even strengthens at room-temperature even at the monolayer limit. Our results highlight iron-based layered oxyhalides as a promising platform for exploring beyond-room-temperature antiferromagnetism in the two-dimensional limit, holding immense potential in areas like information storage and spin-based devices.

items.title: Surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides
items.summary: Magnetically intercalated transition metal dichalcogenides are layered materials with highly tunable magnetic orders and unconventional transport properties. Here we report a surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy in $\mathrm{M}_{1/3}\mathrm{T}\mathrm{X}_{2}$, in which the surface and bulk favor distinct magnetic orders. In $\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) results are reproduced by an A-type antiferromagnetic electronic structure, while neutron scattering and bulk DFT+$U$ calculations identify stripe order as the bulk ground state. DFT+$U$ slab calculations resolve this contradiction by showing that relaxation of an Fe-terminated surface reverses the magnetic preference from stripe to A-type order. The same dichotomy recovers the $K$-centered Fermi-surface pockets that are observed in $\mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{Co}_{1/3}\mathrm{Ta}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ but absent from previous bulk calculations. Notably, the surface-stabilized magnetic phase of $\mathrm{Fe}_{1/3}\mathrm{Nb}\mathrm{S}_{2}$ carries nonrelativistic spin splitting and can exhibit altermagnetic character. These results caution against the general association of ARPES signals with bulk magnetic states in these systems, and suggest surface-bulk magnetic dichotomy as a promising route to realize magnetic phases, including altermagnetism, that are not energetically favored in the bulk.

items.title: Matching two-dimensional statistics does not certify three-dimensional transport in battery electrodes
items.summary: Three-dimensional battery electrode structures reconstructed from two-dimensional micrographs are routinely used to predict transport, assuming that matching the measured 2D statistics reproduces the relevant 3D properties. We test this premise on X-ray tomograms of three all-solid-state cathodes. With a differentiable conductivity solver, we optimise voxel structures that match the real electrode in phase fractions, boundary density, two- and three-point correlations and lineal-path functions, on all section planes, slab by slab and layer by layer, within measurement noise. Every sample has statistical twins conducting 10-88-fold less than the real electrode, robust to 5^3 majority filtering, whereas the most conductive are at most 3.3-fold above it. The twins rearrange rather than remove material, severing or funnelling through-plane paths. A classifier on 2D sections detects them, as it does current 2D-to-3D generators: the information is in the images but not in the statistics. Matching standard 2D statistics therefore does not certify 3D transport.

items.title: Multi-symmetry projected coupled cluster theory with triples corrections
items.summary: Symmetry projection and coupled cluster theory provide complementary descriptions of static and dynamic correlation. We introduce two approximate perturbative triples corrections to spin- and point-group-projected coupled cluster with single and double excitations (PCCSD). The coherent $(T)$ correction combines triples intermediates over the projection grid, whereas $+(T)$ evaluates the conventional triples expression using PCCSD amplitudes. Both recover conventional $(T)$ in the absence of projection. We assess these corrections for N$_2$ and C$_2$ dissociation, $3d$ transition-metal monoxides, and Cr$_2$. Projection improves the singles-and-doubles description and distinguishes selected low-lying symmetry sectors. For the six-monoxide benchmark subset, coherent $(T)$ reduces the PCCSD mean absolute error from $13.4$ to $3.0~\mEh$, achieving accuracy comparable to conventional CCSD(T). Both triples corrections restore the short-bond minimum missing from the PCCSD curves of Cr$_2$, with coherent $(T)$ giving a well depth closer to extrapolated DMRG. In contrast, $+(T)$ provides more balanced N$_2$ and C$_2$ dissociation curves. These results demonstrate the benefits of perturbative triples in PCC, while their system-dependent performance highlights the need for a more systematic treatment.

items.title: Two channels of magnetic renormalization in the terahertz lattice response of FePS$_{3}$
items.summary: Interlayer vibrations probe how magnetic van der Waals layers are stacked and coupled. In the zigzag antiferromagnet FePS$_3$, ultrafast experiments show that the interlayer shear couples strongly to the magnetic order, but not how magnetism renormalizes the shear stiffness and damping. Here, using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, we measure the anisotropic conductivity of FePS$_3$ from 1.6 to 300 K and in fields up to 7 T normal to the layers. We observe absorption bands at 0.6-0.8 and 1.3-2.4 THz that persist into the paramagnetic phase. The lower one is consistent with an interlayer shear resonance; the magnetic order stiffens one of its in-plane components and softens the other, reversing their splitting at the Néel temperature. We identify two channels of magnetic renormalization: frequency shifts are confined to the ordered phase, whereas the linewidths of this resonance and most oscillator strengths follow short-range spin correlations persisting well above the transition. The field acts mainly on the higher resonance in one orientation: near 3.2 T, its softening accelerates and its linewidth has a cusp-like minimum, consistent with critical slowing down of a field-induced order parameter. These results give an equilibrium view of spin-shear coupling, which is anisotropic and persists above the Néel temperature through short-range correlations.

items.title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
items.summary: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying Lüscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.

items.title: Quantitative Theory for the Amplitude of Fluorescence Quantum Beats from Geminate Triplet-Pair Fusion
items.summary: We derive the amplitude of fluorescence quantum beats caused by geminate triplet-exciton fusion from the full set of parameters that characterize singlet fission and triplet exciton dynamics. We apply the theory to tetracene and rubrene single crystals. We find that the amplitude depends on the fission time in tetracene, but does not do so in rubrene, where it is determined by the dimensionality of triplet transport. Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the experimental data in both materials, for a fission time of the order of 200 ps and isotropic triplet transport in tetracene, and for a triplet hopping time along the herringbone axis of 200-300 ps and anisotropic transport in rubrene.

items.title: Ferroelectric Polarization Dynamics of HZO FeCAPs at a Verified Subnanosecond Time Scale
authors: Mor M. Dahan, Emanuel Ber, Florian Wunderwald, Guy Orlev, Edan Gefen, Ilya V. Karpov, Thomas Mikolajick, Sou-Chi Chang, Uwe Schroeder, and Eilam Yalon
items.summary: Abstract Ferroelectric random-access memory (FeRAM) based on the ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) offers a promising solution for next-generation embedded memory. In this Letter, we demonstrate subnanosecond ferroelectric polarization dynamics in HZO FeCAPs using an RF-compatible structure. By simultaneously measuring the electrode voltage and transient current under subnanosecond pulsing, we directly observe polarization dynamics with a temporal resolution below 100 ps. Our results demonstrate subnanosecond switching under directly monitored TE pulses with voltage amplitudes of 5 V in 8 nm-thick HZO capacitors with an area of 16 μm 2 . We also map switching kinetics for sub-10 ns pulse widths using this methodology. We further correlate polarization obtained from the dynamic current transient with the results from the postpulse readout scheme. Motivated by dynamic random-access-memory (DRAM) latency targets, these results establish a device-level benchmark for delivered subnanosecond switching in HZO FeCAPs and, together with a simplified nucleation-limited switching (NLS) analysis, define an effective ultrafast switching window for FeCAP evaluation.

items.title: Stochastic Thermodynamics of Associative Memory
items.summary: Dense Associative Memory networks (DenseAMs) unify several popular paradigms in Artificial Intelligence (AI), such as Hopfield Networks, transformers, and diffusion models, while casting their computational properties into the language of dynamical systems and energy landscapes. This formulation provides a natural setting for studying thermodynamics and computation in neural systems, because DenseAMs are simultaneously simple enough to admit analytic treatment and rich enough to implement nontrivial computational function. Aspects of these networks have been studied at equilibrium and at zero temperature, but the thermodynamic costs associated with their operation out of equilibrium are largely unexplored. Here, we define the thermodynamic entropy production associated with the operation of such networks, and study polynomial DenseAMs at intermediate memory load. At large system sizes and intermediate and low load, we use dynamical mean field theory to characterize out-of-equilibrium properties, work requirements, and memory transition times when driving the system with corrupted memories. We characterize a failure mode of higher order networks not observed at zero temperature. Further, we develop a method for calculating work and power costs in the mean field limit. Finally, we find tradeoffs between entropy production, memory retrieval accuracy, and operation speed.

items.title: U-HamGNN: a universal model for magnetic Hamiltonians conditioned on spin and Hubbard U
items.summary: The electronic structure of a magnetic crystal depends jointly on its spin configuration and the on-site Hubbard correction U, requiring a separate DFT+U calculation for each combination. We introduce U-HamGNN, an equivariant network that takes these two inputs directly and predicts spin-resolved Hamiltonians across diverse crystal chemistries. A spectral-hybrid optimizer that weights each update direction by how consistently the gradient points along it reaches 8% lower Hamiltonian error than Muon and 26% lower than AdamW in a ten-epoch benchmark. The predicted bands reproduce U-dependent gap opening and altermagnetic spin splitting within the trained window and beyond it; exchange couplings and magnetic-order calls derived from the Hamiltonian agree with DFT+U on a calibration set. This universal model provides a new tool for magnetic research.

items.title: The microscopic origin of the hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes bundles
items.summary: In a recent study we reported large hysteretic hydrogen adsorption in samples made out of Double Wall Carbon Nanotubes (DWCNT) at supercritical temperatures (50 K, 77 K and 150 K), a physical behavior of practical interest. Here, we center our efforts in elucidate its physical origin by means of neutron diffraction (ND) and computer simulations. After a detailed theoretical modeling of the ND signal we were able to quantitatively study how the nanostructure of the material reacts to the hydrogen loads. An expansion of the bundle structure with increasing hydrogen load was found. Taking advantage of the translational symmetry of a DWCNT bundle along the nanotube axis, a two dimensional numerical analogue of the system helped us to clarify the microscopic origin of the hysteresis. Two microscopic mechanisms are identified as responsible for the metastable hydrogen adsorption, one structurally static in character, namely, H$_{2}$-load dependent effective energy barriers between interstitials, the other related to the structural deformation, namely, the opening/closing of the channels between interstitials with increasing/decreasing H$_{2}$ loads owing to the concomitant bundle expansion/contraction.

items.title: Distinguishing thyroid nodule malignancy using digital palpation
items.summary: Accurate pre-operative diagnosis of thyroid nodules remains a major clinical challenge. Current diagnostic techniques rely on fine-needle aspiration and demonstrate high rates of inconclusive results, often leading to avoidable thyroidectomies with lifelong implications. Here, we introduce a mechanics-based diagnostic method that leverages Digital Palpation to determine malignancy and identify tissue subtypes in human thyroid nodules. From a cohort of patients undergoing thyroidectomies, we evaluated ex vivo thyroid specimens and processed the resulting mechanical data from 36 tests in 10 thyroid nodules. Principal Component Analysis reveals that these experimental results are distributed within a three-dimensional space of interpretable scalar features reflecting tissue grittiness, strength, and toughness, which map closely to descriptions of malignant and benign nodules given by clinicians. Our results further demonstrate that malignant nodules exhibit distinct mechanical signatures compared to their benign counterparts. This revealed a statistically significant difference (p = 9 x 10^-4) and separability (95% lower-bound Hedges' g = 1.08) between benign and malignant nodules along a direction in principal component space representing effective stiffness. Preliminary clustering patterns were also observed among malignant subtypes, including follicular, oncocytic, and papillary thyroid carcinomas. Together, these results highlight the potential of Digital Palpation as a novel mechanics-based method for tissue characterization and motivate its further development toward diagnostic applications.

items.title: Polarization waves in open-barrier quantum-dot cellular automata
items.summary: Quantum-dot cellular automata (QCA) are almost always operated as bistable digital logic. We develop a closed-form theory of small-signal polarization waves in the open-barrier regime, where tunnelling within each cell is comparable to or stronger than the electrostatic kink coupling between cells, so that a line of cells responds linearly instead of latching. Linearizing the coherence-vector equations of the intercellular Hartree approximation (ICHA) about the unpolarized state gives a lattice dispersion with a low-frequency cutoff, an evanescent band below it and a Klein-Gordon long-wavelength limit, and relaxation toward the instantaneous equilibrium damps the waves at a rate that depends on the wavenumber. The exact Jordan-Wigner solution and exact diagonalization confirm the mode as a sharp quasiparticle, with ICHA frequencies within 6% of the exact ones once the tunnelling energy is at least twice the kink energy, and show that the exact chain also carries waves over a range of couplings where the ICHA predicts latching. A leading low-temperature estimate of thermal dephasing sets a ceiling on the operating temperature of about 13.6 K per terahertz of gap for a carrier that keeps its phase over 30 periods. At junctions the waves scatter through a lattice scattering matrix that reaches the familiar transmission-line value only at mid-band.

items.title: Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the MoS$_2$/Sapphire System
items.summary: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the MoS$_2$/ $α$-Al$_2$O$_3$(0001) system. The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from ~1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On 2,820 held-out test structures from the DFT pool, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/angstrom. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5 %, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of point defects (Spearman $ρ$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($ρ$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($ρ$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %.

items.title: Symmetry-protected isolation of the quantum metric in chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals
items.summary: Quantum geometry, comprising the Berry curvature (BC) and the quantum metric (QM), underpins a wide array of topological and transport phenomena. However, in most solid-state platforms, BC and QM signals are inherently entangled, making their experimental separation highly challenging. Here, we demonstrate that the chiral limit of type-II semi-Dirac semimetals provides a symmetry-protected mechanism to cleanly isolate the QM. At the chiral limit where the spin-orbit gap $m_z=0$, chiral and $\mathcal{PT}$ symmetries strictly suppress the BC, its dipole (BCD), and the shift current, leaving the QM and its dipole (QMD) as the sole sources of the optical and nonlinear Hall responses. This pure-QM regime exhibits distinct experimental fingerprints, including a divergent longitudinal optical conductivity and a QMD-induced nonlinear Hall conductivity that exhibits a pronounced singularity as the chemical potential approaches the nodal point. Turning on a finite $m_z$ reactivates the BC channels, transitioning the system from a pure-QM phase into a mixed geometric phase. By deriving a scaling law for the nonlinear Hall conductivity, we establish a direct experimental strategy to separate the mixed Drude, BCD, and QMD contributions based on their distinct relaxation-time dependencies. Our findings identify chiral type-II semi-Dirac semimetals as highly tunable platforms for isolating and probing intrinsic quantum geometric effects.

items.title: Self-assembly of dipolar nanoclusters on an attractive substrate: A coarse-grained simulation approach
items.summary: Recently, Thomas et al. [Nanoscale 17, 18291 (2025)] showed that bismuth oxido nanoclusters (BiO-NCs) of the type [Bi$_{38}$ O$_{45}$ (Boc-L-Phe-O)$_{24}$] form chains when deposited onto gold or pyrolitic graphite substrates. This chain formation is significantly enhanced when the bismuth in the BiO-NCs is partially replaced by cerium through doping. In this work, we study a simplified, coarse-grained model of this process, namely (magnetic) Stockmayer particles in the presence of an attractive substrate. The model is investigated by means of molecular dynamics simulations. The deposition experiment is mimicked by a rapid quench from high temperature to a low temperature below the bulk coexistence curve. The results are found to be qualitatively similar to the experimental observations reported earlier. In our simulations, we find significant chain formation in the bulk even at rather low concentrations, which is in contrast to the BiO-NCs in ethanol for which dynamic light scattering reveals negligible aggregation in the absence of the substrate. This lends support to a scenario, conjectured in the work of Thomas at al., where the dipole moments are induced by the particle-substrate interaction and hence there is little dipole moment in the bulk. In a second part, we study the system in equilibrium. We consider the scaling of chains, the number of layers populated as a function of two-dimensional density, and we draw analogies to polymers on interfaces, which have been extensively studied over the past decades. Most notably, it is found that the chains behave as self-avoiding walks at low densities, which gives way to rod-like scaling at higher densities.

items.title: Kinematic Foundations of Defect-Mediated Plasticity: A Gauge-Theoretic Framework
items.summary: Plastic deformation is widely regarded as an intrinsically dissipative phenomenon whose theoretical description relies heavily on phenomenological constitutive assumptions. We argue instead that defect-mediated plasticity possesses a universal, non-dissipative backbone: the kinematics and mobility constraints of defects are fixed by symmetry and conservation laws prior to dissipation. Starting from the spontaneous breaking of spacetime symmetries in a crystalline phase, we construct an effective field theory in which elasticity reorganizes into a coupled higher-rank tensor-vector gauge structure emerging directly from stress and defect conservation laws rather than being postulated microscopically. Dislocations, disclinations, and singular frame-geometric configurations appear as gauge sources whose coupled continuity equations and mobility constraints follow from generalized Gauss laws. The construction provides a symmetry-based organization of the kinematic sectors relevant to defect-mediated plasticity and a starting point for a subsequent dissipative theory of defect motion and stress relaxation.

items.title: Angular dependence of the low-temperature skyrmion state in Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$
items.summary: In the cubic chiral magnet Cu$_2$OSeO$_3$, a low-temperature skyrmion state (LTS) and a metastable tilted conical state emerge for magnetic field along $\langle 100\rangle$, both stabilized by magnetocrystalline anisotropies. We report how these states evolve when the magnetic field is rotated from $\langle 100\rangle$ via $\langle 111\rangle$ to $\langle 110\rangle$. Measurements of the magnetization and the AC susceptibility are combined with broadband microwave spectroscopy on the same cuboid sample at 5\,K. In the microwave spectra, the characteristic gigahertz excitations, notably the counterclockwise gyration mode of the skyrmions, provide a direct indicator of the character of the magnetic states and a qualitative measure of their volume fractions. Both techniques consistently show that signatures of the LTS decrease in strength under rotation and are observed only for field directions within ${\sim}20^{\circ}$ of $\langle 100\rangle$. In this range, the field values at which the skyrmions unwind remain essentially unchanged. In contrast, signatures of the tilted conical state persist up to ${\sim}40^{\circ}$, beyond which the conventional sequence of helical, conical, and field-polarized states is recovered. Thus, the tilted conical state, while being a prerequisite for the nucleation of the LTS under field sweeps, is not sufficient for its formation.

items.title: Giant Raman Optical Activity in Chiral and Polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$
items.summary: Raman optical activity (ROA) measures the difference in Raman scattering intensity for right- and left-circularly polarized light and reflects the chirality of excitations. In solids, ROA is commonly very weak. For the phonons of chiral and polar Ni$_3$TeO$_6$, we find a giant ROA with magnitude 100 times higher than commonly reported for molecules. The systematic analysis based on phonon selection rules allows the chiral and achiral scattering channels to be separated. First-principles calculations of the Raman tensor at finite phonon momentum relate the effect to the phonon modulation of the band-geometric and band-dispersion contributions to optical gyrotropy. This establishes Raman optical activity as a probe of electron--phonon modulation of the band geometry in an insulator.

items.title: Interaction-driven Weyl superfluids from topologically trivial bands in an optical Raman lattice
items.summary: We propose an interaction-driven route to Weyl superfluidity from topologically trivial noninteracting bands in a three-dimensional optical Raman lattice. The scheme builds on a pairing mechanism arising from the interplay between a large Zeeman splitting and an attractive Hubbard interaction. The large Zeeman splitting renders the noninteracting bands topologically trivial and suppresses spin-flip hopping. These otherwise off-resonant spin-flip processes are resonantly restored when the attractive Hubbard interaction compensates the energy mismatch, generating occupation-dependent spin-orbit coupling that coherently couples neighboring spin-down fermion pairs to onsite doublons. Combining this density-dependent in-plane spin-orbit coupling with density-dependent spin-conserving interlayer tunneling extends the pairing mechanism to three dimensions. A self-consistent mean-field treatment of the microscopic model yields Weyl superfluids with two, four, or eight nodes, together with fully gapped weak topological superfluids. We further propose an experimental implementation with ultracold ${}^{40}\mathrm{K}$ atoms. Our results provide a route to Weyl superfluidity enabled by interaction-assisted spin-orbit coupling, without requiring nontrivial single-particle band topology.

items.title: On the richness of metamaterials generated by recursive cell division
items.summary: Scale-rich metamaterials are one member of a family of recursive cell divisions, which differ in which cell is cut, where the cut passes and at what angle. We characterise six members of this family through three network mappings, the cell tree, the dual graph of ligaments and junctions, and the frame graph of spans, and through their elastic-wave properties: the effective refractive index n, its isotropy and the band over which it holds. The dual-graph degree law, the mean degree and the age law of the ligaments hit by new ones are the same for every rule, so they cannot distinguish the materials. The cell tree and the cell shapes do differ, and one consequence of them explains the physics: the tail of long spans in the frame graph. With the longest spans as the length scale, the bending part of the inverse squared index follows a single power law across rules, densities and numbers of ligaments, and the same spans set the lowest local resonance and the band edge. The stretching part, which caps the index, is carried by the straight frame lines of the tiling rather than by the division. Random cut angles produce elongated cells and long spans, hence high index and a narrow band; cuts perpendicular to the long axis of the cell keep the cells compact, giving low index and a wide band. Cutting through the centroid instead of a random point bounds the split fraction between 4/9 and 5/9, which removes the area hierarchy without changing the index. The cut angle interpolates continuously between these limits, and the isotropy peaks where the ligament orientations become isotropic while the cells are still compact. In three dimensions the plate and strut divisions are stretching dominated and the index stays low for every rule.

items.title: Experimental methods to measure thermal hysteresis of martensite-austenite transition in bulk \b{eta}-Cu-Zn-Al composition gradient single crystals
items.summary: Improvement of functional and structural fatigue endurance for applications of ferroelastic materials requires an optimization of their composition. We propose an experimental methodology to explore the model \b{eta}-Cu-Zn-Al system. It is based on an original route to process bulk gradient composition single crystals to investigate fine variation of composition range coupled with local measurements of the austenite-martensite microstructure by light microscopy during the transformation. The latter method is compared with differential scanning calorimetry measurements. The methodology is applied to different narrow ranges (up to 4 at%) of composition of standard CuZnAl shape memory alloys where local fluctuations of hysteresis of 3 K are observed.

items.title: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
items.summary: At strong on-site repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto configurations without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments, for few fermions in the square-lattice Hubbard model and, where the arguments allow, on any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on any $N\geq2$-site graph, $μ_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$, for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $μ_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count, as four hops permute particles by at most a transposition or 3-cycle; for uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$ the slope is $α(N,n)=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$, fixed by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles. (3) At large finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient, an exact trace checked by exact diagonalization, is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Under a Peierls flux, the exchange slope $α(N,2,Φ)=-\frac{64}{N-1}\cosΦ_\square$ ($L\times L$ tori, $L=3$ or $L\geq5$) carries the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, while the doublon (bound-pair) hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $π$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows numerically, up to $O((2λ)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the permutation bound, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moment structure and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.

items.title: Emergent kagome-like electronic texture in epitaxial $β$-Sb on Al(111)
items.summary: We report the epitaxial growth of $β$-Sb on Al(111) and the emergence of a kagome-like electronic texture with increasing Sb coverage. The surface evolves from disordered clusters through honeycomb and dice patterns before kagome-like regions appear. Diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, spectroscopy, and density functional calculations identify the ordered phase as $β$-Sb formed by AB stacking of two dice layers, with the honeycomb phase serving as a precursor. The kagome-like maxima occupy bridge positions within the same lateral lattice and differ in apparent height from dice regions by only about 25 pm. Together with the absence of an additional chemical component or distinct band manifold in photoemission, these observations support an electronic origin of the kagome-like contrast. Comparison of local tunneling spectra with calculated orbital projections suggests an energy selective change in the relative spectral contributions of Sb p states. Interface separation tests reveal sensitivity to Al-Sb coupling, while vacuum local density of states calculations identify states with enhanced bridge density. These results suggest that local interface changes could alter the balance between atomic and bridge contributions to tunneling within $β$-Sb. For a reference $β$-Sb model retaining the epitaxial geometry after Al removal, spin-orbit coupling modifies local band dispersions while the structure remains metallic. The model exhibits a finite intrinsic spin Hall response that varies with chemical potential.

items.title: Orbital antiferromagnetic currents in a frustrated fermionic ladder
items.summary: We consider a spinless $t$-$t'$ ionic Hubbard chain at 1/2 filling and large hopping ratio $t'/t$. In this limit the model adequately maps onto a weakly coupled triangular ladder with a potential interchain bias. The low-energy properties of the system are formed due to the interplay of geometrical frustration, correlations and charge imbalance. We derive the effective field-theoretical model to study universal properties of the model in the scaling limit. We show that at full dynamical frustration the ground state of the ladder represents a repulsive version of the Luther-Emery liquid with dominant orbital antiferromagnetic correlations exhibiting the slowest power-law decay in the ground state. Pairing correlations also display algebraic order but are subdominant. At an incomplete dynamical frustration a finite commensurability gap is dynamically generated, and the fluctuating OAF transforms to a long-range ordered state with a spontaneously broken time reversal symmetry. The mass gap in the spectrum of relative density fluctuations gets suppressed upon increasing the potential bias.

items.title: Basic introduction to Freidlin-Wentzell theory
items.summary: Freidlin-Wentzell theory provides the quantitative foundation for rare, noise-induced transitions in stochastic dynamical systems, predicting optimal transition pathways, the exponential scaling of mean escape times, and the long-term occupancy of competing attractors in metastable systems. Here we present a pedagogical, physics-oriented review built around a unified Hamiltonian framework: starting from the infinitesimal generator of a continuous-time Markov process, we derive the local Hamiltonian, obtain the Lagrangian and action functional via Legendre-Fenchel duality, and construct the quasi-potential landscape. We apply this streamlined formalism across weak-noise diffusions, Markov jump processes, weakly interacting particle ensembles, and nonequilibrium stochastic fields, alongside exact conditions for macroscopic coarse-graining. Along the way, we highlight how broken detailed balance drives forward and reverse transition paths apart, explain where local linear stability and Gaussian approximations break down, and assemble multi-attractor landscapes using combinatorial $W$-graphs. Finally, we bridge the analytical theory to modern numerical solvers, including ordered upwind methods, geometric minimum action algorithms, and neural-network parameterizations, and provide an accompanying GPU-accelerated Python package.

items.title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
items.summary: AgBiS2 has rapidly risen in efficiency as single-junction photovoltaics (PVs), but its potential for tandem PVs is unexplored. Herein, we perform optical modeling based on the experimental absorption spectrum of AgBiS2, revealing that, as the NIR sub-cell, efficiencies exceeding 47.5% are achievable in triple-junction tandems, superseding tandems using Pb/Sn perovskite NIR cells (44.2%). However, fulfilling this potential requires overcoming the limited transport properties of AgBiS2 nanocrystal films, which constrains film thicknesses to only 30-50 nm, severely restricting NIR response. A solution-phase ligand exchange process is herein developed, allowing one-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals that maintain efficient charge-carrier extraction despite an order of magnitude increase in film thickness. These films enable 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with visible-light-absorbing lead-halide perovskite sub-cells, and monolithic tandems successfully demonstrating voltage addition. AgBiS2 PVs have high stability, retaining >90% of the original efficiency after 3 months of storage in dry air without encapsulation. This work establishes the significant potential of AgBiS2 as a stable and scalable NIR absorber for tandem PVs.

items.title: The large $|U|$ expansion for a half-filled asymmetric Hubbard model on a triangular ladder in the presence of spin-dependent magnetic flux
items.summary: We consider a half-filled system of spin-1/2 fermions on a triangular ladder with spin-dependent hopping in the presence of spin-dependent flux. Using the Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, we derive an effective spin Hamiltonian describing the infrared properties of the system in the limit of strong on-site repulsion. The expansion is performed up to the third order in the hopping amplitude over on-site interaction energy. It is shown that the low-energy spin excitations are described by an anisotropic $XXZ$ Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and an unconventional three-spin (correlated exchange) term in the presence of an extended magnetic field. The latter couples not only to $z$-projection of the total spin on a triangular plaquette but also to the product of $z$-components of three spins located on vertices of the triangle. In the case of strong attractive interaction, the corresponding effective model is derived from the repulsive one using the one-spin-component particle-hole transformation. The effective Hamiltonian is given by the same $XXZ$ Heisenberg model, as in the repulsive case, but in terms of pseudospin (charge) operators.

items.title: Chirality-polarized superradiance induced by quantized orbital-angular-momentum transfer in a ring cavity
items.summary: We investigate a spin-$1/2$ Bose-Einstein condensate coupled to two counterpropagating modes of an optical ring cavity and driven by Laguerre-Gaussian Raman beams carrying quantized orbital angular momentum (OAM). We demonstrate that competition between OAM-selective Raman scattering channels controls collective superradiance through self-consistent atom--cavity feedback, linking atomic orbital motion to cavity-chirality selection. For unequal OAM transfer, one cavity mode dominates the superradiant response, with its chirality switchable by the Raman pump strengths. In contrast, equal OAM transfer allows both counterpropagating modes to coexist. The resulting chirality-polarized phases support distinct vortex and vortex--antivortex configurations with reconstructed synthetic gauge-field textures. Remarkably, contact interactions can reshape the vortex topology without changing the dominant cavity chirality, revealing distinct responses of atomic and photonic degrees of freedom. The predicted mode switching and vortex ordering can be probed through cavity output and spin-resolved imaging in a proposed $^{87}$Rb implementation. Our results establish quantized OAM transfer as a mechanism for controlling collective cavity emission beyond conventional atomic SOAMC.

items.title: Harmonic Control of Dynamical Freezing in Programmable Rydberg Atom Arrays
items.summary: Periodic driving enables the engineering of complex quantum matter, yet in interacting systems it generically leads to energy absorption, which limits the lifetime of the engineered states. To address this challenge, dynamical freezing has been proposed as a mechanism for stabilizing non-equilibrium states over parametrically long timescales. While theory predicts robust freezing under simplifying assumptions, realistic platforms inevitably include additional interaction processes that alter its stability. Here, we report the experimental observation of dynamical freezing in programmable Rydberg atom arrays of up to 100 atoms in one and two dimensions. We find that while single-frequency driving produces pronounced suppression of excitation dynamics, the freezing behavior is restricted to a narrow parameter regime due to interaction-induced heating channels present in realistic simulators. Using a perturbative Floquet analysis of the fully interacting atomic system, we identify the dominant microscopic heating processes responsible for this destabilization. Leveraging this understanding, we design a dual-parameter modulation of detuning and Rabi frequency that coherently suppresses these absorption pathways and substantially broadens the freezing regime, making it also robust across different geometries. Our results reveal how heating processes shape the stability of dynamical freezing in interacting Floquet systems and demonstrates a route to control driven many-body dynamics in realistic experimental platforms.

items.title: Metallic or insulating magnetic phases of transition-metal oxides in light of the Slater vs Mott controversy
items.summary: Magnetic d-electron oxides usually have a long-range-ordered ground state and an above-ground-state disordered para phase. The historical Slater-Mott controversy still reverberating to date pertains to understanding the origin of the insulating vs metallic nature of these two phases. Slater suggested that the insulating character evolved from the long-range order (LRO) antiferromagnetic (AFM) cell-doubling, leading to energy band repulsion and thus to forming a band gap. The reliance on LRO to explain gapping suggests that the absence of LRO in the spin-disordered para-phase would deprive the system from band repulsion, thus predicting a metallic paramagnetic (PM) phase. This, however, conflicts with numerous current observations. The alternative Mott-Peierls-Hubbard view abandons the mean-field-like band structure view emphasizing instead the local interelectronic repulsion U as a strong correlation signature of gapping both at the presence or absence of LRO. However, U is not an easily measured or calculated quantity in periodic systems, a situation often leading in practice to treating U as an adjustable parameter. The current work uses a parameter-free mean-field-like approach (Density Functional Theory, DFT), allowing energy-lowering symmetry breaking. This is done by considering local magnetic motifs as building blocks of the macroscopic AFM or PM phases. It is found that even when such motifs are isolated electronically from each other (i.e. vanishing LRO) by embedding them in quantum barriers (such as magnetic NiO6 octahedra surrounded locally by wide-gap MgO) they exhibit an intrinsic band gap. Thus, the origin of the band gaps in AFM or PM phases need not be LRO or strong correlation and can be understood within the mean-field-like band structure approach with symmetry breaking.

items.title: Growing length scales while approaching the glass transition
items.summary: Even after decades of research, the nature of the glass transition is controversially debated: Kinetic freezing phenomena, purely local strain-mediated effects, or collective phenomena including a hidden phase transition are usually discussed. In this work, we check reports on clusters of correlated particles in supercooled liquids which grow upon approaching the glass-transition. We specifically focus on dielectric studies providing approximate access to the four-point correlation function, which allows insight into the evolution of so-called amorphous order. Existing temperature-dependent data derived from the three-point correlation function or higher-order dielectric susceptibilities are modeled using the random first-order transition theory combined with the Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann law. This ansatz enables detailed predictions concerning normalized correlation lengths or the number of correlated particles as function of temperature and fragility. It provides a good fit to the experimental data for all materials investigated, including network and molecular glass formers and polymers. We conclude that length scales and corresponding particle numbers determined by the different methods used are at least similar and closely related to those considered by the theory. Moreover, the model predictions on the fragility dependence of the number of correlated molecules are at least approximately fulfilled. Existing criticism concerning an apparent lack of criticality in the temperature dependence of experimental correlation lengths is discussed in terms of this fragility dependence: All available data are well consistent with a hidden phase transition which is best revealed for the most fragile liquids.

items.title: Exciton-polarons in monolayer semiconductors with drifting electrons
items.summary: Recent work has demonstrated that the optical absorption of moderately doped two-dimensional semiconductors can be described in terms of exciton-polarons. In this picture, interactions between a photoexcited exciton and a Fermi sea of excess charge carriers split the exciton spectrum into a lower-energy attractive polaron branch and a higher-energy repulsive polaron branch. Due to the negligible in-plane momentum of photons, however, optical measurements probe only exciton-polarons near zero momentum, leaving their finite-momentum physics largely unexplored. Here we propose accessing this regime by measuring the absorption in the presence of an electric bias current. In effect, this displaces the electronic Fermi sea in momentum space, such that an optically active exciton-polaron at rest acquires finite momentum relative to the charge carriers. Using a diagrammatic formulation of the exciton-polaron problem, we derive exact relations between the spectral and quasiparticle properties of current-biased exciton-polarons and their finite-momentum counterparts in an equilibrium Fermi sea. These relations show that absorption measurements with drifting electrons can reconstruct the momentum dependence of the quasiparticle properties for both branches. We estimate that experimentally accessible currents can probe a broad momentum range while remaining within the linear-response regime.

items.title: An active Lorentz gas: walking droplets in periodic media
authors: Aleksi Majaniemi, Esko Toivonen, Rahil N Valani, Rainer Klages and Esa Räsänen
items.summary: The Lorentz gas is a paradigmatic model in dynamical systems theory for understanding the origin of nonequilibrium transport in terms of microscopic deterministic chaos. In the periodic setting, a point particle scatters elastically off disks arranged on a two-dimensional lattice. Here we replace the disks by smooth potentials and the particle by the widely studied walking droplet, which propels itself on a vertically vibrating fluid. In the low-memory limit, this droplet reduces to a particle with nonlinear active friction. We call this system an active Lorentz gas. Using extensive numerical simulations, we analyse how dissipation generated by the active deterministic dynamics alters the phase-space structure of the corresponding conservative Lorentz gas. We find that islands of stability collapse into attracting and repelling sets. To characterize these structures, we introduce an energy-variance filtering method that distinguishes localized periodic, quasi-ballistic periodic, and chaotic trajectories, enabling the construction of bifurcation diagrams in a non-conservative setting. We identify parameter regimes exhibiting strong bifurcation cascades, anomalous diffusion, and significant phase-space contraction. Our results establish the active Lorentz gas as a rich framework for studying transport in dissipative dynamical systems and provide a bridge between active matter and classical models of chaotic transport, with potential implications for hydrodynamic quantum analogs in periodic media.

items.title: Coupled propagation of acoustic topological states
authors: Ming-Zhu Li, Lei Shi, Zhe-Yu Ji, Zhaojiang Chen and Ya-Xi Shen
items.summary: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupled propagation of two pseudospin states in an acoustic topological heterostructure. Within the framework of coupled-mode theory, the heterostructure is mapped onto a two-waveguide model, in which the two pseudospin topological states serve as guiding modes. The propagation constants of the individual topological states and the coupling strength between them are quantitatively extracted from the projected band structures of supercells. When the two topological states are decoupled, acoustic energy remains confined to the excited topological interface. When the two topological states are coupled, acoustic energy undergoes Bloch oscillation between two topological interfaces. Notably, the energy-transfer coefficient of the Bloch oscillation can be tuned by introducing interface detuning. Owing to the frequency dispersion of the coupling strength, the heterostructure can function as a wavelength-selective demultiplexer. This work establishes a generalized coupled-mode framework for the quantitative analysis and flexible manipulation of topological-state coupling, offering new insights into the design of topologically protected acoustic devices with controllable multichannel functionalities.

items.title: Three-dimensional topological disclination in acoustic crystals
authors: Zhenxiao Zhu, Yan Meng, Minmiao Wang, Xiang Xi, Yuxin Zhong, Linyun Yang, Bei Yan, Jingming Chen, Ziyao Wang, Thomas Christensen, Caigui Jiang, Changqing Xu, Ce Shang, Zhen Gao
items.summary: Topological disclinations are rotational-symmetry-breaking lattice defects that can probe crystalline topology and offer a versatile platform for topological cavities, waveguides, and lasers. Here, Zhu et al. report a three-dimensional topological disclination that carries a fractional charge of 1/2 and hosts zero-dimensional topological bound states embedded in the bulk. The result extends disclination physics beyond layered or surface-based designs and opens new possibilities for controlling waves through the interplay of band topology and defect geometry in three dimensions.

items.title: Spin group symmetry criteria for unconventional magnetism
authors: Xun-Jiang Luo, Jin-Xin Hu, Mengli Hu, Kam Tuen Law
items.summary: Unconventional magnets combine the compensated magnetization of antiferromagnets with ferromagnet-like spin splitting, promising next-generation spintronics, yet a unified symmetry principle for their classification has been lacking. Luo et al. show that just six symmetry operations in the spin space group fully determine the dimensionality and parity of the spin splitting, yielding a complete classification that overturns established paradigms and uncovering numerous candidate materials for even- and odd-parity magnets.

items.title: Conformational dynamics of exopolysaccharides underlie biofilm matrix mechanics in Vibrio cholerae
authors: Kee-Myoung Nam, Nathan Fowler, Rajan Kandel, Yongqi Zhu, Yuchu Liu, Yi-Jhen Lai, Muhammad Faheem Hassan, Emma Gerace, Alexander J. Hinbest, Merrill Asp, Rich Olson, Ying Li, Mu-Ping Nieh, Mingjiang Zhong, Robert J. Woods, Alexis Moreau, Jing Yan
items.summary: Bacterial biofilms are encased within polymeric matrices that allow them to withstand large mechanical perturbations, but how this capability arises from individual matrix components is not well-understood. Combining experiments and simulations, Nam et al. characterize the physical properties of a key polysaccharide in the Vibrio cholerae biofilm matrix and show that it is a semiflexible polymer with unusual nanoscale conformational features that may contribute to its viscosity and, in turn, to biofilm mechanics.

Issue Editorial Masthead
Toward Unified and Accurate Description of Multidimensional Nuclear Observables via a Prior-Informed Large Language Model
authors: Shijie Guo, 世杰 郭, Shouyu Wang, 守宇 王, Enhong Wang, 恩宏 王, Zhongming Niu, 中明 牛, Yiming Ding and 一鸣 丁
items.summary: A prior-informed large language model (LLM)-driven multi-task learning framework is proposed for the unified and accurate description of multiple nuclear observables. By fine-tuning the pre-trained DeepSeek-R1-1.5B model with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), lightweight adapters are introduced while preserving general pre-trained parameters. Under a causal language modeling paradigm, the model is trained autoregressively on deviations between experimental and theoretical values. Significant accuracy improvements are achieved across seven observables, including charge radii, masses, binding energies, separation energies, and decay energies, with the training loss decreasing by over 98% across all tasks. This demonstrates that the LLM-based framework, through structured prior embedding, offers an efficient and shared approach for multi-task regression in fundamental nuclear properties.

items.title: On the Precise Boundary of the Néel Antiferromagnetic Phase in the Shastry-Sutherland Model
authors: Rongyi Lv, 融一 吕, Xiangjian Qian, 湘坚 钱, Mingpu Qin and 明普 秦
items.summary: The ground state phase diagram of the Shastry-Sutherland model remains controversial. In particular, the nature of the transition between the plaquette valence bond solid (PVBS) phase and the Néel antiferromagnetic (AFM) phase is still under debate. While some studies suggest a direct transition between the two phases, others propose the existence of a narrow intermediate quantum spin liquid regime. To address this issue, we perform large-scale Density Matrix Renormalization Group calculations to determine the Néel AFM phase boundary in the Shastry-Sutherland model. By applying staggered boundary pinning fields and directly measuring the bulk staggered magnetization, and through systematic extrapolations with respect to truncation error as well as careful finite-size scaling, we find that the staggered magnetization remains finite across the controversial region 0.78 ≲J1/J2 ≤ 0.81, which was suggested to host a quantum spin liquid phase in some studies. Together with the previously established consensus placing the PVBS phase boundary at J1/J2 ≈ 0.78, these results, within the resolution of the present calculations, provide evidence against the existence of an intermediate quantum spin liquid phase and support a direct PVBS–Néel AFM transition in the Shastry-Sutherland model.
